quiz_questions.q: [Page 1 · Beginner Orientation] Before pasting Page 1's one-liner (`Page 1: Master Roadmap  -  Rebuilding the 520 MH`), which terminal environment should you paste into, and what happens immediately after you press `Return`?
options: A) Paste it into Microsoft Word or a browser URL bar.

B) Paste it into your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`); `snap_step` executes the command, verifies the output against Page 1's expected result, and either unlocks the green Post-Lab Learning view or provides a 1-click Auto-Debug Fix command if an error occurs.
C) Paste it into a disconnected terminal window showing `Broken pipe` without reconnecting.
D) Reboot the laptop after every single command.
quiz_questions.hint: Check the environment badge on Page 1: is this step running locally on your MacBook Air or on the remote SFSU Linux EDA server (`mahmoodi`), and how does `snap_step` talk back to the website?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Shell commands must be pasted into an active UNIX terminal emulator (`Terminal.app` or `XQuartz xterm`), not a word processor or browser address bar.

Correct! Pasting into your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`) runs the command inside `snap_step`, which automatically checks the exit code and required markers and updates your live `:8788` web console!

Incorrect — A terminal showing `client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe` has lost its SSH connection; you must either use your clean local terminal window or run the Step 0 Auto-Connect command first.
Incorrect — You never need to reboot between pages; `snap_step` preserves your state continuously from Page 1 to Page 100.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Page 1 runs in your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`). Pressing `Return` triggers `snap_step`, which logs the output, captures the screenshot, and sends real-time verification telemetry to the website.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 1 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 1's combined one-liner, why do we execute `mkdir -p ~/Developer/engr852_practice` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 1's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/Developer/engr852_practice` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 1's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.q: [Page 1 · Workstation & X11 Flow] Why must we use `ssh -Y` (trusted X11 forwarding) inside an active XQuartz session when connecting to `926784856@mahmoodi.rcc.at.sfsu.edu`?
options: A) Because Verilog files cannot be edited without a GUI.

B) Because Synopsys Verdi (`verdi`) and Fusion Compiler GUI (`fc_shell -gui`) render X11 graphics on the remote Linux server and forward the window draw calls over SSH to your MacBook's XQuartz display (`localhost:10.0`).
C) Because `ssh -Y` doubles the clock frequency of the Motion Estimator.
D) Because GitHub requires XQuartz to push commits.
quiz_questions.hint: Think about where the Synopsys EDA binaries (`verdi`, `fc_shell`) physically execute (on SFSU's Linux server) versus where your physical monitor is located (on your MacBook Air).
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Verilog source files are plain ASCII text and can be edited in terminal editors (`vim`, `nano`, `cat << 'EOF'`) without any GUI.
Correct! Remote Linux EDA tools are X11 clients; `ssh -Y` sets `DISPLAY=localhost:10.0` on `mahmoodi` and tunnels window drawing commands over SSH to your MacBook's XQuartz X11 server.
Incorrect — Clock frequency (`520 MHz`) is defined in the Verilog testbench (`#0.9615`) and SDC constraints (`create_clock -period 1.923`), not by SSH flags.
Incorrect — `git push` uses HTTPS or SSH port 22 and never uses X11 display forwarding.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Remote Linux EDA tools (`verdi`, `fc_shell -gui`) are X11 clients. `ssh -Y` sets `DISPLAY=localhost:10.0` on `mahmoodi` and securely tunnels X11 GUI frames back to XQuartz on your MacBook Air.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (V1→V9 Top-Level ASIC Port Boundary)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 1 · Rubric & Top-Level Boundary] Why are the frame-buffer memories `RMEM` (256x8) and `SMEM` (1024x8) instantiated inside the testbench (`top_tb.v`) rather than inside the synthesizable `top.v` module?
options: A) To measure and synthesize only the 16-PE systolic motion-estimator core + controller (449 FFs, 0 SRAM macros, 7,854.4 um^2) rather than bloating core area >10x by synthesizing 1,280 bytes (10,240 bits) of frame-buffer storage into standard-cell flip-flops.
B) Because `RMEM` uses analog voltages that cannot be simulated in VCS.
C) Because Synopsys VCS cannot simulate modules with memory ports.
D) Because `AddressR` is an input port of `top.v`.
quiz_questions.hint: Calculate how many D flip-flops would be created if `256 x 8` + `1024 x 8` bits of memory were synthesized directly into standard cells (`1,280 bytes * 8 bits/byte = 10,240 FFs`) vs. the 449 FFs in the 16-PE datapath.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Synthesizing 1,280 bytes of memory as flip-flops would add 10,240 DFFs (more than 22x our 449-FF datapath!). Keeping `RMEM`/`SMEM` in the testbench isolates the pure 16-PE Motion Estimator core.
Incorrect — Both `RMEM` and `SMEM` are pure digital 8-bit behavioral arrays (`reg [7:0] RMEM[0:255]`).
Incorrect — VCS simulates memory ports effortlessly; the separation is strictly an ASIC synthesis boundary decision.
Incorrect — `AddressR[7:0]` is an OUTPUT port driven by `top.v` (`control.v`) to address the external `RMEM`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) `top.v` outputs `AddressR[7:0]`, `AddressS1[9:0]`, `AddressS2[9:0]` and receives `R[7:0]`, `S1[7:0]`, `S2[7:0]` from external memory, keeping the synthesized 14nm core compact (`125.07 x 62.80 um`, 8,230 cells, 449 FFs, 0 SRAM macros).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (520 MHz Timing Budget & Lecture 1 Economics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 1 · Advanced ASIC Specification] Our Motion Estimator targets `f_clk = 520 MHz` in Synopsys `SAED14nm` FinFET with external `RMEM`/`SMEM` memories and `set_input_delay 0.50 ns` / `set_clock_uncertainty -setup 0.30 ns`. If internal DFF setup time is `t_setup = 0.05 ns`, what is the maximum combinational delay allowed on the input path from port `R[7:0]` into `pe0`?
options: B) 1.073 ns (since T_clk = 1/520 MHz = 1.923 ns, and T_logic,max = 1.923 - 0.50 [input_delay] - 0.30 [uncertainty] - 0.05 [t_setup] = 1.073 ns)
quiz_questions.hint: Apply the Midterm Q7 Input-to-Register formula: `T_logic,max = T_clk - set_input_delay - T_uncertainty - T_setup`, where `T_clk = 1000 / 520 = 1.923 ns`.
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — `1.923 ns` is the full clock period `T_clk` before subtracting external input delay (`0.50 ns`), clock uncertainty (`0.30 ns`), and flip-flop setup time (`0.05 ns`).
Correct! By Midterm Q7's Input-to-Register equation: `T_logic,max = 1.923 - 0.50 - 0.30 - 0.05 = 1.073 ns`.
Incorrect — `1.423 ns` subtracts `input_delay (0.50 ns)` but forgets `clock_uncertainty (0.30 ns)` and `t_setup (0.05 ns)`.
Incorrect — `0.500 ns` is the external input arrival delay (`set_input_delay`), not the remaining internal logic budget.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) First compute `T_clk = 1 / (520 x 10^6) = 1.923 ns`. Then subtract external arrival delay (`0.50 ns`), setup uncertainty (`0.30 ns`), and DFF setup time (`0.05 ns`): `1.923 - 0.50 - 0.30 - 0.05 = 1.073 ns`.

choice_diagnostics: Correct! `cd ~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` performs: Executes sequential step operation: `cd ~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 2's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Lecture 1 & EDA Server Architecture)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 2 · Workstation & X11 Flow] Why must we use `ssh -Y` (trusted X11 forwarding) inside an active XQuartz session when connecting to `926784856@mahmoodi.rcc.at.sfsu.edu`?
options: A) Because Verilog files cannot be edited without a GUI.

B) Because Synopsys Verdi (`verdi`) and Fusion Compiler GUI (`fc_shell -gui`) render X11 graphics on the remote Linux server and forward the window draw calls over SSH to your MacBook's XQuartz display (`localhost:10.0`).
C) Because `ssh -Y` doubles the clock frequency of the Motion Estimator.
D) Because GitHub requires XQuartz to push commits.
quiz_questions.hint: Think about where the Synopsys EDA binaries (`verdi`, `fc_shell`) physically execute (on SFSU's Linux server) versus where your physical monitor is located (on your MacBook Air).
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Verilog source files are plain ASCII text and can be edited in terminal editors (`vim`, `nano`, `cat << 'EOF'`) without any GUI.
Correct! Remote Linux EDA tools are X11 clients; `ssh -Y` sets `DISPLAY=localhost:10.0` on `mahmoodi` and tunnels window drawing commands over SSH to your MacBook's XQuartz X11 server.
Incorrect — Clock frequency (`520 MHz`) is defined in the Verilog testbench (`#0.9615`) and SDC constraints (`create_clock -period 1.923`), not by SSH flags.
Incorrect — `git push` uses HTTPS or SSH port 22 and never uses X11 display forwarding.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Remote Linux EDA tools (`verdi`, `fc_shell -gui`) are X11 clients. `ssh -Y` sets `DISPLAY=localhost:10.0` on `mahmoodi` and securely tunnels X11 GUI frames back to XQuartz on your MacBook Air.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (V1→V9 Top-Level ASIC Port Boundary)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 2 · Rubric & Top-Level Boundary] Why are the frame-buffer memories `RMEM` (256x8) and `SMEM` (1024x8) instantiated inside the testbench (`top_tb.v`) rather than inside the synthesizable `top.v` module?
options: A) To measure and synthesize only the 16-PE systolic motion-estimator core + controller (449 FFs, 0 SRAM macros, 7,854.4 um^2) rather than bloating core area >10x by synthesizing 1,280 bytes (10,240 bits) of frame-buffer storage into standard-cell flip-flops.
B) Because `RMEM` uses analog voltages that cannot be simulated in VCS.
C) Because Synopsys VCS cannot simulate modules with memory ports.
D) Because `AddressR` is an input port of `top.v`.
quiz_questions.hint: Calculate how many D flip-flops would be created if `256 x 8` + `1024 x 8` bits of memory were synthesized directly into standard cells (`1,280 bytes * 8 bits/byte = 10,240 FFs`) vs. the 449 FFs in the 16-PE datapath.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Synthesizing 1,280 bytes of memory as flip-flops would add 10,240 DFFs (more than 22x our 449-FF datapath!). Keeping `RMEM`/`SMEM` in the testbench isolates the pure 16-PE Motion Estimator core.
Incorrect — Both `RMEM` and `SMEM` are pure digital 8-bit behavioral arrays (`reg [7:0] RMEM[0:255]`).
Incorrect — VCS simulates memory ports effortlessly; the separation is strictly an ASIC synthesis boundary decision.
Incorrect — `AddressR[7:0]` is an OUTPUT port driven by `top.v` (`control.v`) to address the external `RMEM`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) `top.v` outputs `AddressR[7:0]`, `AddressS1[9:0]`, `AddressS2[9:0]` and receives `R[7:0]`, `S1[7:0]`, `S2[7:0]` from external memory, keeping the synthesized 14nm core compact (`125.07 x 62.80 um`, 8,230 cells, 449 FFs, 0 SRAM macros).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (520 MHz Timing Budget & Lecture 1 Economics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 2 · Advanced ASIC Specification] Our Motion Estimator targets `f_clk = 520 MHz` in Synopsys `SAED14nm` FinFET with external `RMEM`/`SMEM` memories and `set_input_delay 0.50 ns` / `set_clock_uncertainty -setup 0.30 ns`. If internal DFF setup time is `t_setup = 0.05 ns`, what is the maximum combinational delay allowed on the input path from port `R[7:0]` into `pe0`?
options: B) 1.073 ns (since T_clk = 1/520 MHz = 1.923 ns, and T_logic,max = 1.923 - 0.50 [input_delay] - 0.30 [uncertainty] - 0.05 [t_setup] = 1.073 ns)
quiz_questions.hint: Apply the Midterm Q7 Input-to-Register formula: `T_logic,max = T_clk - set_input_delay - T_uncertainty - T_setup`, where `T_clk = 1000 / 520 = 1.923 ns`.
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — `1.923 ns` is the full clock period `T_clk` before subtracting external input delay (`0.50 ns`), clock uncertainty (`0.30 ns`), and flip-flop setup time (`0.05 ns`).
Correct! By Midterm Q7's Input-to-Register equation: `T_logic,max = 1.923 - 0.50 - 0.30 - 0.05 = 1.073 ns`.
Incorrect — `1.423 ns` subtracts `input_delay (0.50 ns)` but forgets `clock_uncertainty (0.30 ns)` and `t_setup (0.05 ns)`.
Incorrect — `0.500 ns` is the external input arrival delay (`set_input_delay`), not the remaining internal logic budget.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) First compute `T_clk = 1 / (520 x 10^6) = 1.923 ns`. Then subtract external arrival delay (`0.50 ns`), setup uncertainty (`0.30 ns`), and DFF setup time (`0.05 ns`): `1.923 - 0.50 - 0.30 - 0.05 = 1.073 ns`.

quiz_questions.hint: Check the environment badge on Page 3: is this step running locally on your MacBook Air or on the remote SFSU Linux EDA server (`mahmoodi`), and how does `snap_step` talk back to the website?

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 3 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 3's combined one-liner, why do we execute `xcode-select -p` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Executes sequential step operation: `xcode-select -p` Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 3's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `xcode-select -p` performs: Executes sequential step operation: `xcode-select -p` And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 3's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Lecture 1 & EDA Server Architecture)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 3 · Workstation & X11 Flow] Why must we use `ssh -Y` (trusted X11 forwarding) inside an active XQuartz session when connecting to `926784856@mahmoodi.rcc.at.sfsu.edu`?
options: A) Because Verilog files cannot be edited without a GUI.

B) Because Synopsys Verdi (`verdi`) and Fusion Compiler GUI (`fc_shell -gui`) render X11 graphics on the remote Linux server and forward the window draw calls over SSH to your MacBook's XQuartz display (`localhost:10.0`).
C) Because `ssh -Y` doubles the clock frequency of the Motion Estimator.
D) Because GitHub requires XQuartz to push commits.
quiz_questions.hint: Think about where the Synopsys EDA binaries (`verdi`, `fc_shell`) physically execute (on SFSU's Linux server) versus where your physical monitor is located (on your MacBook Air).
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Verilog source files are plain ASCII text and can be edited in terminal editors (`vim`, `nano`, `cat << 'EOF'`) without any GUI.
Correct! Remote Linux EDA tools are X11 clients; `ssh -Y` sets `DISPLAY=localhost:10.0` on `mahmoodi` and tunnels window drawing commands over SSH to your MacBook's XQuartz X11 server.
Incorrect — Clock frequency (`520 MHz`) is defined in the Verilog testbench (`#0.9615`) and SDC constraints (`create_clock -period 1.923`), not by SSH flags.
Incorrect — `git push` uses HTTPS or SSH port 22 and never uses X11 display forwarding.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Remote Linux EDA tools (`verdi`, `fc_shell -gui`) are X11 clients. `ssh -Y` sets `DISPLAY=localhost:10.0` on `mahmoodi` and securely tunnels X11 GUI frames back to XQuartz on your MacBook Air.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (V1→V9 Top-Level ASIC Port Boundary)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 3 · Rubric & Top-Level Boundary] Why are the frame-buffer memories `RMEM` (256x8) and `SMEM` (1024x8) instantiated inside the testbench (`top_tb.v`) rather than inside the synthesizable `top.v` module?
options: A) To measure and synthesize only the 16-PE systolic motion-estimator core + controller (449 FFs, 0 SRAM macros, 7,854.4 um^2) rather than bloating core area >10x by synthesizing 1,280 bytes (10,240 bits) of frame-buffer storage into standard-cell flip-flops.
B) Because `RMEM` uses analog voltages that cannot be simulated in VCS.
C) Because Synopsys VCS cannot simulate modules with memory ports.
D) Because `AddressR` is an input port of `top.v`.
quiz_questions.hint: Calculate how many D flip-flops would be created if `256 x 8` + `1024 x 8` bits of memory were synthesized directly into standard cells (`1,280 bytes * 8 bits/byte = 10,240 FFs`) vs. the 449 FFs in the 16-PE datapath.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Synthesizing 1,280 bytes of memory as flip-flops would add 10,240 DFFs (more than 22x our 449-FF datapath!). Keeping `RMEM`/`SMEM` in the testbench isolates the pure 16-PE Motion Estimator core.
Incorrect — Both `RMEM` and `SMEM` are pure digital 8-bit behavioral arrays (`reg [7:0] RMEM[0:255]`).
Incorrect — VCS simulates memory ports effortlessly; the separation is strictly an ASIC synthesis boundary decision.
Incorrect — `AddressR[7:0]` is an OUTPUT port driven by `top.v` (`control.v`) to address the external `RMEM`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) `top.v` outputs `AddressR[7:0]`, `AddressS1[9:0]`, `AddressS2[9:0]` and receives `R[7:0]`, `S1[7:0]`, `S2[7:0]` from external memory, keeping the synthesized 14nm core compact (`125.07 x 62.80 um`, 8,230 cells, 449 FFs, 0 SRAM macros).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (520 MHz Timing Budget & Lecture 1 Economics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 3 · Advanced ASIC Specification] Our Motion Estimator targets `f_clk = 520 MHz` in Synopsys `SAED14nm` FinFET with external `RMEM`/`SMEM` memories and `set_input_delay 0.50 ns` / `set_clock_uncertainty -setup 0.30 ns`. If internal DFF setup time is `t_setup = 0.05 ns`, what is the maximum combinational delay allowed on the input path from port `R[7:0]` into `pe0`?
options: B) 1.073 ns (since T_clk = 1/520 MHz = 1.923 ns, and T_logic,max = 1.923 - 0.50 [input_delay] - 0.30 [uncertainty] - 0.05 [t_setup] = 1.073 ns)
quiz_questions.hint: Apply the Midterm Q7 Input-to-Register formula: `T_logic,max = T_clk - set_input_delay - T_uncertainty - T_setup`, where `T_clk = 1000 / 520 = 1.923 ns`.
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — `1.923 ns` is the full clock period `T_clk` before subtracting external input delay (`0.50 ns`), clock uncertainty (`0.30 ns`), and flip-flop setup time (`0.05 ns`).
Correct! By Midterm Q7's Input-to-Register equation: `T_logic,max = 1.923 - 0.50 - 0.30 - 0.05 = 1.073 ns`.
Incorrect — `1.423 ns` subtracts `input_delay (0.50 ns)` but forgets `clock_uncertainty (0.30 ns)` and `t_setup (0.05 ns)`.
Incorrect — `0.500 ns` is the external input arrival delay (`set_input_delay`), not the remaining internal logic budget.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) First compute `T_clk = 1 / (520 x 10^6) = 1.923 ns`. Then subtract external arrival delay (`0.50 ns`), setup uncertainty (`0.30 ns`), and DFF setup time (`0.05 ns`): `1.923 - 0.50 - 0.30 - 0.05 = 1.073 ns`.

choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Shell commands must be pasted into an active UNIX terminal emulator (`Terminal.app` or `XQuartz xterm`), not a word processor or browser address bar.

Correct! Pasting into your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`) runs the command inside `snap_step`, which automatically checks the exit code and required markers and updates your live `:8788` web console!

Incorrect — A terminal showing `client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe` has lost its SSH connection; you must either use your clean local terminal window or run the Step 0 Auto-Connect command first.
Incorrect — You never need to reboot between pages; `snap_step` preserves your state continuously from Page 1 to Page 100.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Page 4 runs in your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`). Pressing `Return` triggers `snap_step`, which logs the output, captures the screenshot, and sends real-time verification telemetry to the website.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 4 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 4's combined one-liner, why do we execute `export PROJ_LOCAL=$HOME/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual PR` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Executes sequential step operation: `export PROJ_LOCAL=$HOME/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual PROJ_REMOTE=me_asic_new_v1 SFSU_USER=926784856 SFSU_HOST=mahmoodi.rcc.at.sfsu.edu` Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 4's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `export PROJ_LOCAL=$HOME/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic` performs: Executes sequential step operation: `export PROJ_LOCAL=$HOME/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual PROJ_REMOTE=me_asic_new_v1 SFSU_USER=926784856 SFSU_HOST=mahmoodi.rcc.at.sfsu.edu` And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 4's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Lecture 1 & EDA Server Architecture)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 4 · Workstation & X11 Flow] Why must we use `ssh -Y` (trusted X11 forwarding) inside an active XQuartz session when connecting to `926784856@mahmoodi.rcc.at.sfsu.edu`?
options: A) Because Verilog files cannot be edited without a GUI.

B) Because Synopsys Verdi (`verdi`) and Fusion Compiler GUI (`fc_shell -gui`) render X11 graphics on the remote Linux server and forward the window draw calls over SSH to your MacBook's XQuartz display (`localhost:10.0`).
C) Because `ssh -Y` doubles the clock frequency of the Motion Estimator.
D) Because GitHub requires XQuartz to push commits.
quiz_questions.hint: Think about where the Synopsys EDA binaries (`verdi`, `fc_shell`) physically execute (on SFSU's Linux server) versus where your physical monitor is located (on your MacBook Air).
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Verilog source files are plain ASCII text and can be edited in terminal editors (`vim`, `nano`, `cat << 'EOF'`) without any GUI.
Correct! Remote Linux EDA tools are X11 clients; `ssh -Y` sets `DISPLAY=localhost:10.0` on `mahmoodi` and tunnels window drawing commands over SSH to your MacBook's XQuartz X11 server.
Incorrect — Clock frequency (`520 MHz`) is defined in the Verilog testbench (`#0.9615`) and SDC constraints (`create_clock -period 1.923`), not by SSH flags.
Incorrect — `git push` uses HTTPS or SSH port 22 and never uses X11 display forwarding.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Remote Linux EDA tools (`verdi`, `fc_shell -gui`) are X11 clients. `ssh -Y` sets `DISPLAY=localhost:10.0` on `mahmoodi` and securely tunnels X11 GUI frames back to XQuartz on your MacBook Air.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (V1→V9 Top-Level ASIC Port Boundary)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 4 · Rubric & Top-Level Boundary] Why are the frame-buffer memories `RMEM` (256x8) and `SMEM` (1024x8) instantiated inside the testbench (`top_tb.v`) rather than inside the synthesizable `top.v` module?
options: A) To measure and synthesize only the 16-PE systolic motion-estimator core + controller (449 FFs, 0 SRAM macros, 7,854.4 um^2) rather than bloating core area >10x by synthesizing 1,280 bytes (10,240 bits) of frame-buffer storage into standard-cell flip-flops.
B) Because `RMEM` uses analog voltages that cannot be simulated in VCS.
C) Because Synopsys VCS cannot simulate modules with memory ports.
D) Because `AddressR` is an input port of `top.v`.
quiz_questions.hint: Calculate how many D flip-flops would be created if `256 x 8` + `1024 x 8` bits of memory were synthesized directly into standard cells (`1,280 bytes * 8 bits/byte = 10,240 FFs`) vs. the 449 FFs in the 16-PE datapath.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Synthesizing 1,280 bytes of memory as flip-flops would add 10,240 DFFs (more than 22x our 449-FF datapath!). Keeping `RMEM`/`SMEM` in the testbench isolates the pure 16-PE Motion Estimator core.
Incorrect — Both `RMEM` and `SMEM` are pure digital 8-bit behavioral arrays (`reg [7:0] RMEM[0:255]`).
Incorrect — VCS simulates memory ports effortlessly; the separation is strictly an ASIC synthesis boundary decision.
Incorrect — `AddressR[7:0]` is an OUTPUT port driven by `top.v` (`control.v`) to address the external `RMEM`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) `top.v` outputs `AddressR[7:0]`, `AddressS1[9:0]`, `AddressS2[9:0]` and receives `R[7:0]`, `S1[7:0]`, `S2[7:0]` from external memory, keeping the synthesized 14nm core compact (`125.07 x 62.80 um`, 8,230 cells, 449 FFs, 0 SRAM macros).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (520 MHz Timing Budget & Lecture 1 Economics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 4 · Advanced ASIC Specification] Our Motion Estimator targets `f_clk = 520 MHz` in Synopsys `SAED14nm` FinFET with external `RMEM`/`SMEM` memories and `set_input_delay 0.50 ns` / `set_clock_uncertainty -setup 0.30 ns`. If internal DFF setup time is `t_setup = 0.05 ns`, what is the maximum combinational delay allowed on the input path from port `R[7:0]` into `pe0`?
options: B) 1.073 ns (since T_clk = 1/520 MHz = 1.923 ns, and T_logic,max = 1.923 - 0.50 [input_delay] - 0.30 [uncertainty] - 0.05 [t_setup] = 1.073 ns)
quiz_questions.hint: Apply the Midterm Q7 Input-to-Register formula: `T_logic,max = T_clk - set_input_delay - T_uncertainty - T_setup`, where `T_clk = 1000 / 520 = 1.923 ns`.
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — `1.923 ns` is the full clock period `T_clk` before subtracting external input delay (`0.50 ns`), clock uncertainty (`0.30 ns`), and flip-flop setup time (`0.05 ns`).
Correct! By Midterm Q7's Input-to-Register equation: `T_logic,max = 1.923 - 0.50 - 0.30 - 0.05 = 1.073 ns`.
Incorrect — `1.423 ns` subtracts `input_delay (0.50 ns)` but forgets `clock_uncertainty (0.30 ns)` and `t_setup (0.05 ns)`.
Incorrect — `0.500 ns` is the external input arrival delay (`set_input_delay`), not the remaining internal logic budget.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) First compute `T_clk = 1 / (520 x 10^6) = 1.923 ns`. Then subtract external arrival delay (`0.50 ns`), setup uncertainty (`0.30 ns`), and DFF setup time (`0.05 ns`): `1.923 - 0.50 - 0.30 - 0.05 = 1.073 ns`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 1 · Easy (Beginner Foundation & Terminal Orientation)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 5 · Beginner Orientation] Before pasting Page 5's one-liner (`Page 5: Installing & Operating Palo Alto GlobalP`), which terminal environment should you paste into, and what happens immediately after you press `Return`?
options: A) Paste it into Microsoft Word or a browser URL bar.

B) Paste it into your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`); `snap_step` executes the command, verifies the output against Page 5's expected result, and either unlocks the green Post-Lab Learning view or provides a 1-click Auto-Debug Fix command if an error occurs.
C) Paste it into a disconnected terminal window showing `Broken pipe` without reconnecting.
D) Reboot the laptop after every single command.
quiz_questions.hint: Check the environment badge on Page 5: is this step running locally on your MacBook Air or on the remote SFSU Linux EDA server (`mahmoodi`), and how does `snap_step` talk back to the website?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Shell commands must be pasted into an active UNIX terminal emulator (`Terminal.app` or `XQuartz xterm`), not a word processor or browser address bar.

Correct! Pasting into your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`) runs the command inside `snap_step`, which automatically checks the exit code and required markers and updates your live `:8788` web console!

Incorrect — A terminal showing `client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe` has lost its SSH connection; you must either use your clean local terminal window or run the Step 0 Auto-Connect command first.
Incorrect — You never need to reboot between pages; `snap_step` preserves your state continuously from Page 1 to Page 100.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Page 5 runs in your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`). Pressing `Return` triggers `snap_step`, which logs the output, captures the screenshot, and sends real-time verification telemetry to the website.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 5 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 5's combined one-liner, why do we execute `pgrep -fl GlobalProtect || true` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Establishes and verifies encrypted SSH + X11 connectivity over SFSU GlobalProtect VPN to `mahmoodi.rcc.at.sfsu.edu`. Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 5's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `pgrep -fl GlobalProtect || true` performs: Establishes and verifies encrypted SSH + X11 connectivity over SFSU GlobalProtect VPN to `mahmoodi.rcc.at.sfsu.edu`. And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 5's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Lecture 1 & EDA Server Architecture)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 5 · Workstation & X11 Flow] Why must we use `ssh -Y` (trusted X11 forwarding) inside an active XQuartz session when connecting to `926784856@mahmoodi.rcc.at.sfsu.edu`?
options: A) Because Verilog files cannot be edited without a GUI.

B) Because Synopsys Verdi (`verdi`) and Fusion Compiler GUI (`fc_shell -gui`) render X11 graphics on the remote Linux server and forward the window draw calls over SSH to your MacBook's XQuartz display (`localhost:10.0`).
C) Because `ssh -Y` doubles the clock frequency of the Motion Estimator.
D) Because GitHub requires XQuartz to push commits.
quiz_questions.hint: Think about where the Synopsys EDA binaries (`verdi`, `fc_shell`) physically execute (on SFSU's Linux server) versus where your physical monitor is located (on your MacBook Air).
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Verilog source files are plain ASCII text and can be edited in terminal editors (`vim`, `nano`, `cat << 'EOF'`) without any GUI.
Correct! Remote Linux EDA tools are X11 clients; `ssh -Y` sets `DISPLAY=localhost:10.0` on `mahmoodi` and tunnels window drawing commands over SSH to your MacBook's XQuartz X11 server.
Incorrect — Clock frequency (`520 MHz`) is defined in the Verilog testbench (`#0.9615`) and SDC constraints (`create_clock -period 1.923`), not by SSH flags.
Incorrect — `git push` uses HTTPS or SSH port 22 and never uses X11 display forwarding.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Remote Linux EDA tools (`verdi`, `fc_shell -gui`) are X11 clients. `ssh -Y` sets `DISPLAY=localhost:10.0` on `mahmoodi` and securely tunnels X11 GUI frames back to XQuartz on your MacBook Air.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (V1→V9 Top-Level ASIC Port Boundary)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 5 · Rubric & Top-Level Boundary] Why are the frame-buffer memories `RMEM` (256x8) and `SMEM` (1024x8) instantiated inside the testbench (`top_tb.v`) rather than inside the synthesizable `top.v` module?
options: A) To measure and synthesize only the 16-PE systolic motion-estimator core + controller (449 FFs, 0 SRAM macros, 7,854.4 um^2) rather than bloating core area >10x by synthesizing 1,280 bytes (10,240 bits) of frame-buffer storage into standard-cell flip-flops.
B) Because `RMEM` uses analog voltages that cannot be simulated in VCS.
C) Because Synopsys VCS cannot simulate modules with memory ports.
D) Because `AddressR` is an input port of `top.v`.
quiz_questions.hint: Calculate how many D flip-flops would be created if `256 x 8` + `1024 x 8` bits of memory were synthesized directly into standard cells (`1,280 bytes * 8 bits/byte = 10,240 FFs`) vs. the 449 FFs in the 16-PE datapath.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Synthesizing 1,280 bytes of memory as flip-flops would add 10,240 DFFs (more than 22x our 449-FF datapath!). Keeping `RMEM`/`SMEM` in the testbench isolates the pure 16-PE Motion Estimator core.
Incorrect — Both `RMEM` and `SMEM` are pure digital 8-bit behavioral arrays (`reg [7:0] RMEM[0:255]`).
Incorrect — VCS simulates memory ports effortlessly; the separation is strictly an ASIC synthesis boundary decision.
Incorrect — `AddressR[7:0]` is an OUTPUT port driven by `top.v` (`control.v`) to address the external `RMEM`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) `top.v` outputs `AddressR[7:0]`, `AddressS1[9:0]`, `AddressS2[9:0]` and receives `R[7:0]`, `S1[7:0]`, `S2[7:0]` from external memory, keeping the synthesized 14nm core compact (`125.07 x 62.80 um`, 8,230 cells, 449 FFs, 0 SRAM macros).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (520 MHz Timing Budget & Lecture 1 Economics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 5 · Advanced ASIC Specification] Our Motion Estimator targets `f_clk = 520 MHz` in Synopsys `SAED14nm` FinFET with external `RMEM`/`SMEM` memories and `set_input_delay 0.50 ns` / `set_clock_uncertainty -setup 0.30 ns`. If internal DFF setup time is `t_setup = 0.05 ns`, what is the maximum combinational delay allowed on the input path from port `R[7:0]` into `pe0`?
options: B) 1.073 ns (since T_clk = 1/520 MHz = 1.923 ns, and T_logic,max = 1.923 - 0.50 [input_delay] - 0.30 [uncertainty] - 0.05 [t_setup] = 1.073 ns)
quiz_questions.hint: Apply the Midterm Q7 Input-to-Register formula: `T_logic,max = T_clk - set_input_delay - T_uncertainty - T_setup`, where `T_clk = 1000 / 520 = 1.923 ns`.
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — `1.923 ns` is the full clock period `T_clk` before subtracting external input delay (`0.50 ns`), clock uncertainty (`0.30 ns`), and flip-flop setup time (`0.05 ns`).
Correct! By Midterm Q7's Input-to-Register equation: `T_logic,max = 1.923 - 0.50 - 0.30 - 0.05 = 1.073 ns`.
Incorrect — `1.423 ns` subtracts `input_delay (0.50 ns)` but forgets `clock_uncertainty (0.30 ns)` and `t_setup (0.05 ns)`.
Incorrect — `0.500 ns` is the external input arrival delay (`set_input_delay`), not the remaining internal logic budget.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) First compute `T_clk = 1 / (520 x 10^6) = 1.923 ns`. Then subtract external arrival delay (`0.50 ns`), setup uncertainty (`0.30 ns`), and DFF setup time (`0.05 ns`): `1.923 - 0.50 - 0.30 - 0.05 = 1.073 ns`.

three_methods.method3: Hardware & Tool Impact: Keeping `~/me_asic_new_v1` isolated and locking the top-level port contract `module top(clock, start, BestDist, motionX, motionY, AddressR, AddressS1, AddressS2, R, S1, S2)` guarantees that synthesis (`fc_shell`) and testbenches (`vcs`) never suffer port-mismatch errors.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 1 · Easy (Beginner Foundation & Terminal Orientation)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 6 · Beginner Orientation] Before pasting Page 6's one-liner (`Page 6: Installing & Configuring XQuartz on macO`), which terminal environment should you paste into, and what happens immediately after you press `Return`?
options: A) Paste it into Microsoft Word or a browser URL bar.

B) Paste it into your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`); `snap_step` executes the command, verifies the output against Page 6's expected result, and either unlocks the green Post-Lab Learning view or provides a 1-click Auto-Debug Fix command if an error occurs.
C) Paste it into a disconnected terminal window showing `Broken pipe` without reconnecting.
D) Reboot the laptop after every single command.
quiz_questions.hint: Check the environment badge on Page 6: is this step running locally on your MacBook Air or on the remote SFSU Linux EDA server (`mahmoodi`), and how does `snap_step` talk back to the website?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Shell commands must be pasted into an active UNIX terminal emulator (`Terminal.app` or `XQuartz xterm`), not a word processor or browser address bar.

Correct! Pasting into your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`) runs the command inside `snap_step`, which automatically checks the exit code and required markers and updates your live `:8788` web console!

Incorrect — A terminal showing `client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe` has lost its SSH connection; you must either use your clean local terminal window or run the Step 0 Auto-Connect command first.
Incorrect — You never need to reboot between pages; `snap_step` preserves your state continuously from Page 1 to Page 100.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Page 6 runs in your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`). Pressing `Return` triggers `snap_step`, which logs the output, captures the screenshot, and sends real-time verification telemetry to the website.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 6 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 6's combined one-liner, why do we execute `open -a XQuartz` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Starts the macOS XQuartz X11 server and verifies the local/forwarded graphical display socket. Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 6's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `open -a XQuartz` performs: Starts the macOS XQuartz X11 server and verifies the local/forwarded graphical display socket. And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 6's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Lecture 1 & EDA Server Architecture)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 6 · Workstation & X11 Flow] Why must we use `ssh -Y` (trusted X11 forwarding) inside an active XQuartz session when connecting to `926784856@mahmoodi.rcc.at.sfsu.edu`?
options: A) Because Verilog files cannot be edited without a GUI.

B) Because Synopsys Verdi (`verdi`) and Fusion Compiler GUI (`fc_shell -gui`) render X11 graphics on the remote Linux server and forward the window draw calls over SSH to your MacBook's XQuartz display (`localhost:10.0`).
C) Because `ssh -Y` doubles the clock frequency of the Motion Estimator.
D) Because GitHub requires XQuartz to push commits.
quiz_questions.hint: Think about where the Synopsys EDA binaries (`verdi`, `fc_shell`) physically execute (on SFSU's Linux server) versus where your physical monitor is located (on your MacBook Air).
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Verilog source files are plain ASCII text and can be edited in terminal editors (`vim`, `nano`, `cat << 'EOF'`) without any GUI.
Correct! Remote Linux EDA tools are X11 clients; `ssh -Y` sets `DISPLAY=localhost:10.0` on `mahmoodi` and tunnels window drawing commands over SSH to your MacBook's XQuartz X11 server.
Incorrect — Clock frequency (`520 MHz`) is defined in the Verilog testbench (`#0.9615`) and SDC constraints (`create_clock -period 1.923`), not by SSH flags.
Incorrect — `git push` uses HTTPS or SSH port 22 and never uses X11 display forwarding.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Remote Linux EDA tools (`verdi`, `fc_shell -gui`) are X11 clients. `ssh -Y` sets `DISPLAY=localhost:10.0` on `mahmoodi` and securely tunnels X11 GUI frames back to XQuartz on your MacBook Air.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (V1→V9 Top-Level ASIC Port Boundary)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 6 · Rubric & Top-Level Boundary] Why are the frame-buffer memories `RMEM` (256x8) and `SMEM` (1024x8) instantiated inside the testbench (`top_tb.v`) rather than inside the synthesizable `top.v` module?
options: A) To measure and synthesize only the 16-PE systolic motion-estimator core + controller (449 FFs, 0 SRAM macros, 7,854.4 um^2) rather than bloating core area >10x by synthesizing 1,280 bytes (10,240 bits) of frame-buffer storage into standard-cell flip-flops.
B) Because `RMEM` uses analog voltages that cannot be simulated in VCS.
C) Because Synopsys VCS cannot simulate modules with memory ports.
D) Because `AddressR` is an input port of `top.v`.
quiz_questions.hint: Calculate how many D flip-flops would be created if `256 x 8` + `1024 x 8` bits of memory were synthesized directly into standard cells (`1,280 bytes * 8 bits/byte = 10,240 FFs`) vs. the 449 FFs in the 16-PE datapath.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Synthesizing 1,280 bytes of memory as flip-flops would add 10,240 DFFs (more than 22x our 449-FF datapath!). Keeping `RMEM`/`SMEM` in the testbench isolates the pure 16-PE Motion Estimator core.
Incorrect — Both `RMEM` and `SMEM` are pure digital 8-bit behavioral arrays (`reg [7:0] RMEM[0:255]`).
Incorrect — VCS simulates memory ports effortlessly; the separation is strictly an ASIC synthesis boundary decision.
Incorrect — `AddressR[7:0]` is an OUTPUT port driven by `top.v` (`control.v`) to address the external `RMEM`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) `top.v` outputs `AddressR[7:0]`, `AddressS1[9:0]`, `AddressS2[9:0]` and receives `R[7:0]`, `S1[7:0]`, `S2[7:0]` from external memory, keeping the synthesized 14nm core compact (`125.07 x 62.80 um`, 8,230 cells, 449 FFs, 0 SRAM macros).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (520 MHz Timing Budget & Lecture 1 Economics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 6 · Advanced ASIC Specification] Our Motion Estimator targets `f_clk = 520 MHz` in Synopsys `SAED14nm` FinFET with external `RMEM`/`SMEM` memories and `set_input_delay 0.50 ns` / `set_clock_uncertainty -setup 0.30 ns`. If internal DFF setup time is `t_setup = 0.05 ns`, what is the maximum combinational delay allowed on the input path from port `R[7:0]` into `pe0`?
options: B) 1.073 ns (since T_clk = 1/520 MHz = 1.923 ns, and T_logic,max = 1.923 - 0.50 [input_delay] - 0.30 [uncertainty] - 0.05 [t_setup] = 1.073 ns)
quiz_questions.hint: Apply the Midterm Q7 Input-to-Register formula: `T_logic,max = T_clk - set_input_delay - T_uncertainty - T_setup`, where `T_clk = 1000 / 520 = 1.923 ns`.
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — `1.923 ns` is the full clock period `T_clk` before subtracting external input delay (`0.50 ns`), clock uncertainty (`0.30 ns`), and flip-flop setup time (`0.05 ns`).
Correct! By Midterm Q7's Input-to-Register equation: `T_logic,max = 1.923 - 0.50 - 0.30 - 0.05 = 1.073 ns`.
Incorrect — `1.423 ns` subtracts `input_delay (0.50 ns)` but forgets `clock_uncertainty (0.30 ns)` and `t_setup (0.05 ns)`.
Incorrect — `0.500 ns` is the external input arrival delay (`set_input_delay`), not the remaining internal logic budget.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) First compute `T_clk = 1 / (520 x 10^6) = 1.923 ns`. Then subtract external arrival delay (`0.50 ns`), setup uncertainty (`0.30 ns`), and DFF setup time (`0.05 ns`): `1.923 - 0.50 - 0.30 - 0.05 = 1.073 ns`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 1 · Easy (Beginner Foundation & Terminal Orientation)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 7 · Beginner Orientation] Before pasting Page 7's one-liner (`Page 7: How XQuartz + ssh -Y Works  -  Visual X1`), which terminal environment should you paste into, and what happens immediately after you press `Return`?
options: A) Paste it into Microsoft Word or a browser URL bar.

B) Paste it into your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`); `snap_step` executes the command, verifies the output against Page 7's expected result, and either unlocks the green Post-Lab Learning view or provides a 1-click Auto-Debug Fix command if an error occurs.
C) Paste it into a disconnected terminal window showing `Broken pipe` without reconnecting.
D) Reboot the laptop after every single command.
quiz_questions.hint: Check the environment badge on Page 7: is this step running locally on your MacBook Air or on the remote SFSU Linux EDA server (`mahmoodi`), and how does `snap_step` talk back to the website?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Shell commands must be pasted into an active UNIX terminal emulator (`Terminal.app` or `XQuartz xterm`), not a word processor or browser address bar.

Correct! Pasting into your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`) runs the command inside `snap_step`, which automatically checks the exit code and required markers and updates your live `:8788` web console!

Incorrect — A terminal showing `client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe` has lost its SSH connection; you must either use your clean local terminal window or run the Step 0 Auto-Connect command first.
Incorrect — You never need to reboot between pages; `snap_step` preserves your state continuously from Page 1 to Page 100.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Page 7 runs in your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`). Pressing `Return` triggers `snap_step`, which logs the output, captures the screenshot, and sends real-time verification telemetry to the website.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 7 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 7's combined one-liner, why do we execute `mkdir -p ~/.ssh` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 7's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/.ssh` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 7's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Lecture 1 & EDA Server Architecture)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 7 · Workstation & X11 Flow] Why must we use `ssh -Y` (trusted X11 forwarding) inside an active XQuartz session when connecting to `926784856@mahmoodi.rcc.at.sfsu.edu`?
options: A) Because Verilog files cannot be edited without a GUI.

B) Because Synopsys Verdi (`verdi`) and Fusion Compiler GUI (`fc_shell -gui`) render X11 graphics on the remote Linux server and forward the window draw calls over SSH to your MacBook's XQuartz display (`localhost:10.0`).
C) Because `ssh -Y` doubles the clock frequency of the Motion Estimator.
D) Because GitHub requires XQuartz to push commits.
quiz_questions.hint: Think about where the Synopsys EDA binaries (`verdi`, `fc_shell`) physically execute (on SFSU's Linux server) versus where your physical monitor is located (on your MacBook Air).
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Verilog source files are plain ASCII text and can be edited in terminal editors (`vim`, `nano`, `cat << 'EOF'`) without any GUI.
Correct! Remote Linux EDA tools are X11 clients; `ssh -Y` sets `DISPLAY=localhost:10.0` on `mahmoodi` and tunnels window drawing commands over SSH to your MacBook's XQuartz X11 server.
Incorrect — Clock frequency (`520 MHz`) is defined in the Verilog testbench (`#0.9615`) and SDC constraints (`create_clock -period 1.923`), not by SSH flags.
Incorrect — `git push` uses HTTPS or SSH port 22 and never uses X11 display forwarding.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Remote Linux EDA tools (`verdi`, `fc_shell -gui`) are X11 clients. `ssh -Y` sets `DISPLAY=localhost:10.0` on `mahmoodi` and securely tunnels X11 GUI frames back to XQuartz on your MacBook Air.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (V1→V9 Top-Level ASIC Port Boundary)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 7 · Rubric & Top-Level Boundary] Why are the frame-buffer memories `RMEM` (256x8) and `SMEM` (1024x8) instantiated inside the testbench (`top_tb.v`) rather than inside the synthesizable `top.v` module?
options: A) To measure and synthesize only the 16-PE systolic motion-estimator core + controller (449 FFs, 0 SRAM macros, 7,854.4 um^2) rather than bloating core area >10x by synthesizing 1,280 bytes (10,240 bits) of frame-buffer storage into standard-cell flip-flops.
B) Because `RMEM` uses analog voltages that cannot be simulated in VCS.
C) Because Synopsys VCS cannot simulate modules with memory ports.
D) Because `AddressR` is an input port of `top.v`.
quiz_questions.hint: Calculate how many D flip-flops would be created if `256 x 8` + `1024 x 8` bits of memory were synthesized directly into standard cells (`1,280 bytes * 8 bits/byte = 10,240 FFs`) vs. the 449 FFs in the 16-PE datapath.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Synthesizing 1,280 bytes of memory as flip-flops would add 10,240 DFFs (more than 22x our 449-FF datapath!). Keeping `RMEM`/`SMEM` in the testbench isolates the pure 16-PE Motion Estimator core.
Incorrect — Both `RMEM` and `SMEM` are pure digital 8-bit behavioral arrays (`reg [7:0] RMEM[0:255]`).
Incorrect — VCS simulates memory ports effortlessly; the separation is strictly an ASIC synthesis boundary decision.
Incorrect — `AddressR[7:0]` is an OUTPUT port driven by `top.v` (`control.v`) to address the external `RMEM`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) `top.v` outputs `AddressR[7:0]`, `AddressS1[9:0]`, `AddressS2[9:0]` and receives `R[7:0]`, `S1[7:0]`, `S2[7:0]` from external memory, keeping the synthesized 14nm core compact (`125.07 x 62.80 um`, 8,230 cells, 449 FFs, 0 SRAM macros).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (520 MHz Timing Budget & Lecture 1 Economics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 7 · Advanced ASIC Specification] Our Motion Estimator targets `f_clk = 520 MHz` in Synopsys `SAED14nm` FinFET with external `RMEM`/`SMEM` memories and `set_input_delay 0.50 ns` / `set_clock_uncertainty -setup 0.30 ns`. If internal DFF setup time is `t_setup = 0.05 ns`, what is the maximum combinational delay allowed on the input path from port `R[7:0]` into `pe0`?
options: B) 1.073 ns (since T_clk = 1/520 MHz = 1.923 ns, and T_logic,max = 1.923 - 0.50 [input_delay] - 0.30 [uncertainty] - 0.05 [t_setup] = 1.073 ns)
quiz_questions.hint: Apply the Midterm Q7 Input-to-Register formula: `T_logic,max = T_clk - set_input_delay - T_uncertainty - T_setup`, where `T_clk = 1000 / 520 = 1.923 ns`.
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — `1.923 ns` is the full clock period `T_clk` before subtracting external input delay (`0.50 ns`), clock uncertainty (`0.30 ns`), and flip-flop setup time (`0.05 ns`).
Correct! By Midterm Q7's Input-to-Register equation: `T_logic,max = 1.923 - 0.50 - 0.30 - 0.05 = 1.073 ns`.
Incorrect — `1.423 ns` subtracts `input_delay (0.50 ns)` but forgets `clock_uncertainty (0.30 ns)` and `t_setup (0.05 ns)`.
Incorrect — `0.500 ns` is the external input arrival delay (`set_input_delay`), not the remaining internal logic budget.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) First compute `T_clk = 1 / (520 x 10^6) = 1.923 ns`. Then subtract external arrival delay (`0.50 ns`), setup uncertainty (`0.30 ns`), and DFF setup time (`0.05 ns`): `1.923 - 0.50 - 0.30 - 0.05 = 1.073 ns`.

table_rows: Why SSH Rejects Keys If Wrong

Automatically enables ForwardX11Trusted yes for mahmoodi
trap_notes: RED:[!] TRAP: Home Directory or ~/.ssh Group-Writable on mahmoodi! [!]

code_block: # Run on your new MacBook Air Terminal:
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "engr852-new-laptop" -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 -N ""
cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub | ssh 926784856@mahmoodi.rcc.at.sfsu.edu \
"mkdir -p ~/.ssh && chmod 700 ~/.ssh && cat >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys && chmod 600 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys"
cat << 'EOF' >> ~/.ssh/config
Host mahmoodi
HostName mahmoodi.rcc.at.sfsu.edu
IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
ForwardX11 yes
ForwardX11Trusted yes
ServerAliveInterval 30
EOF
chmod 600 ~/.ssh/config

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 1 · Easy (Beginner Foundation & Terminal Orientation)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 8 · Beginner Orientation] Before pasting Page 8's one-liner (`Page 8: Setting Up Passwordless Ed25519 SSH Keys`), which terminal environment should you paste into, and what happens immediately after you press `Return`?
options: A) Paste it into Microsoft Word or a browser URL bar.

B) Paste it into your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`); `snap_step` executes the command, verifies the output against Page 8's expected result, and either unlocks the green Post-Lab Learning view or provides a 1-click Auto-Debug Fix command if an error occurs.
C) Paste it into a disconnected terminal window showing `Broken pipe` without reconnecting.
D) Reboot the laptop after every single command.
quiz_questions.hint: Check the environment badge on Page 8: is this step running locally on your MacBook Air or on the remote SFSU Linux EDA server (`mahmoodi`), and how does `snap_step` talk back to the website?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Shell commands must be pasted into an active UNIX terminal emulator (`Terminal.app` or `XQuartz xterm`), not a word processor or browser address bar.

Correct! Pasting into your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`) runs the command inside `snap_step`, which automatically checks the exit code and required markers and updates your live `:8788` web console!

Incorrect — A terminal showing `client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe` has lost its SSH connection; you must either use your clean local terminal window or run the Step 0 Auto-Connect command first.
Incorrect — You never need to reboot between pages; `snap_step` preserves your state continuously from Page 1 to Page 100.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Page 8 runs in your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`). Pressing `Return` triggers `snap_step`, which logs the output, captures the screenshot, and sends real-time verification telemetry to the website.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 8 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 8's combined one-liner, why do we execute `cd ~/motion-estimator-asic-lab-notebook-2026` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Executes sequential step operation: `cd ~/motion-estimator-asic-lab-notebook-2026` Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 8's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `cd ~/motion-estimator-asic-lab-notebook-2026` performs: Executes sequential step operation: `cd ~/motion-estimator-asic-lab-notebook-2026` And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 8's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Lecture 1 & EDA Server Architecture)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 8 · Workstation & X11 Flow] Why must we use `ssh -Y` (trusted X11 forwarding) inside an active XQuartz session when connecting to `926784856@mahmoodi.rcc.at.sfsu.edu`?
options: A) Because Verilog files cannot be edited without a GUI.

B) Because Synopsys Verdi (`verdi`) and Fusion Compiler GUI (`fc_shell -gui`) render X11 graphics on the remote Linux server and forward the window draw calls over SSH to your MacBook's XQuartz display (`localhost:10.0`).
C) Because `ssh -Y` doubles the clock frequency of the Motion Estimator.
D) Because GitHub requires XQuartz to push commits.
quiz_questions.hint: Think about where the Synopsys EDA binaries (`verdi`, `fc_shell`) physically execute (on SFSU's Linux server) versus where your physical monitor is located (on your MacBook Air).
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Verilog source files are plain ASCII text and can be edited in terminal editors (`vim`, `nano`, `cat << 'EOF'`) without any GUI.
Correct! Remote Linux EDA tools are X11 clients; `ssh -Y` sets `DISPLAY=localhost:10.0` on `mahmoodi` and tunnels window drawing commands over SSH to your MacBook's XQuartz X11 server.
Incorrect — Clock frequency (`520 MHz`) is defined in the Verilog testbench (`#0.9615`) and SDC constraints (`create_clock -period 1.923`), not by SSH flags.
Incorrect — `git push` uses HTTPS or SSH port 22 and never uses X11 display forwarding.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Remote Linux EDA tools (`verdi`, `fc_shell -gui`) are X11 clients. `ssh -Y` sets `DISPLAY=localhost:10.0` on `mahmoodi` and securely tunnels X11 GUI frames back to XQuartz on your MacBook Air.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (V1→V9 Top-Level ASIC Port Boundary)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 8 · Rubric & Top-Level Boundary] Why are the frame-buffer memories `RMEM` (256x8) and `SMEM` (1024x8) instantiated inside the testbench (`top_tb.v`) rather than inside the synthesizable `top.v` module?
options: A) To measure and synthesize only the 16-PE systolic motion-estimator core + controller (449 FFs, 0 SRAM macros, 7,854.4 um^2) rather than bloating core area >10x by synthesizing 1,280 bytes (10,240 bits) of frame-buffer storage into standard-cell flip-flops.
B) Because `RMEM` uses analog voltages that cannot be simulated in VCS.
C) Because Synopsys VCS cannot simulate modules with memory ports.
D) Because `AddressR` is an input port of `top.v`.
quiz_questions.hint: Calculate how many D flip-flops would be created if `256 x 8` + `1024 x 8` bits of memory were synthesized directly into standard cells (`1,280 bytes * 8 bits/byte = 10,240 FFs`) vs. the 449 FFs in the 16-PE datapath.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Synthesizing 1,280 bytes of memory as flip-flops would add 10,240 DFFs (more than 22x our 449-FF datapath!). Keeping `RMEM`/`SMEM` in the testbench isolates the pure 16-PE Motion Estimator core.
Incorrect — Both `RMEM` and `SMEM` are pure digital 8-bit behavioral arrays (`reg [7:0] RMEM[0:255]`).
Incorrect — VCS simulates memory ports effortlessly; the separation is strictly an ASIC synthesis boundary decision.
Incorrect — `AddressR[7:0]` is an OUTPUT port driven by `top.v` (`control.v`) to address the external `RMEM`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) `top.v` outputs `AddressR[7:0]`, `AddressS1[9:0]`, `AddressS2[9:0]` and receives `R[7:0]`, `S1[7:0]`, `S2[7:0]` from external memory, keeping the synthesized 14nm core compact (`125.07 x 62.80 um`, 8,230 cells, 449 FFs, 0 SRAM macros).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (520 MHz Timing Budget & Lecture 1 Economics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 8 · Advanced ASIC Specification] Our Motion Estimator targets `f_clk = 520 MHz` in Synopsys `SAED14nm` FinFET with external `RMEM`/`SMEM` memories and `set_input_delay 0.50 ns` / `set_clock_uncertainty -setup 0.30 ns`. If internal DFF setup time is `t_setup = 0.05 ns`, what is the maximum combinational delay allowed on the input path from port `R[7:0]` into `pe0`?
options: B) 1.073 ns (since T_clk = 1/520 MHz = 1.923 ns, and T_logic,max = 1.923 - 0.50 [input_delay] - 0.30 [uncertainty] - 0.05 [t_setup] = 1.073 ns)
quiz_questions.hint: Apply the Midterm Q7 Input-to-Register formula: `T_logic,max = T_clk - set_input_delay - T_uncertainty - T_setup`, where `T_clk = 1000 / 520 = 1.923 ns`.
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — `1.923 ns` is the full clock period `T_clk` before subtracting external input delay (`0.50 ns`), clock uncertainty (`0.30 ns`), and flip-flop setup time (`0.05 ns`).
Correct! By Midterm Q7's Input-to-Register equation: `T_logic,max = 1.923 - 0.50 - 0.30 - 0.05 = 1.073 ns`.
Incorrect — `1.423 ns` subtracts `input_delay (0.50 ns)` but forgets `clock_uncertainty (0.30 ns)` and `t_setup (0.05 ns)`.
Incorrect — `0.500 ns` is the external input arrival delay (`set_input_delay`), not the remaining internal logic budget.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) First compute `T_clk = 1 / (520 x 10^6) = 1.923 ns`. Then subtract external arrival delay (`0.50 ns`), setup uncertainty (`0.30 ns`), and DFF setup time (`0.05 ns`): `1.923 - 0.50 - 0.30 - 0.05 = 1.073 ns`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 1 · Easy (Beginner Foundation & Terminal Orientation)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 9 · Beginner Orientation] Before pasting Page 9's one-liner (`Page 9: Creating a Brand-New Isolated Workspace `), which terminal environment should you paste into, and what happens immediately after you press `Return`?
options: A) Paste it into Microsoft Word or a browser URL bar.

B) Paste it into your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`); `snap_step` executes the command, verifies the output against Page 9's expected result, and either unlocks the green Post-Lab Learning view or provides a 1-click Auto-Debug Fix command if an error occurs.
C) Paste it into a disconnected terminal window showing `Broken pipe` without reconnecting.
D) Reboot the laptop after every single command.
quiz_questions.hint: Check the environment badge on Page 9: is this step running locally on your MacBook Air or on the remote SFSU Linux EDA server (`mahmoodi`), and how does `snap_step` talk back to the website?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Shell commands must be pasted into an active UNIX terminal emulator (`Terminal.app` or `XQuartz xterm`), not a word processor or browser address bar.

Correct! Pasting into your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`) runs the command inside `snap_step`, which automatically checks the exit code and required markers and updates your live `:8788` web console!

Incorrect — A terminal showing `client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe` has lost its SSH connection; you must either use your clean local terminal window or run the Step 0 Auto-Connect command first.
Incorrect — You never need to reboot between pages; `snap_step` preserves your state continuously from Page 1 to Page 100.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Page 9 runs in your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`). Pressing `Return` triggers `snap_step`, which logs the output, captures the screenshot, and sends real-time verification telemetry to the website.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 9 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 9's combined one-liner, why do we execute `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/{rtl/8bit,rtl/16bit,tb/8bit,tb/16bit,constra` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 9's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/{rtl/8bit,rtl/16bit,tb/8bit,tb/16b` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 9's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Lecture 1 & EDA Server Architecture)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 9 · Workstation & X11 Flow] Why must we use `ssh -Y` (trusted X11 forwarding) inside an active XQuartz session when connecting to `926784856@mahmoodi.rcc.at.sfsu.edu`?
options: A) Because Verilog files cannot be edited without a GUI.

B) Because Synopsys Verdi (`verdi`) and Fusion Compiler GUI (`fc_shell -gui`) render X11 graphics on the remote Linux server and forward the window draw calls over SSH to your MacBook's XQuartz display (`localhost:10.0`).
C) Because `ssh -Y` doubles the clock frequency of the Motion Estimator.
D) Because GitHub requires XQuartz to push commits.
quiz_questions.hint: Think about where the Synopsys EDA binaries (`verdi`, `fc_shell`) physically execute (on SFSU's Linux server) versus where your physical monitor is located (on your MacBook Air).
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Verilog source files are plain ASCII text and can be edited in terminal editors (`vim`, `nano`, `cat << 'EOF'`) without any GUI.
Correct! Remote Linux EDA tools are X11 clients; `ssh -Y` sets `DISPLAY=localhost:10.0` on `mahmoodi` and tunnels window drawing commands over SSH to your MacBook's XQuartz X11 server.
Incorrect — Clock frequency (`520 MHz`) is defined in the Verilog testbench (`#0.9615`) and SDC constraints (`create_clock -period 1.923`), not by SSH flags.
Incorrect — `git push` uses HTTPS or SSH port 22 and never uses X11 display forwarding.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Remote Linux EDA tools (`verdi`, `fc_shell -gui`) are X11 clients. `ssh -Y` sets `DISPLAY=localhost:10.0` on `mahmoodi` and securely tunnels X11 GUI frames back to XQuartz on your MacBook Air.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (V1→V9 Top-Level ASIC Port Boundary)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 9 · Rubric & Top-Level Boundary] Why are the frame-buffer memories `RMEM` (256x8) and `SMEM` (1024x8) instantiated inside the testbench (`top_tb.v`) rather than inside the synthesizable `top.v` module?
options: A) To measure and synthesize only the 16-PE systolic motion-estimator core + controller (449 FFs, 0 SRAM macros, 7,854.4 um^2) rather than bloating core area >10x by synthesizing 1,280 bytes (10,240 bits) of frame-buffer storage into standard-cell flip-flops.
B) Because `RMEM` uses analog voltages that cannot be simulated in VCS.
C) Because Synopsys VCS cannot simulate modules with memory ports.
D) Because `AddressR` is an input port of `top.v`.
quiz_questions.hint: Calculate how many D flip-flops would be created if `256 x 8` + `1024 x 8` bits of memory were synthesized directly into standard cells (`1,280 bytes * 8 bits/byte = 10,240 FFs`) vs. the 449 FFs in the 16-PE datapath.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Synthesizing 1,280 bytes of memory as flip-flops would add 10,240 DFFs (more than 22x our 449-FF datapath!). Keeping `RMEM`/`SMEM` in the testbench isolates the pure 16-PE Motion Estimator core.
Incorrect — Both `RMEM` and `SMEM` are pure digital 8-bit behavioral arrays (`reg [7:0] RMEM[0:255]`).
Incorrect — VCS simulates memory ports effortlessly; the separation is strictly an ASIC synthesis boundary decision.
Incorrect — `AddressR[7:0]` is an OUTPUT port driven by `top.v` (`control.v`) to address the external `RMEM`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) `top.v` outputs `AddressR[7:0]`, `AddressS1[9:0]`, `AddressS2[9:0]` and receives `R[7:0]`, `S1[7:0]`, `S2[7:0]` from external memory, keeping the synthesized 14nm core compact (`125.07 x 62.80 um`, 8,230 cells, 449 FFs, 0 SRAM macros).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (520 MHz Timing Budget & Lecture 1 Economics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 9 · Advanced ASIC Specification] Our Motion Estimator targets `f_clk = 520 MHz` in Synopsys `SAED14nm` FinFET with external `RMEM`/`SMEM` memories and `set_input_delay 0.50 ns` / `set_clock_uncertainty -setup 0.30 ns`. If internal DFF setup time is `t_setup = 0.05 ns`, what is the maximum combinational delay allowed on the input path from port `R[7:0]` into `pe0`?
options: B) 1.073 ns (since T_clk = 1/520 MHz = 1.923 ns, and T_logic,max = 1.923 - 0.50 [input_delay] - 0.30 [uncertainty] - 0.05 [t_setup] = 1.073 ns)
quiz_questions.hint: Apply the Midterm Q7 Input-to-Register formula: `T_logic,max = T_clk - set_input_delay - T_uncertainty - T_setup`, where `T_clk = 1000 / 520 = 1.923 ns`.
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — `1.923 ns` is the full clock period `T_clk` before subtracting external input delay (`0.50 ns`), clock uncertainty (`0.30 ns`), and flip-flop setup time (`0.05 ns`).
Correct! By Midterm Q7's Input-to-Register equation: `T_logic,max = 1.923 - 0.50 - 0.30 - 0.05 = 1.073 ns`.
Incorrect — `1.423 ns` subtracts `input_delay (0.50 ns)` but forgets `clock_uncertainty (0.30 ns)` and `t_setup (0.05 ns)`.
Incorrect — `0.500 ns` is the external input arrival delay (`set_input_delay`), not the remaining internal logic budget.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) First compute `T_clk = 1 / (520 x 10^6) = 1.923 ns`. Then subtract external arrival delay (`0.50 ns`), setup uncertainty (`0.30 ns`), and DFF setup time (`0.05 ns`): `1.923 - 0.50 - 0.30 - 0.05 = 1.073 ns`.
