code_block: // Top-level module signature (rtl/16bit/top.v):
module top (clock, start, BestDist, motionX, motionY, AddressR, AddressS1, AddressS2, R, S1, S2);
input clock, start; input [7:0] R, S1, S2;
output [15:0] BestDist; output [7:0] motionX, motionY, AddressR; output [9:0] AddressS1, AddressS2;
// --- Interactive Hardware Verification of This Architectural Step on mahmoodi ---

TERM_SFSU: [926784856@mahmoodi me_asic_new_v1]$ tcsh -c 'source ./scripts/synopsys_setup.tcl; vcs -full64 -sverilog -debug_access+all rtl/16bit/top.v tb/16bit/top_tb_direct.v -o simv_check && ./simv_check'
OUT_OK:    Cycle 256 (0x0100): CompStart=1, PEready=0x0001 | Cycle 4111 (0x100F): completed=1, BestDist=16'h0000
// --- Comparing 8-Bit Baseline (rtl/8bit/top.v) vs. 16-Bit Non-Saturating Upgrade (rtl/16bit/top.v) ---
01: // In 8-bit PE:  {Carry, AccumulateIn} = Accumulate + difference; if (Carry == 1) AccumulateIn = 8'hFF;
02: // In 16-bit PE: AccumulateIn = Accumulate + {8'd0, difference};  // Exact sum up to 256*255 = 65,280 (16'hFF00)
03: // In 8-bit Control:  reg [11:0] count; // Wraps to 0 at cycle 4096 -> resets BestDist during Row 15!
04: // In 16-bit Control: reg [12:0] count; reg completed; // Holds at count == 13'h100F (cycle 4111)!
05: // In 8-bit Comparator:  if (CompStart == 0) BestDist <= 8'hFF;   // Ties when newDist == 8'hFF!
06: // In 16-bit Comparator: if (CompStart == 0) BestDist <= 16'hFFFF; // 16'hFF00 < 16'hFFFF is always TRUE!
// --- Course Project Syllabus Requirements Checklist (Items 1-5) ---
07: // [x] Clock Period = 1.923 ns (520.02 MHz) | Input Delay = 0.5 ns | Output Delay = 0.5 ns | Uncertainty = 0.2 ns
08: // [x] Exclude Reference (RMEM 256x8) and Search (SMEM 1024x8) memories from top.v synthesis!

cmd_explanations: - **`clock`** → **`input (top)`**: 1 bit | 1 bit | Clock (520 MHz) | Global rising-edge clock (1.923 ns period)
- **`start`** → **`input (top)`**: 1 bit | 1 bit | Synchronous Ctrl | 0 = reset counter/BestDist; 1 = run 4,111-cycle search
- **`R, S1, S2`** → **`input (top)`**: [7:0] each | [7:0] each | Registered in TB | Reference pixel byte and dual search window pixel bytes
- **`AddressR`** → **`output (top)`**: [7:0] | [7:0] | Comb from count | 8-bit address (0..255) into external RMEM
- **`AddressS1, AddressS2`** → **`output (top)`**: [9:0] each | [9:0] each | Comb from count | 10-bit addresses (0..960) into external SMEM
- **`BestDist`** → **`output reg (top)`**: [7:0] | [15:0] | Clocked DFF | Minimum distortion D(i*,j*) found across all candidates
- **`motionX, motionY`** → **`output reg (top)`**: [7:0] each | [7:0] each | Clocked DFF | Signed 2's complement motion vector (i*-8, j*-8)
- **`PEout`** → **`wire (internal)`**: [127:0] | [255:0] | Clocked in PEs | Concatenated bus of all 16 PE Accumulate registers

foundation_text: Chapter 10 Sec. 10.4 Foundation Bridge (Page 24): Each grayscale video pixel is an 8-bit unsigned integer `0..255` (`2^8 = 256` levels). Comparing a 16x16 Reference macroblock (`256` pixels) against a 16x16 Search candidate adds 256 absolute differences `|R - S|`. Since each pixel difference can be up to `255`, the maximum possible sum is `256 * 255 = 65,280` (`16'hFF00`).

three_methods.method1: Behavior on Page 24 (Page 24: Complete Hardware-to-Verilog Signal Dictionary for module top): Trace how the 16 Processing Elements (`PE0..PE15`) evaluate 16 horizontal candidates `u in [-8..+7]` in parallel while `R` shifts through `Rpipe[0..14]`.
three_methods.method2: Mathematical & Bit-Width Proof: `SAD(u,v) = sum_{i=0..15} sum_{j=0..15} |R(i,j) - S(i+u, j+v)|`. Bit width required = `ceil(log2(256 * 255 + 1)) = 16 bits` (`max 65,535 = 16'hFFFF`). An 8-bit register (`max 255 = 8'hFF`) overflows on Row 0 whenever average `|R-S| >= 1`!
three_methods.method3: RTL & Hardware Mapping: Each PE needs an 8-bit 2:1 mux (`S1` vs `S2`), an 8-bit absolute difference circuit (`|R - S|`), a 16-bit adder, and a 16-bit DFF accumulator (`Accumulate[15:0]`), feeding a 16:1 mux and 16-bit comparator (`BestDist[15:0]`).

Correct! Pasting into your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`) runs the command inside `snap_step`, which automatically checks the exit code and required markers and updates your live `:8788` web console!

Incorrect — A terminal showing `client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe` has lost its SSH connection; you must either use your clean local terminal window or run the Step 0 Auto-Connect command first.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 24 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 24's combined one-liner, why do we execute `snap_step "page024_complete_hardware_verilog_signal" 'diff -u ~/ENGR85` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Loads the telemetry bridge and wraps the page's command sequence in the Expected-Outcome Verifier. Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 24's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `snap_step "page024_complete_hardware_verilog_signal" 'diff -` performs: Loads the telemetry bridge and wraps the page's command sequence in the Expected-Outcome Verifier. And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 24's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Ch. 10 SAD Bit-Width & Saturation Math)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 24 · Bit-Width & Saturation Math (Midterm Q2 Connection)] What is the maximum possible SAD value for a 16x16 macroblock of 8-bit pixels (`0..255`), and how many bits are required to represent it without saturation or wrap-around?
options: A) Max SAD = 255 (8'hFF); requires 8 bits.
B) Max SAD = 4,080 (16'h0FF0); requires 12 bits.
C) Max SAD = 65,280 (16'hFF00 = 256 pixels * 255 max diff); requires 16 bits (with 16'hFFFF = 65,535 reserved as the initial BestDist).
D) Max SAD = 65,536; requires 17 bits.
quiz_questions.hint: Multiply the total number of pixels in a 16x16 macroblock (`16 * 16 = 256`) by the maximum possible 8-bit pixel difference (`|255 - 0| = 255`).
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — `255 (8'hFF)` is the maximum difference of a SINGLE pixel, not the sum across 256 pixels!
Incorrect — `4,080 (16 * 255)` is the maximum SAD of a single 16-pixel row (`Row 0`), not all 16 rows (`256` pixels).
Correct! `256 pixels * 255 max diff = 65,280 = 16'hFF00`. Using 16 bits (`max 65,535 = 16'hFFFF`) prevents overflow and leaves `16'hFFFF` as a valid sentinel initial value for `BestDist`!
Incorrect — `65,280` fits comfortably inside 16 unsigned bits (`0..65,535`), so a 17th bit is unnecessary.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: C) `16 * 16 = 256` pixels, each with max difference `|0 - 255| = 255`. Thus `SAD_max = 256 * 255 = 65,280 = 16'hFF00`. Using 16 bits allows `BestDist` to initialize to `16'hFFFF (65,535)` so even a max-contrast block (`16'hFF00 < 16'hFFFF`) triggers `newBest = 1`!

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (Two's-Complement Motion Vectors & Systolic Addressing)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 24 · Two's-Complement Motion Vectors] In our `[-8, +7]` search range, what are the 8-bit two's-complement hexadecimal values for `motionX = -8`, `motionX = -5`, and `motionY = +7`?
quiz_questions.hint: For a negative integer `-k` in 8-bit two's complement, compute `256 - k` and convert to hexadecimal (`256 - 8 = 248`, `256 - 5 = 251`).
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — `8'h88` and `8'h85` are sign-magnitude encodings, whereas Verilog arithmetic uses two's complement.
Incorrect — `8'h08` and `8'h05` are positive `+8` and `+5`, while `8'hF7` is `-9`.
Incorrect — `8'hFF` is `-1` and `8'hFA` is `-6`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In 8-bit two's complement (`256 + negative_offset`): `-8 -> 256 - 8 = 248 = 8'hF8`; `-5 -> 256 - 5 = 251 = 8'hFB`; `+7 -> 8'h07`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Systolic Pipeline Latency & Throughput Math)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 24 · Advanced Systolic Array Timing] Why does a full 256-candidate macroblock search across the 16-PE systolic array take exactly `4,111` clock cycles (`count == 13'h100F`), and what is the throughput in macroblocks/second at `520 MHz`?
options: A) 256 candidates * 256 pixels = 65,536 cycles (7,934 macroblocks/sec)

B) 16 vertical search rows * 256 cycles/row = 4,096 cycles + 15 Rpipe pipeline fill cycles for PE15 = 4,111 cycles (`7.906 us` per macroblock = `126,489 macroblocks/sec`, or `30.9 frames/sec` for 1024x1024 video!)
C) 16 PEs * 16 rows = 256 cycles
D) 4,095 cycles (`12'hFFF`)
quiz_questions.hint: Remember that all 16 horizontal candidates in a row are computed in parallel across `PE0..PE15` in 256 cycles, but `PE15` receives `R` delayed by 15 `Rpipe` stages!
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — `65,536` cycles would be a sequential 1-PE engine; our 16-PE systolic array achieves a 16x speedup!

Correct! `16 rows * 256 cycles/row = 4,096 cycles`, plus `15` cycles for `Rpipe[0..14]` to reach `PE15` = `4,111 cycles` (`13'h100F`). At `1.923 ns/cycle`, `4,111 * 1.923 ns = 7.906 us` (`126,489 macroblocks/s`).
Incorrect — Each candidate requires accumulating `16 * 16 = 256` pixels, not 16 pixels.
Incorrect — At cycle `4,095`, `PE15` still has 15 pixels left in the `Rpipe` shift register before completing its 256-pixel sum at cycle `4,111`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) `4,096 + 15 = 4,111` clock cycles (`13'h100F`). Dividing `520,000,000 Hz / 4,111 cycles = 126,489.9 macroblocks/sec`, which processes `4,096` macroblocks (a full `1024x1024` frame) at `30.88 fps`!

options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 25's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/rtl/8bit` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q1 & Q6 — Synthesizable Verilog Rules)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 25 · Verilog Synthesis Rules (Midterm Q1 & Q6)] Inside `pe.v` and `top.v`, why must sequential registers (`Accumulate`, `Rpipe`, `BestDist`, `count`) use non-blocking `<=` inside a single `always @(posedge clock)` block per signal?
options: A) Because `<=` means 'less than or equal to' in sequential blocks.

B) Because non-blocking `<=` samples all right-hand sides before the clock edge and updates left-hand registers in the NBA region (preventing shift-register race-through like in `Rpipe`), and keeping one `always` block per `reg` prevents multiple-driver short-circuit contention (`1'bX`).
C) Because blocking `=` cannot be simulated in VCS.
D) Because `<=` automatically inserts clock tree buffers.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall Midterm Q1 (what happens when two `always` blocks drive the same `reg`) and Midterm Q6 (what happens in a shift register `B = A; C = B;` if blocking `=` is used on a clock edge).
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Inside procedural assignment statements, `<=` is the non-blocking assignment operator, not a relational comparator.

Correct! Non-blocking `<=` prevents shift-register race-through across `Rpipe[0..14]`, and assigning each `reg` in a single `always` block satisfies the CMOS single-driver synthesis rule (Midterm Q1 & Q6).
Incorrect — VCS simulates blocking `=`, but using `=` inside `always @(posedge clock)` causes simulation-synthesis mismatches and shift-register collapse.
Incorrect — Clock tree buffers are inserted during physical Clock Tree Synthesis (`clock_opt`) in Fusion Compiler, not by Verilog syntax.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly matching Midterm Q1 (single driver per `reg`) and Midterm Q6 (non-blocking `<=` in shift-register rings), `<=` guarantees race-free synchronous DFF updates.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (V1 8-Bit Trap vs. V2 16-Bit Surgical RTL Fix)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 25 · V1->V2 RTL Upgrade] Which 4 exact architectural changes transform the failing V1 8-bit baseline (`rtl/8bit/top.v`) into the passing V2 16-bit design (`rtl/16bit/top.v`)?
options: A) (1) Widen `BestDist` & `Accumulate` from `[7:0]` to `[15:0]`; (2) Remove the 8-bit `if (AccumulateCarry) 8'hFF` clamp in `PE`; (3) Initialize `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF` on reset; (4) Add `else if (count == 13'h100f) Completed <= 1'b1;` hold in `control`.
B) Change the clock period from 10 ns to 20 ns.
C) Replace `RMEM` with a 32-bit floating-point multiplier.
D) Change `AddressR` from 8 bits to 16 bits.
quiz_questions.hint: Trace the two hardware bugs in V1: (1) Why did `Accumulate` saturate at `255` and fail `8'hFF < 8'hFF` in `comp.v`? (2) Why did `count` wrap around to `0` after cycle `4,111`?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Those exact 4 surgical edits resolve both the `8'hFF` Row-1 saturation bug and the cycle-4111 counter wrap-around bug while keeping the external memory ports 100% compatible.
Incorrect — Changing the clock period does not fix an 8-bit arithmetic overflow (`256 * 255 = 65,280 > 255`).
Incorrect — Motion estimation SAD uses integer absolute differences `|R - S|`, not floating-point multiplication.
Incorrect — `RMEM` holds `16x16 = 256` bytes, so `AddressR[7:0]` (`2^8 = 256`) is already the exact required address width.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Widening the SAD datapath to 16 bits (`[15:0]`), removing the 8-bit saturation clamp, initializing `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF`, and freezing `control.v` at `count == 13'h100F` fixes all functional bugs.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Comparator Strict Inequality `<` vs. Tie-Breaking)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 25 · Advanced Comparator Corner Case] Suppose every candidate in the search window has maximum contrast (`|R - S| = 255` for all 256 pixels, so `SAD = 65,280 = 16'hFF00`). Why did V1 (`BestDist` init `8'hFF`, `PE` clamp `8'hFF`) leave `motionX/Y = 8'hxx`, whereas V2 (`BestDist` init `16'hFFFF`, `PE` sum `16'hFF00`) deterministically latches `motionX = -8 (8'hF8), motionY = -8 (8'hF8)` on candidate 0?
options: A) Because in V1, `8'hFF < 8'hFF` is FALSE (`0`) on every single candidate so `newBest` never asserts; in V2, candidate 0's `16'hFF00 (65,280) < 16'hFFFF (65,535)` is TRUE (`1`), latching `(-8, -8)` and updating `BestDist` to `16'hFF00`!
B) Because V2 changes `<` to `>`.
C) Because candidate 0 has `SAD = 0`.
D) Because `16'hFF00` is negative.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the strict inequality `pe_sad < BestDist` on candidate 0 (`u = -8, v = -8`) when `pe_sad = 65,280 (16'hFF00)` and `BestDist` was initialized to `65,535 (16'hFFFF)`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Reserved sentinel `16'hFFFF (65,535)` is strictly greater than the maximum possible physical SAD `16'hFF00 (65,280)`, guaranteeing that candidate 0 (`-8, -8`) wins `16'hFF00 < 16'hFFFF` even in an all-saturated stress test!
Incorrect — Both V1 and V2 seek the MINIMUM distortion (`pe_sad < BestDist`), so `<` is preserved.
Incorrect — In the all-saturated stress test, every candidate has `SAD = 65,280 (16'hFF00)`.
Incorrect — `SAD` and `BestDist` are unsigned 16-bit magnitudes (`0..65,535`).
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Because `256 * 255 = 65,280 = 16'hFF00`, the values `16'hFF01..16'hFFFF` are unreachable by any real 16x16 pixel sum. Initializing `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF` guarantees that candidate 0 (`u=-8, v=-8`) satisfies `16'hFF00 < 16'hFFFF` (`newBest = 1`).

In V2 16-bit `pe.v`, `AccumulateIn = Accumulate + {8'b0, difference};` has zero saturation up to `65,280 (16'hFF00)`, and `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF` on `start == 0` guarantees `16'hFF00 < 16'hFFFF` succeeds.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 26 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 26's combined one-liner, why do we execute `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/rtl/8bit` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 26's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/rtl/8bit` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 26's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q1 & Q6 — Synthesizable Verilog Rules)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 26 · Verilog Synthesis Rules (Midterm Q1 & Q6)] Inside `pe.v` and `top.v`, why must sequential registers (`Accumulate`, `Rpipe`, `BestDist`, `count`) use non-blocking `<=` inside a single `always @(posedge clock)` block per signal?
options: A) Because `<=` means 'less than or equal to' in sequential blocks.

B) Because non-blocking `<=` samples all right-hand sides before the clock edge and updates left-hand registers in the NBA region (preventing shift-register race-through like in `Rpipe`), and keeping one `always` block per `reg` prevents multiple-driver short-circuit contention (`1'bX`).
C) Because blocking `=` cannot be simulated in VCS.
D) Because `<=` automatically inserts clock tree buffers.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall Midterm Q1 (what happens when two `always` blocks drive the same `reg`) and Midterm Q6 (what happens in a shift register `B = A; C = B;` if blocking `=` is used on a clock edge).
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Inside procedural assignment statements, `<=` is the non-blocking assignment operator, not a relational comparator.

Correct! Non-blocking `<=` prevents shift-register race-through across `Rpipe[0..14]`, and assigning each `reg` in a single `always` block satisfies the CMOS single-driver synthesis rule (Midterm Q1 & Q6).
Incorrect — VCS simulates blocking `=`, but using `=` inside `always @(posedge clock)` causes simulation-synthesis mismatches and shift-register collapse.
Incorrect — Clock tree buffers are inserted during physical Clock Tree Synthesis (`clock_opt`) in Fusion Compiler, not by Verilog syntax.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly matching Midterm Q1 (single driver per `reg`) and Midterm Q6 (non-blocking `<=` in shift-register rings), `<=` guarantees race-free synchronous DFF updates.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (V1 8-Bit Trap vs. V2 16-Bit Surgical RTL Fix)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 26 · V1->V2 RTL Upgrade] Which 4 exact architectural changes transform the failing V1 8-bit baseline (`rtl/8bit/top.v`) into the passing V2 16-bit design (`rtl/16bit/top.v`)?
options: A) (1) Widen `BestDist` & `Accumulate` from `[7:0]` to `[15:0]`; (2) Remove the 8-bit `if (AccumulateCarry) 8'hFF` clamp in `PE`; (3) Initialize `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF` on reset; (4) Add `else if (count == 13'h100f) Completed <= 1'b1;` hold in `control`.
B) Change the clock period from 10 ns to 20 ns.
C) Replace `RMEM` with a 32-bit floating-point multiplier.
D) Change `AddressR` from 8 bits to 16 bits.
quiz_questions.hint: Trace the two hardware bugs in V1: (1) Why did `Accumulate` saturate at `255` and fail `8'hFF < 8'hFF` in `comp.v`? (2) Why did `count` wrap around to `0` after cycle `4,111`?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Those exact 4 surgical edits resolve both the `8'hFF` Row-1 saturation bug and the cycle-4111 counter wrap-around bug while keeping the external memory ports 100% compatible.
Incorrect — Changing the clock period does not fix an 8-bit arithmetic overflow (`256 * 255 = 65,280 > 255`).
Incorrect — Motion estimation SAD uses integer absolute differences `|R - S|`, not floating-point multiplication.
Incorrect — `RMEM` holds `16x16 = 256` bytes, so `AddressR[7:0]` (`2^8 = 256`) is already the exact required address width.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Widening the SAD datapath to 16 bits (`[15:0]`), removing the 8-bit saturation clamp, initializing `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF`, and freezing `control.v` at `count == 13'h100F` fixes all functional bugs.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Comparator Strict Inequality `<` vs. Tie-Breaking)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 26 · Advanced Comparator Corner Case] Suppose every candidate in the search window has maximum contrast (`|R - S| = 255` for all 256 pixels, so `SAD = 65,280 = 16'hFF00`). Why did V1 (`BestDist` init `8'hFF`, `PE` clamp `8'hFF`) leave `motionX/Y = 8'hxx`, whereas V2 (`BestDist` init `16'hFFFF`, `PE` sum `16'hFF00`) deterministically latches `motionX = -8 (8'hF8), motionY = -8 (8'hF8)` on candidate 0?
options: A) Because in V1, `8'hFF < 8'hFF` is FALSE (`0`) on every single candidate so `newBest` never asserts; in V2, candidate 0's `16'hFF00 (65,280) < 16'hFFFF (65,535)` is TRUE (`1`), latching `(-8, -8)` and updating `BestDist` to `16'hFF00`!
B) Because V2 changes `<` to `>`.
C) Because candidate 0 has `SAD = 0`.
D) Because `16'hFF00` is negative.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the strict inequality `pe_sad < BestDist` on candidate 0 (`u = -8, v = -8`) when `pe_sad = 65,280 (16'hFF00)` and `BestDist` was initialized to `65,535 (16'hFFFF)`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Reserved sentinel `16'hFFFF (65,535)` is strictly greater than the maximum possible physical SAD `16'hFF00 (65,280)`, guaranteeing that candidate 0 (`-8, -8`) wins `16'hFF00 < 16'hFFFF` even in an all-saturated stress test!
Incorrect — Both V1 and V2 seek the MINIMUM distortion (`pe_sad < BestDist`), so `<` is preserved.
Incorrect — In the all-saturated stress test, every candidate has `SAD = 65,280 (16'hFF00)`.
Incorrect — `SAD` and `BestDist` are unsigned 16-bit magnitudes (`0..65,535`).
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Because `256 * 255 = 65,280 = 16'hFF00`, the values `16'hFF01..16'hFFFF` are unreachable by any real 16x16 pixel sum. Initializing `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF` guarantees that candidate 0 (`u=-8, v=-8`) satisfies `16'hFF00 < 16'hFFFF` (`newBest = 1`).

In V2 16-bit `pe.v`, `AccumulateIn = Accumulate + {8'b0, difference};` has zero saturation up to `65,280 (16'hFF00)`, and `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF` on `start == 0` guarantees `16'hFF00 < 16'hFFFF` succeeds.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 27 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 27's combined one-liner, why do we execute `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/rtl/8bit` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 27's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/rtl/8bit` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 27's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q1 & Q6 — Synthesizable Verilog Rules)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 27 · Verilog Synthesis Rules (Midterm Q1 & Q6)] Inside `pe.v` and `top.v`, why must sequential registers (`Accumulate`, `Rpipe`, `BestDist`, `count`) use non-blocking `<=` inside a single `always @(posedge clock)` block per signal?
options: A) Because `<=` means 'less than or equal to' in sequential blocks.

B) Because non-blocking `<=` samples all right-hand sides before the clock edge and updates left-hand registers in the NBA region (preventing shift-register race-through like in `Rpipe`), and keeping one `always` block per `reg` prevents multiple-driver short-circuit contention (`1'bX`).
C) Because blocking `=` cannot be simulated in VCS.
D) Because `<=` automatically inserts clock tree buffers.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall Midterm Q1 (what happens when two `always` blocks drive the same `reg`) and Midterm Q6 (what happens in a shift register `B = A; C = B;` if blocking `=` is used on a clock edge).
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Inside procedural assignment statements, `<=` is the non-blocking assignment operator, not a relational comparator.

Correct! Non-blocking `<=` prevents shift-register race-through across `Rpipe[0..14]`, and assigning each `reg` in a single `always` block satisfies the CMOS single-driver synthesis rule (Midterm Q1 & Q6).
Incorrect — VCS simulates blocking `=`, but using `=` inside `always @(posedge clock)` causes simulation-synthesis mismatches and shift-register collapse.
Incorrect — Clock tree buffers are inserted during physical Clock Tree Synthesis (`clock_opt`) in Fusion Compiler, not by Verilog syntax.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly matching Midterm Q1 (single driver per `reg`) and Midterm Q6 (non-blocking `<=` in shift-register rings), `<=` guarantees race-free synchronous DFF updates.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (V1 8-Bit Trap vs. V2 16-Bit Surgical RTL Fix)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 27 · V1->V2 RTL Upgrade] Which 4 exact architectural changes transform the failing V1 8-bit baseline (`rtl/8bit/top.v`) into the passing V2 16-bit design (`rtl/16bit/top.v`)?
options: A) (1) Widen `BestDist` & `Accumulate` from `[7:0]` to `[15:0]`; (2) Remove the 8-bit `if (AccumulateCarry) 8'hFF` clamp in `PE`; (3) Initialize `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF` on reset; (4) Add `else if (count == 13'h100f) Completed <= 1'b1;` hold in `control`.
B) Change the clock period from 10 ns to 20 ns.
C) Replace `RMEM` with a 32-bit floating-point multiplier.
D) Change `AddressR` from 8 bits to 16 bits.
quiz_questions.hint: Trace the two hardware bugs in V1: (1) Why did `Accumulate` saturate at `255` and fail `8'hFF < 8'hFF` in `comp.v`? (2) Why did `count` wrap around to `0` after cycle `4,111`?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Those exact 4 surgical edits resolve both the `8'hFF` Row-1 saturation bug and the cycle-4111 counter wrap-around bug while keeping the external memory ports 100% compatible.
Incorrect — Changing the clock period does not fix an 8-bit arithmetic overflow (`256 * 255 = 65,280 > 255`).
Incorrect — Motion estimation SAD uses integer absolute differences `|R - S|`, not floating-point multiplication.
Incorrect — `RMEM` holds `16x16 = 256` bytes, so `AddressR[7:0]` (`2^8 = 256`) is already the exact required address width.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Widening the SAD datapath to 16 bits (`[15:0]`), removing the 8-bit saturation clamp, initializing `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF`, and freezing `control.v` at `count == 13'h100F` fixes all functional bugs.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Comparator Strict Inequality `<` vs. Tie-Breaking)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 27 · Advanced Comparator Corner Case] Suppose every candidate in the search window has maximum contrast (`|R - S| = 255` for all 256 pixels, so `SAD = 65,280 = 16'hFF00`). Why did V1 (`BestDist` init `8'hFF`, `PE` clamp `8'hFF`) leave `motionX/Y = 8'hxx`, whereas V2 (`BestDist` init `16'hFFFF`, `PE` sum `16'hFF00`) deterministically latches `motionX = -8 (8'hF8), motionY = -8 (8'hF8)` on candidate 0?
options: A) Because in V1, `8'hFF < 8'hFF` is FALSE (`0`) on every single candidate so `newBest` never asserts; in V2, candidate 0's `16'hFF00 (65,280) < 16'hFFFF (65,535)` is TRUE (`1`), latching `(-8, -8)` and updating `BestDist` to `16'hFF00`!
B) Because V2 changes `<` to `>`.
C) Because candidate 0 has `SAD = 0`.
D) Because `16'hFF00` is negative.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the strict inequality `pe_sad < BestDist` on candidate 0 (`u = -8, v = -8`) when `pe_sad = 65,280 (16'hFF00)` and `BestDist` was initialized to `65,535 (16'hFFFF)`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Reserved sentinel `16'hFFFF (65,535)` is strictly greater than the maximum possible physical SAD `16'hFF00 (65,280)`, guaranteeing that candidate 0 (`-8, -8`) wins `16'hFF00 < 16'hFFFF` even in an all-saturated stress test!
Incorrect — Both V1 and V2 seek the MINIMUM distortion (`pe_sad < BestDist`), so `<` is preserved.
Incorrect — In the all-saturated stress test, every candidate has `SAD = 65,280 (16'hFF00)`.
Incorrect — `SAD` and `BestDist` are unsigned 16-bit magnitudes (`0..65,535`).
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Because `256 * 255 = 65,280 = 16'hFF00`, the values `16'hFF01..16'hFFFF` are unreachable by any real 16x16 pixel sum. Initializing `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF` guarantees that candidate 0 (`u=-8, v=-8`) satisfies `16'hFF00 < 16'hFFFF` (`newBest = 1`).

foundation_text: Chapters 3–5 Foundation Bridge (Page 28): Combinational logic (`always @(*)`) uses blocking assignments (`=`) with default values so every path assigns every output (preventing unintentional latches). Sequential registers (`always @(posedge clock)`) use non-blocking assignments (`<=`) so all 449 D flip-flops sample their inputs at the rising clock edge without race-through.

three_methods.method1: Behavior on Page 28 (Page 28: Baseline 8-Bit Saturating Verilog RTL  -  Lines 85..85 (rtl/8bit/top.v)): Compare V1 8-bit baseline (`rtl/8bit/top.v`, where `Accumulate[7:0]` clamps to `8'hFF`) against V2 16-bit upgraded RTL (`rtl/16bit/top.v`, where `Accumulate[15:0]` and `BestDist[15:0]` preserve full precision and `control.v` freezes at `count == 13'h100F`).
three_methods.method2: RTL Bug vs. Fix Proof: In V1 8-bit `pe.v`, `if (AccumulateCarry) AccumulateIn = 8'hFF;` destroys all SAD sums >= 255. In V2 16-bit `pe.v`, `AccumulateIn = Accumulate + {8'b0, difference};` has zero saturation up to `65,280 (16'hFF00)`, and `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF` on `start == 0` guarantees `16'hFF00 < 16'hFFFF` succeeds.
three_methods.method3: Synthesizable Hardware Structure: 16 PEs (`pe0..pe15`), 15 inter-PE pipeline registers (`Rpipe[0..14]`), 16-bit comparator (`comp.v`), and 13-bit cycle counter (`control.v` with `Completed` hold register at `13'h100F`).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 28 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 28's combined one-liner, why do we execute `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/rtl/8bit` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 28's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/rtl/8bit` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 28's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q1 & Q6 — Synthesizable Verilog Rules)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 28 · Verilog Synthesis Rules (Midterm Q1 & Q6)] Inside `pe.v` and `top.v`, why must sequential registers (`Accumulate`, `Rpipe`, `BestDist`, `count`) use non-blocking `<=` inside a single `always @(posedge clock)` block per signal?
options: A) Because `<=` means 'less than or equal to' in sequential blocks.

B) Because non-blocking `<=` samples all right-hand sides before the clock edge and updates left-hand registers in the NBA region (preventing shift-register race-through like in `Rpipe`), and keeping one `always` block per `reg` prevents multiple-driver short-circuit contention (`1'bX`).
C) Because blocking `=` cannot be simulated in VCS.
D) Because `<=` automatically inserts clock tree buffers.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall Midterm Q1 (what happens when two `always` blocks drive the same `reg`) and Midterm Q6 (what happens in a shift register `B = A; C = B;` if blocking `=` is used on a clock edge).
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Inside procedural assignment statements, `<=` is the non-blocking assignment operator, not a relational comparator.

Correct! Non-blocking `<=` prevents shift-register race-through across `Rpipe[0..14]`, and assigning each `reg` in a single `always` block satisfies the CMOS single-driver synthesis rule (Midterm Q1 & Q6).
Incorrect — VCS simulates blocking `=`, but using `=` inside `always @(posedge clock)` causes simulation-synthesis mismatches and shift-register collapse.
Incorrect — Clock tree buffers are inserted during physical Clock Tree Synthesis (`clock_opt`) in Fusion Compiler, not by Verilog syntax.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly matching Midterm Q1 (single driver per `reg`) and Midterm Q6 (non-blocking `<=` in shift-register rings), `<=` guarantees race-free synchronous DFF updates.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (V1 8-Bit Trap vs. V2 16-Bit Surgical RTL Fix)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 28 · V1->V2 RTL Upgrade] Which 4 exact architectural changes transform the failing V1 8-bit baseline (`rtl/8bit/top.v`) into the passing V2 16-bit design (`rtl/16bit/top.v`)?
options: A) (1) Widen `BestDist` & `Accumulate` from `[7:0]` to `[15:0]`; (2) Remove the 8-bit `if (AccumulateCarry) 8'hFF` clamp in `PE`; (3) Initialize `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF` on reset; (4) Add `else if (count == 13'h100f) Completed <= 1'b1;` hold in `control`.
B) Change the clock period from 10 ns to 20 ns.
C) Replace `RMEM` with a 32-bit floating-point multiplier.
D) Change `AddressR` from 8 bits to 16 bits.
quiz_questions.hint: Trace the two hardware bugs in V1: (1) Why did `Accumulate` saturate at `255` and fail `8'hFF < 8'hFF` in `comp.v`? (2) Why did `count` wrap around to `0` after cycle `4,111`?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Those exact 4 surgical edits resolve both the `8'hFF` Row-1 saturation bug and the cycle-4111 counter wrap-around bug while keeping the external memory ports 100% compatible.
Incorrect — Changing the clock period does not fix an 8-bit arithmetic overflow (`256 * 255 = 65,280 > 255`).
Incorrect — Motion estimation SAD uses integer absolute differences `|R - S|`, not floating-point multiplication.
Incorrect — `RMEM` holds `16x16 = 256` bytes, so `AddressR[7:0]` (`2^8 = 256`) is already the exact required address width.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Widening the SAD datapath to 16 bits (`[15:0]`), removing the 8-bit saturation clamp, initializing `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF`, and freezing `control.v` at `count == 13'h100F` fixes all functional bugs.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Comparator Strict Inequality `<` vs. Tie-Breaking)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 28 · Advanced Comparator Corner Case] Suppose every candidate in the search window has maximum contrast (`|R - S| = 255` for all 256 pixels, so `SAD = 65,280 = 16'hFF00`). Why did V1 (`BestDist` init `8'hFF`, `PE` clamp `8'hFF`) leave `motionX/Y = 8'hxx`, whereas V2 (`BestDist` init `16'hFFFF`, `PE` sum `16'hFF00`) deterministically latches `motionX = -8 (8'hF8), motionY = -8 (8'hF8)` on candidate 0?
options: A) Because in V1, `8'hFF < 8'hFF` is FALSE (`0`) on every single candidate so `newBest` never asserts; in V2, candidate 0's `16'hFF00 (65,280) < 16'hFFFF (65,535)` is TRUE (`1`), latching `(-8, -8)` and updating `BestDist` to `16'hFF00`!
B) Because V2 changes `<` to `>`.
C) Because candidate 0 has `SAD = 0`.
D) Because `16'hFF00` is negative.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the strict inequality `pe_sad < BestDist` on candidate 0 (`u = -8, v = -8`) when `pe_sad = 65,280 (16'hFF00)` and `BestDist` was initialized to `65,535 (16'hFFFF)`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Reserved sentinel `16'hFFFF (65,535)` is strictly greater than the maximum possible physical SAD `16'hFF00 (65,280)`, guaranteeing that candidate 0 (`-8, -8`) wins `16'hFF00 < 16'hFFFF` even in an all-saturated stress test!
Incorrect — Both V1 and V2 seek the MINIMUM distortion (`pe_sad < BestDist`), so `<` is preserved.
Incorrect — In the all-saturated stress test, every candidate has `SAD = 65,280 (16'hFF00)`.
Incorrect — `SAD` and `BestDist` are unsigned 16-bit magnitudes (`0..65,535`).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q1 & Q6 — Synthesizable Verilog Rules)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 29 · Verilog Synthesis Rules (Midterm Q1 & Q6)] Inside `pe.v` and `top.v`, why must sequential registers (`Accumulate`, `Rpipe`, `BestDist`, `count`) use non-blocking `<=` inside a single `always @(posedge clock)` block per signal?
options: A) Because `<=` means 'less than or equal to' in sequential blocks.

B) Because non-blocking `<=` samples all right-hand sides before the clock edge and updates left-hand registers in the NBA region (preventing shift-register race-through like in `Rpipe`), and keeping one `always` block per `reg` prevents multiple-driver short-circuit contention (`1'bX`).
C) Because blocking `=` cannot be simulated in VCS.
D) Because `<=` automatically inserts clock tree buffers.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall Midterm Q1 (what happens when two `always` blocks drive the same `reg`) and Midterm Q6 (what happens in a shift register `B = A; C = B;` if blocking `=` is used on a clock edge).
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Inside procedural assignment statements, `<=` is the non-blocking assignment operator, not a relational comparator.

Correct! Non-blocking `<=` prevents shift-register race-through across `Rpipe[0..14]`, and assigning each `reg` in a single `always` block satisfies the CMOS single-driver synthesis rule (Midterm Q1 & Q6).
Incorrect — VCS simulates blocking `=`, but using `=` inside `always @(posedge clock)` causes simulation-synthesis mismatches and shift-register collapse.
Incorrect — Clock tree buffers are inserted during physical Clock Tree Synthesis (`clock_opt`) in Fusion Compiler, not by Verilog syntax.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly matching Midterm Q1 (single driver per `reg`) and Midterm Q6 (non-blocking `<=` in shift-register rings), `<=` guarantees race-free synchronous DFF updates.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (V1 8-Bit Trap vs. V2 16-Bit Surgical RTL Fix)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 29 · V1->V2 RTL Upgrade] Which 4 exact architectural changes transform the failing V1 8-bit baseline (`rtl/8bit/top.v`) into the passing V2 16-bit design (`rtl/16bit/top.v`)?
options: A) (1) Widen `BestDist` & `Accumulate` from `[7:0]` to `[15:0]`; (2) Remove the 8-bit `if (AccumulateCarry) 8'hFF` clamp in `PE`; (3) Initialize `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF` on reset; (4) Add `else if (count == 13'h100f) Completed <= 1'b1;` hold in `control`.
B) Change the clock period from 10 ns to 20 ns.
C) Replace `RMEM` with a 32-bit floating-point multiplier.
D) Change `AddressR` from 8 bits to 16 bits.
quiz_questions.hint: Trace the two hardware bugs in V1: (1) Why did `Accumulate` saturate at `255` and fail `8'hFF < 8'hFF` in `comp.v`? (2) Why did `count` wrap around to `0` after cycle `4,111`?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Those exact 4 surgical edits resolve both the `8'hFF` Row-1 saturation bug and the cycle-4111 counter wrap-around bug while keeping the external memory ports 100% compatible.
Incorrect — Changing the clock period does not fix an 8-bit arithmetic overflow (`256 * 255 = 65,280 > 255`).
Incorrect — Motion estimation SAD uses integer absolute differences `|R - S|`, not floating-point multiplication.
Incorrect — `RMEM` holds `16x16 = 256` bytes, so `AddressR[7:0]` (`2^8 = 256`) is already the exact required address width.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Widening the SAD datapath to 16 bits (`[15:0]`), removing the 8-bit saturation clamp, initializing `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF`, and freezing `control.v` at `count == 13'h100F` fixes all functional bugs.

quiz_questions.q: [Page 29 · Advanced Comparator Corner Case] Suppose every candidate in the search window has maximum contrast (`|R - S| = 255` for all 256 pixels, so `SAD = 65,280 = 16'hFF00`). Why did V1 (`BestDist` init `8'hFF`, `PE` clamp `8'hFF`) leave `motionX/Y = 8'hxx`, whereas V2 (`BestDist` init `16'hFFFF`, `PE` sum `16'hFF00`) deterministically latches `motionX = -8 (8'hF8), motionY = -8 (8'hF8)` on candidate 0?
options: A) Because in V1, `8'hFF < 8'hFF` is FALSE (`0`) on every single candidate so `newBest` never asserts; in V2, candidate 0's `16'hFF00 (65,280) < 16'hFFFF (65,535)` is TRUE (`1`), latching `(-8, -8)` and updating `BestDist` to `16'hFF00`!
B) Because V2 changes `<` to `>`.
C) Because candidate 0 has `SAD = 0`.
D) Because `16'hFF00` is negative.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the strict inequality `pe_sad < BestDist` on candidate 0 (`u = -8, v = -8`) when `pe_sad = 65,280 (16'hFF00)` and `BestDist` was initialized to `65,535 (16'hFFFF)`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Reserved sentinel `16'hFFFF (65,535)` is strictly greater than the maximum possible physical SAD `16'hFF00 (65,280)`, guaranteeing that candidate 0 (`-8, -8`) wins `16'hFF00 < 16'hFFFF` even in an all-saturated stress test!
Incorrect — Both V1 and V2 seek the MINIMUM distortion (`pe_sad < BestDist`), so `<` is preserved.
Incorrect — In the all-saturated stress test, every candidate has `SAD = 65,280 (16'hFF00)`.
Incorrect — `SAD` and `BestDist` are unsigned 16-bit magnitudes (`0..65,535`).
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Because `256 * 255 = 65,280 = 16'hFF00`, the values `16'hFF01..16'hFFFF` are unreachable by any real 16x16 pixel sum. Initializing `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF` guarantees that candidate 0 (`u=-8, v=-8`) satisfies `16'hFF00 < 16'hFFFF` (`newBest = 1`).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q1 & Q6 — Synthesizable Verilog Rules)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 30 · Verilog Synthesis Rules (Midterm Q1 & Q6)] Inside `pe.v` and `top.v`, why must sequential registers (`Accumulate`, `Rpipe`, `BestDist`, `count`) use non-blocking `<=` inside a single `always @(posedge clock)` block per signal?
options: A) Because `<=` means 'less than or equal to' in sequential blocks.

B) Because non-blocking `<=` samples all right-hand sides before the clock edge and updates left-hand registers in the NBA region (preventing shift-register race-through like in `Rpipe`), and keeping one `always` block per `reg` prevents multiple-driver short-circuit contention (`1'bX`).
C) Because blocking `=` cannot be simulated in VCS.
D) Because `<=` automatically inserts clock tree buffers.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall Midterm Q1 (what happens when two `always` blocks drive the same `reg`) and Midterm Q6 (what happens in a shift register `B = A; C = B;` if blocking `=` is used on a clock edge).
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Inside procedural assignment statements, `<=` is the non-blocking assignment operator, not a relational comparator.

Correct! Non-blocking `<=` prevents shift-register race-through across `Rpipe[0..14]`, and assigning each `reg` in a single `always` block satisfies the CMOS single-driver synthesis rule (Midterm Q1 & Q6).
Incorrect — VCS simulates blocking `=`, but using `=` inside `always @(posedge clock)` causes simulation-synthesis mismatches and shift-register collapse.
Incorrect — Clock tree buffers are inserted during physical Clock Tree Synthesis (`clock_opt`) in Fusion Compiler, not by Verilog syntax.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly matching Midterm Q1 (single driver per `reg`) and Midterm Q6 (non-blocking `<=` in shift-register rings), `<=` guarantees race-free synchronous DFF updates.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (V1 8-Bit Trap vs. V2 16-Bit Surgical RTL Fix)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 30 · V1->V2 RTL Upgrade] Which 4 exact architectural changes transform the failing V1 8-bit baseline (`rtl/8bit/top.v`) into the passing V2 16-bit design (`rtl/16bit/top.v`)?
options: A) (1) Widen `BestDist` & `Accumulate` from `[7:0]` to `[15:0]`; (2) Remove the 8-bit `if (AccumulateCarry) 8'hFF` clamp in `PE`; (3) Initialize `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF` on reset; (4) Add `else if (count == 13'h100f) Completed <= 1'b1;` hold in `control`.
B) Change the clock period from 10 ns to 20 ns.
C) Replace `RMEM` with a 32-bit floating-point multiplier.
D) Change `AddressR` from 8 bits to 16 bits.
quiz_questions.hint: Trace the two hardware bugs in V1: (1) Why did `Accumulate` saturate at `255` and fail `8'hFF < 8'hFF` in `comp.v`? (2) Why did `count` wrap around to `0` after cycle `4,111`?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Those exact 4 surgical edits resolve both the `8'hFF` Row-1 saturation bug and the cycle-4111 counter wrap-around bug while keeping the external memory ports 100% compatible.
Incorrect — Changing the clock period does not fix an 8-bit arithmetic overflow (`256 * 255 = 65,280 > 255`).
Incorrect — Motion estimation SAD uses integer absolute differences `|R - S|`, not floating-point multiplication.
Incorrect — `RMEM` holds `16x16 = 256` bytes, so `AddressR[7:0]` (`2^8 = 256`) is already the exact required address width.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Widening the SAD datapath to 16 bits (`[15:0]`), removing the 8-bit saturation clamp, initializing `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF`, and freezing `control.v` at `count == 13'h100F` fixes all functional bugs.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Comparator Strict Inequality `<` vs. Tie-Breaking)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 30 · Advanced Comparator Corner Case] Suppose every candidate in the search window has maximum contrast (`|R - S| = 255` for all 256 pixels, so `SAD = 65,280 = 16'hFF00`). Why did V1 (`BestDist` init `8'hFF`, `PE` clamp `8'hFF`) leave `motionX/Y = 8'hxx`, whereas V2 (`BestDist` init `16'hFFFF`, `PE` sum `16'hFF00`) deterministically latches `motionX = -8 (8'hF8), motionY = -8 (8'hF8)` on candidate 0?
options: A) Because in V1, `8'hFF < 8'hFF` is FALSE (`0`) on every single candidate so `newBest` never asserts; in V2, candidate 0's `16'hFF00 (65,280) < 16'hFFFF (65,535)` is TRUE (`1`), latching `(-8, -8)` and updating `BestDist` to `16'hFF00`!
B) Because V2 changes `<` to `>`.
C) Because candidate 0 has `SAD = 0`.
D) Because `16'hFF00` is negative.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the strict inequality `pe_sad < BestDist` on candidate 0 (`u = -8, v = -8`) when `pe_sad = 65,280 (16'hFF00)` and `BestDist` was initialized to `65,535 (16'hFFFF)`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Reserved sentinel `16'hFFFF (65,535)` is strictly greater than the maximum possible physical SAD `16'hFF00 (65,280)`, guaranteeing that candidate 0 (`-8, -8`) wins `16'hFF00 < 16'hFFFF` even in an all-saturated stress test!
Incorrect — Both V1 and V2 seek the MINIMUM distortion (`pe_sad < BestDist`), so `<` is preserved.
Incorrect — In the all-saturated stress test, every candidate has `SAD = 65,280 (16'hFF00)`.
Incorrect — `SAD` and `BestDist` are unsigned 16-bit magnitudes (`0..65,535`).
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Because `256 * 255 = 65,280 = 16'hFF00`, the values `16'hFF01..16'hFFFF` are unreachable by any real 16x16 pixel sum. Initializing `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF` guarantees that candidate 0 (`u=-8, v=-8`) satisfies `16'hFF00 < 16'hFFFF` (`newBest = 1`).

Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 31's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/rtl/16bit` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 31's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q1 & Q6 — Synthesizable Verilog Rules)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 31 · Verilog Synthesis Rules (Midterm Q1 & Q6)] Inside `pe.v` and `top.v`, why must sequential registers (`Accumulate`, `Rpipe`, `BestDist`, `count`) use non-blocking `<=` inside a single `always @(posedge clock)` block per signal?
options: A) Because `<=` means 'less than or equal to' in sequential blocks.

B) Because non-blocking `<=` samples all right-hand sides before the clock edge and updates left-hand registers in the NBA region (preventing shift-register race-through like in `Rpipe`), and keeping one `always` block per `reg` prevents multiple-driver short-circuit contention (`1'bX`).
C) Because blocking `=` cannot be simulated in VCS.
D) Because `<=` automatically inserts clock tree buffers.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall Midterm Q1 (what happens when two `always` blocks drive the same `reg`) and Midterm Q6 (what happens in a shift register `B = A; C = B;` if blocking `=` is used on a clock edge).
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Inside procedural assignment statements, `<=` is the non-blocking assignment operator, not a relational comparator.

Correct! Non-blocking `<=` prevents shift-register race-through across `Rpipe[0..14]`, and assigning each `reg` in a single `always` block satisfies the CMOS single-driver synthesis rule (Midterm Q1 & Q6).
Incorrect — VCS simulates blocking `=`, but using `=` inside `always @(posedge clock)` causes simulation-synthesis mismatches and shift-register collapse.
Incorrect — Clock tree buffers are inserted during physical Clock Tree Synthesis (`clock_opt`) in Fusion Compiler, not by Verilog syntax.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly matching Midterm Q1 (single driver per `reg`) and Midterm Q6 (non-blocking `<=` in shift-register rings), `<=` guarantees race-free synchronous DFF updates.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (V1 8-Bit Trap vs. V2 16-Bit Surgical RTL Fix)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 31 · V1->V2 RTL Upgrade] Which 4 exact architectural changes transform the failing V1 8-bit baseline (`rtl/8bit/top.v`) into the passing V2 16-bit design (`rtl/16bit/top.v`)?
options: A) (1) Widen `BestDist` & `Accumulate` from `[7:0]` to `[15:0]`; (2) Remove the 8-bit `if (AccumulateCarry) 8'hFF` clamp in `PE`; (3) Initialize `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF` on reset; (4) Add `else if (count == 13'h100f) Completed <= 1'b1;` hold in `control`.
B) Change the clock period from 10 ns to 20 ns.
C) Replace `RMEM` with a 32-bit floating-point multiplier.
D) Change `AddressR` from 8 bits to 16 bits.
quiz_questions.hint: Trace the two hardware bugs in V1: (1) Why did `Accumulate` saturate at `255` and fail `8'hFF < 8'hFF` in `comp.v`? (2) Why did `count` wrap around to `0` after cycle `4,111`?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Those exact 4 surgical edits resolve both the `8'hFF` Row-1 saturation bug and the cycle-4111 counter wrap-around bug while keeping the external memory ports 100% compatible.
Incorrect — Changing the clock period does not fix an 8-bit arithmetic overflow (`256 * 255 = 65,280 > 255`).
Incorrect — Motion estimation SAD uses integer absolute differences `|R - S|`, not floating-point multiplication.
Incorrect — `RMEM` holds `16x16 = 256` bytes, so `AddressR[7:0]` (`2^8 = 256`) is already the exact required address width.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Widening the SAD datapath to 16 bits (`[15:0]`), removing the 8-bit saturation clamp, initializing `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF`, and freezing `control.v` at `count == 13'h100F` fixes all functional bugs.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Comparator Strict Inequality `<` vs. Tie-Breaking)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 31 · Advanced Comparator Corner Case] Suppose every candidate in the search window has maximum contrast (`|R - S| = 255` for all 256 pixels, so `SAD = 65,280 = 16'hFF00`). Why did V1 (`BestDist` init `8'hFF`, `PE` clamp `8'hFF`) leave `motionX/Y = 8'hxx`, whereas V2 (`BestDist` init `16'hFFFF`, `PE` sum `16'hFF00`) deterministically latches `motionX = -8 (8'hF8), motionY = -8 (8'hF8)` on candidate 0?
options: A) Because in V1, `8'hFF < 8'hFF` is FALSE (`0`) on every single candidate so `newBest` never asserts; in V2, candidate 0's `16'hFF00 (65,280) < 16'hFFFF (65,535)` is TRUE (`1`), latching `(-8, -8)` and updating `BestDist` to `16'hFF00`!
B) Because V2 changes `<` to `>`.
C) Because candidate 0 has `SAD = 0`.
D) Because `16'hFF00` is negative.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the strict inequality `pe_sad < BestDist` on candidate 0 (`u = -8, v = -8`) when `pe_sad = 65,280 (16'hFF00)` and `BestDist` was initialized to `65,535 (16'hFFFF)`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Reserved sentinel `16'hFFFF (65,535)` is strictly greater than the maximum possible physical SAD `16'hFF00 (65,280)`, guaranteeing that candidate 0 (`-8, -8`) wins `16'hFF00 < 16'hFFFF` even in an all-saturated stress test!
Incorrect — Both V1 and V2 seek the MINIMUM distortion (`pe_sad < BestDist`), so `<` is preserved.
Incorrect — In the all-saturated stress test, every candidate has `SAD = 65,280 (16'hFF00)`.
Incorrect — `SAD` and `BestDist` are unsigned 16-bit magnitudes (`0..65,535`).
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Because `256 * 255 = 65,280 = 16'hFF00`, the values `16'hFF01..16'hFFFF` are unreachable by any real 16x16 pixel sum. Initializing `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF` guarantees that candidate 0 (`u=-8, v=-8`) satisfies `16'hFF00 < 16'hFFFF` (`newBest = 1`).

options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 32's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/rtl/16bit ~/me_asic_new_v1/common/` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 32's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q1 & Q6 — Synthesizable Verilog Rules)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 32 · Verilog Synthesis Rules (Midterm Q1 & Q6)] Inside `pe.v` and `top.v`, why must sequential registers (`Accumulate`, `Rpipe`, `BestDist`, `count`) use non-blocking `<=` inside a single `always @(posedge clock)` block per signal?
options: A) Because `<=` means 'less than or equal to' in sequential blocks.

B) Because non-blocking `<=` samples all right-hand sides before the clock edge and updates left-hand registers in the NBA region (preventing shift-register race-through like in `Rpipe`), and keeping one `always` block per `reg` prevents multiple-driver short-circuit contention (`1'bX`).
C) Because blocking `=` cannot be simulated in VCS.
D) Because `<=` automatically inserts clock tree buffers.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall Midterm Q1 (what happens when two `always` blocks drive the same `reg`) and Midterm Q6 (what happens in a shift register `B = A; C = B;` if blocking `=` is used on a clock edge).
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Inside procedural assignment statements, `<=` is the non-blocking assignment operator, not a relational comparator.

Correct! Non-blocking `<=` prevents shift-register race-through across `Rpipe[0..14]`, and assigning each `reg` in a single `always` block satisfies the CMOS single-driver synthesis rule (Midterm Q1 & Q6).
Incorrect — VCS simulates blocking `=`, but using `=` inside `always @(posedge clock)` causes simulation-synthesis mismatches and shift-register collapse.
Incorrect — Clock tree buffers are inserted during physical Clock Tree Synthesis (`clock_opt`) in Fusion Compiler, not by Verilog syntax.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly matching Midterm Q1 (single driver per `reg`) and Midterm Q6 (non-blocking `<=` in shift-register rings), `<=` guarantees race-free synchronous DFF updates.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (V1 8-Bit Trap vs. V2 16-Bit Surgical RTL Fix)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 32 · V1->V2 RTL Upgrade] Which 4 exact architectural changes transform the failing V1 8-bit baseline (`rtl/8bit/top.v`) into the passing V2 16-bit design (`rtl/16bit/top.v`)?
options: A) (1) Widen `BestDist` & `Accumulate` from `[7:0]` to `[15:0]`; (2) Remove the 8-bit `if (AccumulateCarry) 8'hFF` clamp in `PE`; (3) Initialize `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF` on reset; (4) Add `else if (count == 13'h100f) Completed <= 1'b1;` hold in `control`.
B) Change the clock period from 10 ns to 20 ns.
C) Replace `RMEM` with a 32-bit floating-point multiplier.
D) Change `AddressR` from 8 bits to 16 bits.
quiz_questions.hint: Trace the two hardware bugs in V1: (1) Why did `Accumulate` saturate at `255` and fail `8'hFF < 8'hFF` in `comp.v`? (2) Why did `count` wrap around to `0` after cycle `4,111`?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Those exact 4 surgical edits resolve both the `8'hFF` Row-1 saturation bug and the cycle-4111 counter wrap-around bug while keeping the external memory ports 100% compatible.
Incorrect — Changing the clock period does not fix an 8-bit arithmetic overflow (`256 * 255 = 65,280 > 255`).
Incorrect — Motion estimation SAD uses integer absolute differences `|R - S|`, not floating-point multiplication.
Incorrect — `RMEM` holds `16x16 = 256` bytes, so `AddressR[7:0]` (`2^8 = 256`) is already the exact required address width.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Widening the SAD datapath to 16 bits (`[15:0]`), removing the 8-bit saturation clamp, initializing `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF`, and freezing `control.v` at `count == 13'h100F` fixes all functional bugs.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Comparator Strict Inequality `<` vs. Tie-Breaking)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 32 · Advanced Comparator Corner Case] Suppose every candidate in the search window has maximum contrast (`|R - S| = 255` for all 256 pixels, so `SAD = 65,280 = 16'hFF00`). Why did V1 (`BestDist` init `8'hFF`, `PE` clamp `8'hFF`) leave `motionX/Y = 8'hxx`, whereas V2 (`BestDist` init `16'hFFFF`, `PE` sum `16'hFF00`) deterministically latches `motionX = -8 (8'hF8), motionY = -8 (8'hF8)` on candidate 0?
options: A) Because in V1, `8'hFF < 8'hFF` is FALSE (`0`) on every single candidate so `newBest` never asserts; in V2, candidate 0's `16'hFF00 (65,280) < 16'hFFFF (65,535)` is TRUE (`1`), latching `(-8, -8)` and updating `BestDist` to `16'hFF00`!
B) Because V2 changes `<` to `>`.
C) Because candidate 0 has `SAD = 0`.
D) Because `16'hFF00` is negative.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the strict inequality `pe_sad < BestDist` on candidate 0 (`u = -8, v = -8`) when `pe_sad = 65,280 (16'hFF00)` and `BestDist` was initialized to `65,535 (16'hFFFF)`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Reserved sentinel `16'hFFFF (65,535)` is strictly greater than the maximum possible physical SAD `16'hFF00 (65,280)`, guaranteeing that candidate 0 (`-8, -8`) wins `16'hFF00 < 16'hFFFF` even in an all-saturated stress test!
Incorrect — Both V1 and V2 seek the MINIMUM distortion (`pe_sad < BestDist`), so `<` is preserved.
Incorrect — In the all-saturated stress test, every candidate has `SAD = 65,280 (16'hFF00)`.
Incorrect — `SAD` and `BestDist` are unsigned 16-bit magnitudes (`0..65,535`).
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Because `256 * 255 = 65,280 = 16'hFF00`, the values `16'hFF01..16'hFFFF` are unreachable by any real 16x16 pixel sum. Initializing `BestDist <= 16'hFFFF` guarantees that candidate 0 (`u=-8, v=-8`) satisfies `16'hFF00 < 16'hFFFF` (`newBest = 1`).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 33 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 33's combined one-liner, why do we execute `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/tb/16bit` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 33's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/tb/16bit` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 33's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (520 MHz Testbench Clock Generation — F1)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 33 · 520 MHz Testbench Clock Generation] In `top_tb.v` with `` `timescale 1ns/10ps ``, how is a 520 MHz clock (`T_clk = 1.923 ns`) generated in Verilog?
options: A) `always #1.923 clock = ~clock;`
B) `always #0.9615 clock = ~clock;` (since a full clock period has two half-cycles: `2 * 0.9615 ns = 1.923 ns = 1 / 520 MHz`).
C) `always #520 clock = ~clock;`
D) `assign clock = 1'b1;`
quiz_questions.hint: Remember that `clock = ~clock` only flips the signal once (either `0->1` or `1->0`). How many inversions make 1 full clock period `T_clk = 1.923 ns`?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Delaying `#1.923` per half-cycle makes the full period `2 * 1.923 = 3.846 ns` (`260 MHz`, half the required frequency!).
Correct! Two half-periods of `0.9615 ns` equal one full period of `1.923 ns` (`1 / 1.923 ns = 520.02 MHz`).
Incorrect — `#520` under `1ns` timescale waits `520 ns` per half-cycle (`T_clk = 1,040 ns = 0.96 MHz`).
Incorrect — Holding `clock = 1'b1` produces zero rising edges, so no sequential logic ever advances.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) `clock = ~clock` inverts the clock twice per period (rising edge + falling edge). Half of `1.923 ns` is `0.9615 ns`, so `always #0.9615 clock = ~clock;` produces `T_clk = 1.923 ns (520 MHz)`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (Verdi nWave Waveform Forensics — Fig 7 vs. Fig 9)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 33 · Verdi nWave Waveform Analysis] In Figure 7 (`V9_fig7_orig8bit_row1_nWave.png`, 8-bit baseline) vs. Figure 9 (`V9_fig9_16bit_saturation_row1_nWave.png`, 16-bit upgrade) at `count = 13'h0100` (end of candidate 0), what happens to `BestDist` and `newBest` under max-contrast input?
options: A) In 8-bit (Fig 7), `pe0.Accumulate = 8'hFF` is NOT `< BestDist (8'hFF)` so `newBest = 0`; in 16-bit (Fig 9), `pe0.Accumulate = 16'hFF00 (65,280) < BestDist (16'hFFFF = 65,535)` so `newBest = 1` and `BestDist` updates to `16'hFF00`!
B) Both 8-bit and 16-bit output `BestDist = 0`.
C) 8-bit updates `BestDist` to `8'h00`.
D) `newBest` is only used during synthesis.
quiz_questions.hint: Inspect the comparator equation `newBest = (pe_sad < BestDist)` at `count = 13'h0100` (`t = 499.0 ns`) when `pe0` finishes its 256th pixel.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! That exact cycle at `count = 13'h0100` is the visual smoking gun comparing V1 (8-bit fail, `8'hFF < 8'hFF` is false) and V2–V9 (16-bit pass, `16'hFF00 < 16'hFFFF` is true).
Incorrect — Under max-contrast input (`|R-S| = 255`), the distortion is maximal (`65,280 = 16'hFF00`), not zero.
Incorrect — The 8-bit PE saturates at `8'hFF` (`if (AccumulateCarry) AccumulateIn = 8'hFF;`) rather than wrapping to `8'h00`.
Incorrect — `newBest` is the active-high enable signal inside `comp.v` that latches `BestDist`, `motionX`, and `motionY` during simulation and hardware operation.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In V1 (Fig 7), `8'hFF < 8'hFF` evaluates to `0`, leaving `motionX/Y = xx`. In V2 (Fig 9), `16'hFF00 < 16'hFFFF` evaluates to `1`, latching `BestDist = 16'hFF00` and `(motionX, motionY) = (-8, -8)`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (+1 LSB Surgical Boundary Test `16'h0100`)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 33 · Surgical Testbench Design] Why did we design Testbench #2 (`top_tb.v`) so that the winning candidate at `(-5, +7)` has every pixel perturbed by exactly `+1` LSB (`|R - S| = 1` across all 256 pixels, yielding `BestDist = 16'h0100 = 256`), while all other candidates differ by `>= 2` LSBs?
options: A) Because `256 (16'h0100)` is the exact mathematical boundary (`255 + 1`) where an 8-bit unsigned accumulator overflows/saturates to `8'hFF (255)`! Thus `BestDist == 16'h0100` with `(motionX, motionY) == (8'hFB, 8'h07)` simultaneously proves bit-8 (`Accumulate[8]`) carry propagation and signed coordinate decoding.
B) Because `+1` LSB makes simulation run 10x faster.
C) Because `16'h0100` equals `100` in decimal.
D) Because `RMEM` can only store `+1`.
quiz_questions.hint: Convert hexadecimal `16'h0100` to decimal (`1 * 16^2 = 256`) and compare `256` against the maximum value of an 8-bit unsigned integer (`255`).
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `256 = 16'h0100` is the very first integer (`255 + 1`) that requires bit 8 (`2^8`) of the 16-bit accumulator, making it the sharpest possible boundary test between 8-bit (`0xFF`) and 16-bit (`0x0100`) precision!
Incorrect — Simulation runtime depends on the number of clock cycles (`4,111`), not the numeric pixel values in `SMEM`.
Incorrect — `16'h0100` in hexadecimal is `1 * 256 = 256` in decimal (not `100`).
Incorrect — `RMEM` stores arbitrary 8-bit grayscale intensities `0x00..0xFF`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) `256 pixels * 1 LSB/pixel = 256_10 = 16'h0100`. In V1 (8-bit), `256` clamped to `255 (8'hFF)`. Observing `BestDist = 16'h0100`, `motionX = 8'hFB (-5)`, `motionY = 8'h07 (+7)` proves bit-accurate 9th-bit carry into the upper byte `[15:8]`.
