quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 58 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 58's combined one-liner, why do we execute `nl -ba ~/ENGR852_Project/16_v3b_final_asic_fc/scripts/create_pg_networ` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Inspects, audits, and verifies generated RTL, memory files (`ref.txt`, `search.txt`), or EDA tool reports. Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 58's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `nl -ba ~/ENGR852_Project/16_v3b_final_asic_fc/scripts/create` performs: Inspects, audits, and verifies generated RTL, memory files (`ref.txt`, `search.txt`), or EDA tool reports. And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 58's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q3/Q4/Q9 — Setup Slack & F_max Math)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 58 · STA Setup & Hold Equations] Our 14nm Motion Estimator achieves Setup WNS = `+0.22 ns` in the worst-case slow corner (`ss0p72vm40c`) at `T_clk = 1.923 ns` (520 MHz). What is the longest critical-path total arrival + setup + uncertainty time in `ss0p72vm40c`, and what is the maximum achievable clock frequency?
options: A) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns - 0.22 ns = 1.703 ns`; max frequency `f_max = 1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`.
B) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns + 0.22 ns = 2.143 ns`; max frequency = `466 MHz`.
C) Critical path total time = `0.22 ns`; max frequency = `4.5 GHz`.
D) Setup WNS does not affect maximum frequency.
quiz_questions.hint: Use the fundamental Setup Slack identity: `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total`. Solve for `T_path_total = T_clk - Slack_setup`, then compute `f_max = 1 / T_path_total`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Positive slack `+0.22 ns` means the critical path finished `0.22 ns` BEFORE the `1.923 ns` deadline (`1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`), allowing operation up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`!
Incorrect — Adding `+0.22 ns` corresponds to a NEGATIVE slack violation (`-0.22 ns`), whereas our slack is positive (`+0.22 ns`).
Incorrect — `0.22 ns` is the spare timing margin (slack), not the path delay.
Incorrect — Setup WNS directly determines the minimum safe clock period `T_clk,min` and therefore `f_max`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Since `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total = +0.22 ns`, the critical path takes `1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`, meaning the routed 14nm chip can run up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz` even in the slowest `0.72V SS` corner!

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (14nm Physical DRC Closure & M7 Clock Routing Rule)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 58 · 14nm Physical DRC & CTS Closure] Why did constraining Clock Tree Synthesis to metal layers `M2..M7` (`set_clock_routing_rules -net_type root -max_routing_layer M7`) eliminate the upper-metal DRC violations in standalone Synopsys IC Validator (`icv`)?
options: A) Because `M8` and `M9` are thick top-level power/global layers with wide minimum-spacing and fat-wire rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`); keeping high-fanout clock tree branches on `M2..M7` avoids wide-metal stub spacing conflicts and achieves `0 / 242` DRC errors.
B) Because `M7` has zero electrical resistance.
C) Because `icv` only checks `M1`.
D) Because `M8` is made of polysilicon.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the physical pitch and spacing rules of intermediate signal routing layers (`M2..M7`) versus top-level thick power/global distribution layers (`M8, M9`) in a 14nm FinFET BEOL stack.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In `SAED14nm`, `M8/M9` carry the PG mesh straps and enforce wide-metal spacing rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`). Restricting CTS to `M2..M7` eliminates all upper-metal stub conflicts (`0 / 242` DRC violations).
Incorrect — All copper metal layers have finite sheet resistance `R_s`.
Incorrect — Standalone `icv` evaluates all 242 foundry deck rules across FEOL (FinFET active/gate) and BEOL (`M1..M9` and vias).
Incorrect — `M8` is an upper back-end-of-line (BEOL) copper interconnect layer, not front-end polysilicon.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Routing clock nets up to `M7` leaves `M8/M9` clean for power/top routing and resolves all 242 SAED14nm deck rules with `0` violations.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Midterm Q3/Q5/Q10 — Same-Edge Hold Physics Across PVT Corners)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 58 · Advanced Multi-Corner STA Physics] Suppose a classmate sees a Hold violation (`Hold WNS = -0.08 ns`) in PrimeTime at the `ff0p88v125c` (Fast-Fast `0.88V`) corner and proposes lowering the clock frequency from `520 MHz` (`1.923 ns`) down to `250 MHz` (`4.000 ns`) to fix it. Based on Midterm Q3 & Q10, will lowering `f_clk` fix the hold violation, and what is the true physical fix?
options: A) Yes, doubling the clock period adds `+2.077 ns` to Hold Slack.

B) No! Hold is checked on the SAME rising clock edge (`Slack_hold = [t_CQ,min + t_logic,min] - [t_hold,max + t_skew]`), which does NOT contain `T_clk`! Lowering frequency has zero effect on hold slack; the true fix is inserting non-inverting delay buffers (`set_fix_hold`) on the short contamination path to increase `t_logic,min` by >= `0.08 ns`.
C) Yes, because hold violations only happen above 500 MHz.
D) No, the only fix is deleting the flip-flop.
quiz_questions.hint: Write down the Hold Slack equation from Midterm Q3 / Q5 / Q10: does the clock period `T_clk` appear anywhere in `(t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)`?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Adding `+2.077 ns` to `T_clk` increases SETUP slack by `+2.077 ns`, but changes HOLD slack by `0.000 ns`!

Correct! Because Hold checks that a launching DFF does not overwrite a capturing DFF on the SAME clock edge (`t = 0`), `T_clk` cancels out completely. Only adding minimum path delay (delay buffers via `set_fix_hold`) or reducing clock skew fixes a hold violation!
Incorrect — Even a `1 Hz` (`T_clk = 1 second`) clock will fail Hold if `t_CQ,min + t_logic,min < t_hold + t_skew` on the active clock edge!
Incorrect — Deleting pipeline flip-flops breaks the synchronous systolic architecture.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly proven in Midterm Q3, Q5, and Q10: `Slack_hold = (t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)` is independent of `T_clk`. In Fusion Compiler / PrimeTime, `set_fix_hold` inserts small delay cells along fast paths (such as direct `Rpipe` shift wires) so `Slack_hold >= 0.00 ns` across all 3 corners.

quiz_questions.q: [Page 59 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 59's combined one-liner, why do we execute `cp ~/ENGR852_Project/20_v5b_520MHz_14nm_cts_area_fix/reports/clock_opt` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Executes Synopsys Fusion Compiler (`fc_shell`) for 520 MHz 14nm FinFET synthesis, floorplanning, CTS (`M7`), and detail routing. Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 59's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `cp ~/ENGR852_Project/20_v5b_520MHz_14nm_cts_area_fix/reports` performs: Executes Synopsys Fusion Compiler (`fc_shell`) for 520 MHz 14nm FinFET synthesis, floorplanning, CTS (`M7`), and detail routing. And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 59's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q3/Q4/Q9 — Setup Slack & F_max Math)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 59 · STA Setup & Hold Equations] Our 14nm Motion Estimator achieves Setup WNS = `+0.22 ns` in the worst-case slow corner (`ss0p72vm40c`) at `T_clk = 1.923 ns` (520 MHz). What is the longest critical-path total arrival + setup + uncertainty time in `ss0p72vm40c`, and what is the maximum achievable clock frequency?
options: A) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns - 0.22 ns = 1.703 ns`; max frequency `f_max = 1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`.
B) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns + 0.22 ns = 2.143 ns`; max frequency = `466 MHz`.
C) Critical path total time = `0.22 ns`; max frequency = `4.5 GHz`.
D) Setup WNS does not affect maximum frequency.
quiz_questions.hint: Use the fundamental Setup Slack identity: `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total`. Solve for `T_path_total = T_clk - Slack_setup`, then compute `f_max = 1 / T_path_total`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Positive slack `+0.22 ns` means the critical path finished `0.22 ns` BEFORE the `1.923 ns` deadline (`1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`), allowing operation up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`!
Incorrect — Adding `+0.22 ns` corresponds to a NEGATIVE slack violation (`-0.22 ns`), whereas our slack is positive (`+0.22 ns`).
Incorrect — `0.22 ns` is the spare timing margin (slack), not the path delay.
Incorrect — Setup WNS directly determines the minimum safe clock period `T_clk,min` and therefore `f_max`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Since `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total = +0.22 ns`, the critical path takes `1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`, meaning the routed 14nm chip can run up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz` even in the slowest `0.72V SS` corner!

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (14nm Physical DRC Closure & M7 Clock Routing Rule)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 59 · 14nm Physical DRC & CTS Closure] Why did constraining Clock Tree Synthesis to metal layers `M2..M7` (`set_clock_routing_rules -net_type root -max_routing_layer M7`) eliminate the upper-metal DRC violations in standalone Synopsys IC Validator (`icv`)?
options: A) Because `M8` and `M9` are thick top-level power/global layers with wide minimum-spacing and fat-wire rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`); keeping high-fanout clock tree branches on `M2..M7` avoids wide-metal stub spacing conflicts and achieves `0 / 242` DRC errors.
B) Because `M7` has zero electrical resistance.
C) Because `icv` only checks `M1`.
D) Because `M8` is made of polysilicon.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the physical pitch and spacing rules of intermediate signal routing layers (`M2..M7`) versus top-level thick power/global distribution layers (`M8, M9`) in a 14nm FinFET BEOL stack.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In `SAED14nm`, `M8/M9` carry the PG mesh straps and enforce wide-metal spacing rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`). Restricting CTS to `M2..M7` eliminates all upper-metal stub conflicts (`0 / 242` DRC violations).
Incorrect — All copper metal layers have finite sheet resistance `R_s`.
Incorrect — Standalone `icv` evaluates all 242 foundry deck rules across FEOL (FinFET active/gate) and BEOL (`M1..M9` and vias).
Incorrect — `M8` is an upper back-end-of-line (BEOL) copper interconnect layer, not front-end polysilicon.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Routing clock nets up to `M7` leaves `M8/M9` clean for power/top routing and resolves all 242 SAED14nm deck rules with `0` violations.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Midterm Q3/Q5/Q10 — Same-Edge Hold Physics Across PVT Corners)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 59 · Advanced Multi-Corner STA Physics] Suppose a classmate sees a Hold violation (`Hold WNS = -0.08 ns`) in PrimeTime at the `ff0p88v125c` (Fast-Fast `0.88V`) corner and proposes lowering the clock frequency from `520 MHz` (`1.923 ns`) down to `250 MHz` (`4.000 ns`) to fix it. Based on Midterm Q3 & Q10, will lowering `f_clk` fix the hold violation, and what is the true physical fix?
options: A) Yes, doubling the clock period adds `+2.077 ns` to Hold Slack.

B) No! Hold is checked on the SAME rising clock edge (`Slack_hold = [t_CQ,min + t_logic,min] - [t_hold,max + t_skew]`), which does NOT contain `T_clk`! Lowering frequency has zero effect on hold slack; the true fix is inserting non-inverting delay buffers (`set_fix_hold`) on the short contamination path to increase `t_logic,min` by >= `0.08 ns`.
C) Yes, because hold violations only happen above 500 MHz.
D) No, the only fix is deleting the flip-flop.
quiz_questions.hint: Write down the Hold Slack equation from Midterm Q3 / Q5 / Q10: does the clock period `T_clk` appear anywhere in `(t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)`?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Adding `+2.077 ns` to `T_clk` increases SETUP slack by `+2.077 ns`, but changes HOLD slack by `0.000 ns`!

Correct! Because Hold checks that a launching DFF does not overwrite a capturing DFF on the SAME clock edge (`t = 0`), `T_clk` cancels out completely. Only adding minimum path delay (delay buffers via `set_fix_hold`) or reducing clock skew fixes a hold violation!
Incorrect — Even a `1 Hz` (`T_clk = 1 second`) clock will fail Hold if `t_CQ,min + t_logic,min < t_hold + t_skew` on the active clock edge!
Incorrect — Deleting pipeline flip-flops breaks the synchronous systolic architecture.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly proven in Midterm Q3, Q5, and Q10: `Slack_hold = (t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)` is independent of `T_clk`. In Fusion Compiler / PrimeTime, `set_fix_hold` inserts small delay cells along fast paths (such as direct `Rpipe` shift wires) so `Slack_hold >= 0.00 ns` across all 3 corners.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q3/Q4/Q9 — Setup Slack & F_max Math)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 60 · STA Setup & Hold Equations] Our 14nm Motion Estimator achieves Setup WNS = `+0.22 ns` in the worst-case slow corner (`ss0p72vm40c`) at `T_clk = 1.923 ns` (520 MHz). What is the longest critical-path total arrival + setup + uncertainty time in `ss0p72vm40c`, and what is the maximum achievable clock frequency?
options: A) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns - 0.22 ns = 1.703 ns`; max frequency `f_max = 1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`.
B) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns + 0.22 ns = 2.143 ns`; max frequency = `466 MHz`.
C) Critical path total time = `0.22 ns`; max frequency = `4.5 GHz`.
D) Setup WNS does not affect maximum frequency.
quiz_questions.hint: Use the fundamental Setup Slack identity: `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total`. Solve for `T_path_total = T_clk - Slack_setup`, then compute `f_max = 1 / T_path_total`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Positive slack `+0.22 ns` means the critical path finished `0.22 ns` BEFORE the `1.923 ns` deadline (`1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`), allowing operation up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`!
Incorrect — Adding `+0.22 ns` corresponds to a NEGATIVE slack violation (`-0.22 ns`), whereas our slack is positive (`+0.22 ns`).
Incorrect — `0.22 ns` is the spare timing margin (slack), not the path delay.
Incorrect — Setup WNS directly determines the minimum safe clock period `T_clk,min` and therefore `f_max`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Since `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total = +0.22 ns`, the critical path takes `1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`, meaning the routed 14nm chip can run up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz` even in the slowest `0.72V SS` corner!

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (14nm Physical DRC Closure & M7 Clock Routing Rule)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 60 · 14nm Physical DRC & CTS Closure] Why did constraining Clock Tree Synthesis to metal layers `M2..M7` (`set_clock_routing_rules -net_type root -max_routing_layer M7`) eliminate the upper-metal DRC violations in standalone Synopsys IC Validator (`icv`)?
options: A) Because `M8` and `M9` are thick top-level power/global layers with wide minimum-spacing and fat-wire rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`); keeping high-fanout clock tree branches on `M2..M7` avoids wide-metal stub spacing conflicts and achieves `0 / 242` DRC errors.
B) Because `M7` has zero electrical resistance.
C) Because `icv` only checks `M1`.
D) Because `M8` is made of polysilicon.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the physical pitch and spacing rules of intermediate signal routing layers (`M2..M7`) versus top-level thick power/global distribution layers (`M8, M9`) in a 14nm FinFET BEOL stack.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In `SAED14nm`, `M8/M9` carry the PG mesh straps and enforce wide-metal spacing rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`). Restricting CTS to `M2..M7` eliminates all upper-metal stub conflicts (`0 / 242` DRC violations).
Incorrect — All copper metal layers have finite sheet resistance `R_s`.
Incorrect — Standalone `icv` evaluates all 242 foundry deck rules across FEOL (FinFET active/gate) and BEOL (`M1..M9` and vias).
Incorrect — `M8` is an upper back-end-of-line (BEOL) copper interconnect layer, not front-end polysilicon.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Routing clock nets up to `M7` leaves `M8/M9` clean for power/top routing and resolves all 242 SAED14nm deck rules with `0` violations.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Midterm Q3/Q5/Q10 — Same-Edge Hold Physics Across PVT Corners)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 60 · Advanced Multi-Corner STA Physics] Suppose a classmate sees a Hold violation (`Hold WNS = -0.08 ns`) in PrimeTime at the `ff0p88v125c` (Fast-Fast `0.88V`) corner and proposes lowering the clock frequency from `520 MHz` (`1.923 ns`) down to `250 MHz` (`4.000 ns`) to fix it. Based on Midterm Q3 & Q10, will lowering `f_clk` fix the hold violation, and what is the true physical fix?
options: A) Yes, doubling the clock period adds `+2.077 ns` to Hold Slack.

B) No! Hold is checked on the SAME rising clock edge (`Slack_hold = [t_CQ,min + t_logic,min] - [t_hold,max + t_skew]`), which does NOT contain `T_clk`! Lowering frequency has zero effect on hold slack; the true fix is inserting non-inverting delay buffers (`set_fix_hold`) on the short contamination path to increase `t_logic,min` by >= `0.08 ns`.
C) Yes, because hold violations only happen above 500 MHz.
D) No, the only fix is deleting the flip-flop.
quiz_questions.hint: Write down the Hold Slack equation from Midterm Q3 / Q5 / Q10: does the clock period `T_clk` appear anywhere in `(t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)`?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Adding `+2.077 ns` to `T_clk` increases SETUP slack by `+2.077 ns`, but changes HOLD slack by `0.000 ns`!

Correct! Because Hold checks that a launching DFF does not overwrite a capturing DFF on the SAME clock edge (`t = 0`), `T_clk` cancels out completely. Only adding minimum path delay (delay buffers via `set_fix_hold`) or reducing clock skew fixes a hold violation!
Incorrect — Even a `1 Hz` (`T_clk = 1 second`) clock will fail Hold if `t_CQ,min + t_logic,min < t_hold + t_skew` on the active clock edge!
Incorrect — Deleting pipeline flip-flops breaks the synchronous systolic architecture.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly proven in Midterm Q3, Q5, and Q10: `Slack_hold = (t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)` is independent of `T_clk`. In Fusion Compiler / PrimeTime, `set_fix_hold` inserts small delay cells along fast paths (such as direct `Rpipe` shift wires) so `Slack_hold >= 0.00 ns` across all 3 corners.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q3/Q4/Q9 — Setup Slack & F_max Math)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 61 · STA Setup & Hold Equations] Our 14nm Motion Estimator achieves Setup WNS = `+0.22 ns` in the worst-case slow corner (`ss0p72vm40c`) at `T_clk = 1.923 ns` (520 MHz). What is the longest critical-path total arrival + setup + uncertainty time in `ss0p72vm40c`, and what is the maximum achievable clock frequency?
options: A) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns - 0.22 ns = 1.703 ns`; max frequency `f_max = 1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`.
B) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns + 0.22 ns = 2.143 ns`; max frequency = `466 MHz`.
C) Critical path total time = `0.22 ns`; max frequency = `4.5 GHz`.
D) Setup WNS does not affect maximum frequency.
quiz_questions.hint: Use the fundamental Setup Slack identity: `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total`. Solve for `T_path_total = T_clk - Slack_setup`, then compute `f_max = 1 / T_path_total`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Positive slack `+0.22 ns` means the critical path finished `0.22 ns` BEFORE the `1.923 ns` deadline (`1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`), allowing operation up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`!
Incorrect — Adding `+0.22 ns` corresponds to a NEGATIVE slack violation (`-0.22 ns`), whereas our slack is positive (`+0.22 ns`).
Incorrect — `0.22 ns` is the spare timing margin (slack), not the path delay.
Incorrect — Setup WNS directly determines the minimum safe clock period `T_clk,min` and therefore `f_max`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Since `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total = +0.22 ns`, the critical path takes `1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`, meaning the routed 14nm chip can run up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz` even in the slowest `0.72V SS` corner!

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (14nm Physical DRC Closure & M7 Clock Routing Rule)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 61 · 14nm Physical DRC & CTS Closure] Why did constraining Clock Tree Synthesis to metal layers `M2..M7` (`set_clock_routing_rules -net_type root -max_routing_layer M7`) eliminate the upper-metal DRC violations in standalone Synopsys IC Validator (`icv`)?
options: A) Because `M8` and `M9` are thick top-level power/global layers with wide minimum-spacing and fat-wire rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`); keeping high-fanout clock tree branches on `M2..M7` avoids wide-metal stub spacing conflicts and achieves `0 / 242` DRC errors.
B) Because `M7` has zero electrical resistance.
C) Because `icv` only checks `M1`.
D) Because `M8` is made of polysilicon.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the physical pitch and spacing rules of intermediate signal routing layers (`M2..M7`) versus top-level thick power/global distribution layers (`M8, M9`) in a 14nm FinFET BEOL stack.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In `SAED14nm`, `M8/M9` carry the PG mesh straps and enforce wide-metal spacing rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`). Restricting CTS to `M2..M7` eliminates all upper-metal stub conflicts (`0 / 242` DRC violations).
Incorrect — All copper metal layers have finite sheet resistance `R_s`.
Incorrect — Standalone `icv` evaluates all 242 foundry deck rules across FEOL (FinFET active/gate) and BEOL (`M1..M9` and vias).
Incorrect — `M8` is an upper back-end-of-line (BEOL) copper interconnect layer, not front-end polysilicon.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Routing clock nets up to `M7` leaves `M8/M9` clean for power/top routing and resolves all 242 SAED14nm deck rules with `0` violations.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Midterm Q3/Q5/Q10 — Same-Edge Hold Physics Across PVT Corners)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 61 · Advanced Multi-Corner STA Physics] Suppose a classmate sees a Hold violation (`Hold WNS = -0.08 ns`) in PrimeTime at the `ff0p88v125c` (Fast-Fast `0.88V`) corner and proposes lowering the clock frequency from `520 MHz` (`1.923 ns`) down to `250 MHz` (`4.000 ns`) to fix it. Based on Midterm Q3 & Q10, will lowering `f_clk` fix the hold violation, and what is the true physical fix?
options: A) Yes, doubling the clock period adds `+2.077 ns` to Hold Slack.

B) No! Hold is checked on the SAME rising clock edge (`Slack_hold = [t_CQ,min + t_logic,min] - [t_hold,max + t_skew]`), which does NOT contain `T_clk`! Lowering frequency has zero effect on hold slack; the true fix is inserting non-inverting delay buffers (`set_fix_hold`) on the short contamination path to increase `t_logic,min` by >= `0.08 ns`.
C) Yes, because hold violations only happen above 500 MHz.
D) No, the only fix is deleting the flip-flop.
quiz_questions.hint: Write down the Hold Slack equation from Midterm Q3 / Q5 / Q10: does the clock period `T_clk` appear anywhere in `(t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)`?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Adding `+2.077 ns` to `T_clk` increases SETUP slack by `+2.077 ns`, but changes HOLD slack by `0.000 ns`!

Correct! Because Hold checks that a launching DFF does not overwrite a capturing DFF on the SAME clock edge (`t = 0`), `T_clk` cancels out completely. Only adding minimum path delay (delay buffers via `set_fix_hold`) or reducing clock skew fixes a hold violation!
Incorrect — Even a `1 Hz` (`T_clk = 1 second`) clock will fail Hold if `t_CQ,min + t_logic,min < t_hold + t_skew` on the active clock edge!
Incorrect — Deleting pipeline flip-flops breaks the synchronous systolic architecture.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly proven in Midterm Q3, Q5, and Q10: `Slack_hold = (t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)` is independent of `T_clk`. In Fusion Compiler / PrimeTime, `set_fix_hold` inserts small delay cells along fast paths (such as direct `Rpipe` shift wires) so `Slack_hold >= 0.00 ns` across all 3 corners.

And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q3/Q4/Q9 — Setup Slack & F_max Math)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 62 · STA Setup & Hold Equations] Our 14nm Motion Estimator achieves Setup WNS = `+0.22 ns` in the worst-case slow corner (`ss0p72vm40c`) at `T_clk = 1.923 ns` (520 MHz). What is the longest critical-path total arrival + setup + uncertainty time in `ss0p72vm40c`, and what is the maximum achievable clock frequency?
options: A) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns - 0.22 ns = 1.703 ns`; max frequency `f_max = 1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`.
B) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns + 0.22 ns = 2.143 ns`; max frequency = `466 MHz`.
C) Critical path total time = `0.22 ns`; max frequency = `4.5 GHz`.
D) Setup WNS does not affect maximum frequency.
quiz_questions.hint: Use the fundamental Setup Slack identity: `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total`. Solve for `T_path_total = T_clk - Slack_setup`, then compute `f_max = 1 / T_path_total`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Positive slack `+0.22 ns` means the critical path finished `0.22 ns` BEFORE the `1.923 ns` deadline (`1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`), allowing operation up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`!
Incorrect — Adding `+0.22 ns` corresponds to a NEGATIVE slack violation (`-0.22 ns`), whereas our slack is positive (`+0.22 ns`).
Incorrect — `0.22 ns` is the spare timing margin (slack), not the path delay.
Incorrect — Setup WNS directly determines the minimum safe clock period `T_clk,min` and therefore `f_max`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Since `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total = +0.22 ns`, the critical path takes `1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`, meaning the routed 14nm chip can run up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz` even in the slowest `0.72V SS` corner!

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (14nm Physical DRC Closure & M7 Clock Routing Rule)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 62 · 14nm Physical DRC & CTS Closure] Why did constraining Clock Tree Synthesis to metal layers `M2..M7` (`set_clock_routing_rules -net_type root -max_routing_layer M7`) eliminate the upper-metal DRC violations in standalone Synopsys IC Validator (`icv`)?
options: A) Because `M8` and `M9` are thick top-level power/global layers with wide minimum-spacing and fat-wire rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`); keeping high-fanout clock tree branches on `M2..M7` avoids wide-metal stub spacing conflicts and achieves `0 / 242` DRC errors.
B) Because `M7` has zero electrical resistance.
C) Because `icv` only checks `M1`.
D) Because `M8` is made of polysilicon.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the physical pitch and spacing rules of intermediate signal routing layers (`M2..M7`) versus top-level thick power/global distribution layers (`M8, M9`) in a 14nm FinFET BEOL stack.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In `SAED14nm`, `M8/M9` carry the PG mesh straps and enforce wide-metal spacing rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`). Restricting CTS to `M2..M7` eliminates all upper-metal stub conflicts (`0 / 242` DRC violations).
Incorrect — All copper metal layers have finite sheet resistance `R_s`.
Incorrect — Standalone `icv` evaluates all 242 foundry deck rules across FEOL (FinFET active/gate) and BEOL (`M1..M9` and vias).
Incorrect — `M8` is an upper back-end-of-line (BEOL) copper interconnect layer, not front-end polysilicon.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Routing clock nets up to `M7` leaves `M8/M9` clean for power/top routing and resolves all 242 SAED14nm deck rules with `0` violations.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Midterm Q3/Q5/Q10 — Same-Edge Hold Physics Across PVT Corners)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 62 · Advanced Multi-Corner STA Physics] Suppose a classmate sees a Hold violation (`Hold WNS = -0.08 ns`) in PrimeTime at the `ff0p88v125c` (Fast-Fast `0.88V`) corner and proposes lowering the clock frequency from `520 MHz` (`1.923 ns`) down to `250 MHz` (`4.000 ns`) to fix it. Based on Midterm Q3 & Q10, will lowering `f_clk` fix the hold violation, and what is the true physical fix?
options: A) Yes, doubling the clock period adds `+2.077 ns` to Hold Slack.

B) No! Hold is checked on the SAME rising clock edge (`Slack_hold = [t_CQ,min + t_logic,min] - [t_hold,max + t_skew]`), which does NOT contain `T_clk`! Lowering frequency has zero effect on hold slack; the true fix is inserting non-inverting delay buffers (`set_fix_hold`) on the short contamination path to increase `t_logic,min` by >= `0.08 ns`.
C) Yes, because hold violations only happen above 500 MHz.
D) No, the only fix is deleting the flip-flop.
quiz_questions.hint: Write down the Hold Slack equation from Midterm Q3 / Q5 / Q10: does the clock period `T_clk` appear anywhere in `(t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)`?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Adding `+2.077 ns` to `T_clk` increases SETUP slack by `+2.077 ns`, but changes HOLD slack by `0.000 ns`!

Correct! Because Hold checks that a launching DFF does not overwrite a capturing DFF on the SAME clock edge (`t = 0`), `T_clk` cancels out completely. Only adding minimum path delay (delay buffers via `set_fix_hold`) or reducing clock skew fixes a hold violation!
Incorrect — Even a `1 Hz` (`T_clk = 1 second`) clock will fail Hold if `t_CQ,min + t_logic,min < t_hold + t_skew` on the active clock edge!
Incorrect — Deleting pipeline flip-flops breaks the synchronous systolic architecture.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly proven in Midterm Q3, Q5, and Q10: `Slack_hold = (t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)` is independent of `T_clk`. In Fusion Compiler / PrimeTime, `set_fix_hold` inserts small delay cells along fast paths (such as direct `Rpipe` shift wires) so `Slack_hold >= 0.00 ns` across all 3 corners.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q3/Q4/Q9 — Setup Slack & F_max Math)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 63 · STA Setup & Hold Equations] Our 14nm Motion Estimator achieves Setup WNS = `+0.22 ns` in the worst-case slow corner (`ss0p72vm40c`) at `T_clk = 1.923 ns` (520 MHz). What is the longest critical-path total arrival + setup + uncertainty time in `ss0p72vm40c`, and what is the maximum achievable clock frequency?
options: A) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns - 0.22 ns = 1.703 ns`; max frequency `f_max = 1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`.
B) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns + 0.22 ns = 2.143 ns`; max frequency = `466 MHz`.
C) Critical path total time = `0.22 ns`; max frequency = `4.5 GHz`.
D) Setup WNS does not affect maximum frequency.
quiz_questions.hint: Use the fundamental Setup Slack identity: `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total`. Solve for `T_path_total = T_clk - Slack_setup`, then compute `f_max = 1 / T_path_total`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Positive slack `+0.22 ns` means the critical path finished `0.22 ns` BEFORE the `1.923 ns` deadline (`1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`), allowing operation up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`!
Incorrect — Adding `+0.22 ns` corresponds to a NEGATIVE slack violation (`-0.22 ns`), whereas our slack is positive (`+0.22 ns`).
Incorrect — `0.22 ns` is the spare timing margin (slack), not the path delay.
Incorrect — Setup WNS directly determines the minimum safe clock period `T_clk,min` and therefore `f_max`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Since `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total = +0.22 ns`, the critical path takes `1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`, meaning the routed 14nm chip can run up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz` even in the slowest `0.72V SS` corner!

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (14nm Physical DRC Closure & M7 Clock Routing Rule)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 63 · 14nm Physical DRC & CTS Closure] Why did constraining Clock Tree Synthesis to metal layers `M2..M7` (`set_clock_routing_rules -net_type root -max_routing_layer M7`) eliminate the upper-metal DRC violations in standalone Synopsys IC Validator (`icv`)?
options: A) Because `M8` and `M9` are thick top-level power/global layers with wide minimum-spacing and fat-wire rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`); keeping high-fanout clock tree branches on `M2..M7` avoids wide-metal stub spacing conflicts and achieves `0 / 242` DRC errors.
B) Because `M7` has zero electrical resistance.
C) Because `icv` only checks `M1`.
D) Because `M8` is made of polysilicon.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the physical pitch and spacing rules of intermediate signal routing layers (`M2..M7`) versus top-level thick power/global distribution layers (`M8, M9`) in a 14nm FinFET BEOL stack.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In `SAED14nm`, `M8/M9` carry the PG mesh straps and enforce wide-metal spacing rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`). Restricting CTS to `M2..M7` eliminates all upper-metal stub conflicts (`0 / 242` DRC violations).
Incorrect — All copper metal layers have finite sheet resistance `R_s`.
Incorrect — Standalone `icv` evaluates all 242 foundry deck rules across FEOL (FinFET active/gate) and BEOL (`M1..M9` and vias).
Incorrect — `M8` is an upper back-end-of-line (BEOL) copper interconnect layer, not front-end polysilicon.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Routing clock nets up to `M7` leaves `M8/M9` clean for power/top routing and resolves all 242 SAED14nm deck rules with `0` violations.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Midterm Q3/Q5/Q10 — Same-Edge Hold Physics Across PVT Corners)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 63 · Advanced Multi-Corner STA Physics] Suppose a classmate sees a Hold violation (`Hold WNS = -0.08 ns`) in PrimeTime at the `ff0p88v125c` (Fast-Fast `0.88V`) corner and proposes lowering the clock frequency from `520 MHz` (`1.923 ns`) down to `250 MHz` (`4.000 ns`) to fix it. Based on Midterm Q3 & Q10, will lowering `f_clk` fix the hold violation, and what is the true physical fix?
options: A) Yes, doubling the clock period adds `+2.077 ns` to Hold Slack.

B) No! Hold is checked on the SAME rising clock edge (`Slack_hold = [t_CQ,min + t_logic,min] - [t_hold,max + t_skew]`), which does NOT contain `T_clk`! Lowering frequency has zero effect on hold slack; the true fix is inserting non-inverting delay buffers (`set_fix_hold`) on the short contamination path to increase `t_logic,min` by >= `0.08 ns`.
C) Yes, because hold violations only happen above 500 MHz.
D) No, the only fix is deleting the flip-flop.
quiz_questions.hint: Write down the Hold Slack equation from Midterm Q3 / Q5 / Q10: does the clock period `T_clk` appear anywhere in `(t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)`?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Adding `+2.077 ns` to `T_clk` increases SETUP slack by `+2.077 ns`, but changes HOLD slack by `0.000 ns`!

Correct! Because Hold checks that a launching DFF does not overwrite a capturing DFF on the SAME clock edge (`t = 0`), `T_clk` cancels out completely. Only adding minimum path delay (delay buffers via `set_fix_hold`) or reducing clock skew fixes a hold violation!
Incorrect — Even a `1 Hz` (`T_clk = 1 second`) clock will fail Hold if `t_CQ,min + t_logic,min < t_hold + t_skew` on the active clock edge!
Incorrect — Deleting pipeline flip-flops breaks the synchronous systolic architecture.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly proven in Midterm Q3, Q5, and Q10: `Slack_hold = (t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)` is independent of `T_clk`. In Fusion Compiler / PrimeTime, `set_fix_hold` inserts small delay cells along fast paths (such as direct `Rpipe` shift wires) so `Slack_hold >= 0.00 ns` across all 3 corners.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q3/Q4/Q9 — Setup Slack & F_max Math)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 64 · STA Setup & Hold Equations] Our 14nm Motion Estimator achieves Setup WNS = `+0.22 ns` in the worst-case slow corner (`ss0p72vm40c`) at `T_clk = 1.923 ns` (520 MHz). What is the longest critical-path total arrival + setup + uncertainty time in `ss0p72vm40c`, and what is the maximum achievable clock frequency?
options: A) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns - 0.22 ns = 1.703 ns`; max frequency `f_max = 1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`.
B) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns + 0.22 ns = 2.143 ns`; max frequency = `466 MHz`.
C) Critical path total time = `0.22 ns`; max frequency = `4.5 GHz`.
D) Setup WNS does not affect maximum frequency.
quiz_questions.hint: Use the fundamental Setup Slack identity: `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total`. Solve for `T_path_total = T_clk - Slack_setup`, then compute `f_max = 1 / T_path_total`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Positive slack `+0.22 ns` means the critical path finished `0.22 ns` BEFORE the `1.923 ns` deadline (`1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`), allowing operation up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`!
Incorrect — Adding `+0.22 ns` corresponds to a NEGATIVE slack violation (`-0.22 ns`), whereas our slack is positive (`+0.22 ns`).
Incorrect — `0.22 ns` is the spare timing margin (slack), not the path delay.
Incorrect — Setup WNS directly determines the minimum safe clock period `T_clk,min` and therefore `f_max`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Since `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total = +0.22 ns`, the critical path takes `1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`, meaning the routed 14nm chip can run up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz` even in the slowest `0.72V SS` corner!

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (14nm Physical DRC Closure & M7 Clock Routing Rule)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 64 · 14nm Physical DRC & CTS Closure] Why did constraining Clock Tree Synthesis to metal layers `M2..M7` (`set_clock_routing_rules -net_type root -max_routing_layer M7`) eliminate the upper-metal DRC violations in standalone Synopsys IC Validator (`icv`)?
options: A) Because `M8` and `M9` are thick top-level power/global layers with wide minimum-spacing and fat-wire rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`); keeping high-fanout clock tree branches on `M2..M7` avoids wide-metal stub spacing conflicts and achieves `0 / 242` DRC errors.
B) Because `M7` has zero electrical resistance.
C) Because `icv` only checks `M1`.
D) Because `M8` is made of polysilicon.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the physical pitch and spacing rules of intermediate signal routing layers (`M2..M7`) versus top-level thick power/global distribution layers (`M8, M9`) in a 14nm FinFET BEOL stack.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In `SAED14nm`, `M8/M9` carry the PG mesh straps and enforce wide-metal spacing rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`). Restricting CTS to `M2..M7` eliminates all upper-metal stub conflicts (`0 / 242` DRC violations).
Incorrect — All copper metal layers have finite sheet resistance `R_s`.
Incorrect — Standalone `icv` evaluates all 242 foundry deck rules across FEOL (FinFET active/gate) and BEOL (`M1..M9` and vias).
Incorrect — `M8` is an upper back-end-of-line (BEOL) copper interconnect layer, not front-end polysilicon.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Routing clock nets up to `M7` leaves `M8/M9` clean for power/top routing and resolves all 242 SAED14nm deck rules with `0` violations.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Midterm Q3/Q5/Q10 — Same-Edge Hold Physics Across PVT Corners)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 64 · Advanced Multi-Corner STA Physics] Suppose a classmate sees a Hold violation (`Hold WNS = -0.08 ns`) in PrimeTime at the `ff0p88v125c` (Fast-Fast `0.88V`) corner and proposes lowering the clock frequency from `520 MHz` (`1.923 ns`) down to `250 MHz` (`4.000 ns`) to fix it. Based on Midterm Q3 & Q10, will lowering `f_clk` fix the hold violation, and what is the true physical fix?
options: A) Yes, doubling the clock period adds `+2.077 ns` to Hold Slack.

B) No! Hold is checked on the SAME rising clock edge (`Slack_hold = [t_CQ,min + t_logic,min] - [t_hold,max + t_skew]`), which does NOT contain `T_clk`! Lowering frequency has zero effect on hold slack; the true fix is inserting non-inverting delay buffers (`set_fix_hold`) on the short contamination path to increase `t_logic,min` by >= `0.08 ns`.
C) Yes, because hold violations only happen above 500 MHz.
D) No, the only fix is deleting the flip-flop.
quiz_questions.hint: Write down the Hold Slack equation from Midterm Q3 / Q5 / Q10: does the clock period `T_clk` appear anywhere in `(t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)`?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Adding `+2.077 ns` to `T_clk` increases SETUP slack by `+2.077 ns`, but changes HOLD slack by `0.000 ns`!

Correct! Because Hold checks that a launching DFF does not overwrite a capturing DFF on the SAME clock edge (`t = 0`), `T_clk` cancels out completely. Only adding minimum path delay (delay buffers via `set_fix_hold`) or reducing clock skew fixes a hold violation!
Incorrect — Even a `1 Hz` (`T_clk = 1 second`) clock will fail Hold if `t_CQ,min + t_logic,min < t_hold + t_skew` on the active clock edge!
Incorrect — Deleting pipeline flip-flops breaks the synchronous systolic architecture.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly proven in Midterm Q3, Q5, and Q10: `Slack_hold = (t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)` is independent of `T_clk`. In Fusion Compiler / PrimeTime, `set_fix_hold` inserts small delay cells along fast paths (such as direct `Rpipe` shift wires) so `Slack_hold >= 0.00 ns` across all 3 corners.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q3/Q4/Q9 — Setup Slack & F_max Math)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 65 · STA Setup & Hold Equations] Our 14nm Motion Estimator achieves Setup WNS = `+0.22 ns` in the worst-case slow corner (`ss0p72vm40c`) at `T_clk = 1.923 ns` (520 MHz). What is the longest critical-path total arrival + setup + uncertainty time in `ss0p72vm40c`, and what is the maximum achievable clock frequency?
options: A) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns - 0.22 ns = 1.703 ns`; max frequency `f_max = 1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`.
B) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns + 0.22 ns = 2.143 ns`; max frequency = `466 MHz`.
C) Critical path total time = `0.22 ns`; max frequency = `4.5 GHz`.
D) Setup WNS does not affect maximum frequency.
quiz_questions.hint: Use the fundamental Setup Slack identity: `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total`. Solve for `T_path_total = T_clk - Slack_setup`, then compute `f_max = 1 / T_path_total`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Positive slack `+0.22 ns` means the critical path finished `0.22 ns` BEFORE the `1.923 ns` deadline (`1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`), allowing operation up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`!
Incorrect — Adding `+0.22 ns` corresponds to a NEGATIVE slack violation (`-0.22 ns`), whereas our slack is positive (`+0.22 ns`).
Incorrect — `0.22 ns` is the spare timing margin (slack), not the path delay.
Incorrect — Setup WNS directly determines the minimum safe clock period `T_clk,min` and therefore `f_max`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Since `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total = +0.22 ns`, the critical path takes `1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`, meaning the routed 14nm chip can run up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz` even in the slowest `0.72V SS` corner!

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (14nm Physical DRC Closure & M7 Clock Routing Rule)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 65 · 14nm Physical DRC & CTS Closure] Why did constraining Clock Tree Synthesis to metal layers `M2..M7` (`set_clock_routing_rules -net_type root -max_routing_layer M7`) eliminate the upper-metal DRC violations in standalone Synopsys IC Validator (`icv`)?
options: A) Because `M8` and `M9` are thick top-level power/global layers with wide minimum-spacing and fat-wire rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`); keeping high-fanout clock tree branches on `M2..M7` avoids wide-metal stub spacing conflicts and achieves `0 / 242` DRC errors.
B) Because `M7` has zero electrical resistance.
C) Because `icv` only checks `M1`.
D) Because `M8` is made of polysilicon.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the physical pitch and spacing rules of intermediate signal routing layers (`M2..M7`) versus top-level thick power/global distribution layers (`M8, M9`) in a 14nm FinFET BEOL stack.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In `SAED14nm`, `M8/M9` carry the PG mesh straps and enforce wide-metal spacing rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`). Restricting CTS to `M2..M7` eliminates all upper-metal stub conflicts (`0 / 242` DRC violations).
Incorrect — All copper metal layers have finite sheet resistance `R_s`.
Incorrect — Standalone `icv` evaluates all 242 foundry deck rules across FEOL (FinFET active/gate) and BEOL (`M1..M9` and vias).
Incorrect — `M8` is an upper back-end-of-line (BEOL) copper interconnect layer, not front-end polysilicon.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Routing clock nets up to `M7` leaves `M8/M9` clean for power/top routing and resolves all 242 SAED14nm deck rules with `0` violations.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Midterm Q3/Q5/Q10 — Same-Edge Hold Physics Across PVT Corners)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 65 · Advanced Multi-Corner STA Physics] Suppose a classmate sees a Hold violation (`Hold WNS = -0.08 ns`) in PrimeTime at the `ff0p88v125c` (Fast-Fast `0.88V`) corner and proposes lowering the clock frequency from `520 MHz` (`1.923 ns`) down to `250 MHz` (`4.000 ns`) to fix it. Based on Midterm Q3 & Q10, will lowering `f_clk` fix the hold violation, and what is the true physical fix?
options: A) Yes, doubling the clock period adds `+2.077 ns` to Hold Slack.

B) No! Hold is checked on the SAME rising clock edge (`Slack_hold = [t_CQ,min + t_logic,min] - [t_hold,max + t_skew]`), which does NOT contain `T_clk`! Lowering frequency has zero effect on hold slack; the true fix is inserting non-inverting delay buffers (`set_fix_hold`) on the short contamination path to increase `t_logic,min` by >= `0.08 ns`.
C) Yes, because hold violations only happen above 500 MHz.
D) No, the only fix is deleting the flip-flop.
quiz_questions.hint: Write down the Hold Slack equation from Midterm Q3 / Q5 / Q10: does the clock period `T_clk` appear anywhere in `(t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)`?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Adding `+2.077 ns` to `T_clk` increases SETUP slack by `+2.077 ns`, but changes HOLD slack by `0.000 ns`!

Correct! Because Hold checks that a launching DFF does not overwrite a capturing DFF on the SAME clock edge (`t = 0`), `T_clk` cancels out completely. Only adding minimum path delay (delay buffers via `set_fix_hold`) or reducing clock skew fixes a hold violation!
Incorrect — Even a `1 Hz` (`T_clk = 1 second`) clock will fail Hold if `t_CQ,min + t_logic,min < t_hold + t_skew` on the active clock edge!
Incorrect — Deleting pipeline flip-flops breaks the synchronous systolic architecture.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly proven in Midterm Q3, Q5, and Q10: `Slack_hold = (t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)` is independent of `T_clk`. In Fusion Compiler / PrimeTime, `set_fix_hold` inserts small delay cells along fast paths (such as direct `Rpipe` shift wires) so `Slack_hold >= 0.00 ns` across all 3 corners.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q3/Q4/Q9 — Setup Slack & F_max Math)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 66 · STA Setup & Hold Equations] Our 14nm Motion Estimator achieves Setup WNS = `+0.22 ns` in the worst-case slow corner (`ss0p72vm40c`) at `T_clk = 1.923 ns` (520 MHz). What is the longest critical-path total arrival + setup + uncertainty time in `ss0p72vm40c`, and what is the maximum achievable clock frequency?
options: A) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns - 0.22 ns = 1.703 ns`; max frequency `f_max = 1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`.
B) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns + 0.22 ns = 2.143 ns`; max frequency = `466 MHz`.
C) Critical path total time = `0.22 ns`; max frequency = `4.5 GHz`.
D) Setup WNS does not affect maximum frequency.
quiz_questions.hint: Use the fundamental Setup Slack identity: `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total`. Solve for `T_path_total = T_clk - Slack_setup`, then compute `f_max = 1 / T_path_total`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Positive slack `+0.22 ns` means the critical path finished `0.22 ns` BEFORE the `1.923 ns` deadline (`1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`), allowing operation up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`!
Incorrect — Adding `+0.22 ns` corresponds to a NEGATIVE slack violation (`-0.22 ns`), whereas our slack is positive (`+0.22 ns`).
Incorrect — `0.22 ns` is the spare timing margin (slack), not the path delay.
Incorrect — Setup WNS directly determines the minimum safe clock period `T_clk,min` and therefore `f_max`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Since `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total = +0.22 ns`, the critical path takes `1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`, meaning the routed 14nm chip can run up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz` even in the slowest `0.72V SS` corner!

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (14nm Physical DRC Closure & M7 Clock Routing Rule)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 66 · 14nm Physical DRC & CTS Closure] Why did constraining Clock Tree Synthesis to metal layers `M2..M7` (`set_clock_routing_rules -net_type root -max_routing_layer M7`) eliminate the upper-metal DRC violations in standalone Synopsys IC Validator (`icv`)?
options: A) Because `M8` and `M9` are thick top-level power/global layers with wide minimum-spacing and fat-wire rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`); keeping high-fanout clock tree branches on `M2..M7` avoids wide-metal stub spacing conflicts and achieves `0 / 242` DRC errors.
B) Because `M7` has zero electrical resistance.
C) Because `icv` only checks `M1`.
D) Because `M8` is made of polysilicon.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the physical pitch and spacing rules of intermediate signal routing layers (`M2..M7`) versus top-level thick power/global distribution layers (`M8, M9`) in a 14nm FinFET BEOL stack.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In `SAED14nm`, `M8/M9` carry the PG mesh straps and enforce wide-metal spacing rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`). Restricting CTS to `M2..M7` eliminates all upper-metal stub conflicts (`0 / 242` DRC violations).
Incorrect — All copper metal layers have finite sheet resistance `R_s`.
Incorrect — Standalone `icv` evaluates all 242 foundry deck rules across FEOL (FinFET active/gate) and BEOL (`M1..M9` and vias).
Incorrect — `M8` is an upper back-end-of-line (BEOL) copper interconnect layer, not front-end polysilicon.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Routing clock nets up to `M7` leaves `M8/M9` clean for power/top routing and resolves all 242 SAED14nm deck rules with `0` violations.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Midterm Q3/Q5/Q10 — Same-Edge Hold Physics Across PVT Corners)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 66 · Advanced Multi-Corner STA Physics] Suppose a classmate sees a Hold violation (`Hold WNS = -0.08 ns`) in PrimeTime at the `ff0p88v125c` (Fast-Fast `0.88V`) corner and proposes lowering the clock frequency from `520 MHz` (`1.923 ns`) down to `250 MHz` (`4.000 ns`) to fix it. Based on Midterm Q3 & Q10, will lowering `f_clk` fix the hold violation, and what is the true physical fix?
options: A) Yes, doubling the clock period adds `+2.077 ns` to Hold Slack.

B) No! Hold is checked on the SAME rising clock edge (`Slack_hold = [t_CQ,min + t_logic,min] - [t_hold,max + t_skew]`), which does NOT contain `T_clk`! Lowering frequency has zero effect on hold slack; the true fix is inserting non-inverting delay buffers (`set_fix_hold`) on the short contamination path to increase `t_logic,min` by >= `0.08 ns`.
C) Yes, because hold violations only happen above 500 MHz.
D) No, the only fix is deleting the flip-flop.
quiz_questions.hint: Write down the Hold Slack equation from Midterm Q3 / Q5 / Q10: does the clock period `T_clk` appear anywhere in `(t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)`?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Adding `+2.077 ns` to `T_clk` increases SETUP slack by `+2.077 ns`, but changes HOLD slack by `0.000 ns`!

Correct! Because Hold checks that a launching DFF does not overwrite a capturing DFF on the SAME clock edge (`t = 0`), `T_clk` cancels out completely. Only adding minimum path delay (delay buffers via `set_fix_hold`) or reducing clock skew fixes a hold violation!
Incorrect — Even a `1 Hz` (`T_clk = 1 second`) clock will fail Hold if `t_CQ,min + t_logic,min < t_hold + t_skew` on the active clock edge!
Incorrect — Deleting pipeline flip-flops breaks the synchronous systolic architecture.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly proven in Midterm Q3, Q5, and Q10: `Slack_hold = (t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)` is independent of `T_clk`. In Fusion Compiler / PrimeTime, `set_fix_hold` inserts small delay cells along fast paths (such as direct `Rpipe` shift wires) so `Slack_hold >= 0.00 ns` across all 3 corners.

options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 67's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q3/Q4/Q9 — Setup Slack & F_max Math)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 67 · STA Setup & Hold Equations] Our 14nm Motion Estimator achieves Setup WNS = `+0.22 ns` in the worst-case slow corner (`ss0p72vm40c`) at `T_clk = 1.923 ns` (520 MHz). What is the longest critical-path total arrival + setup + uncertainty time in `ss0p72vm40c`, and what is the maximum achievable clock frequency?
options: A) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns - 0.22 ns = 1.703 ns`; max frequency `f_max = 1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`.
B) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns + 0.22 ns = 2.143 ns`; max frequency = `466 MHz`.
C) Critical path total time = `0.22 ns`; max frequency = `4.5 GHz`.
D) Setup WNS does not affect maximum frequency.
quiz_questions.hint: Use the fundamental Setup Slack identity: `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total`. Solve for `T_path_total = T_clk - Slack_setup`, then compute `f_max = 1 / T_path_total`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Positive slack `+0.22 ns` means the critical path finished `0.22 ns` BEFORE the `1.923 ns` deadline (`1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`), allowing operation up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`!
Incorrect — Adding `+0.22 ns` corresponds to a NEGATIVE slack violation (`-0.22 ns`), whereas our slack is positive (`+0.22 ns`).
Incorrect — `0.22 ns` is the spare timing margin (slack), not the path delay.
Incorrect — Setup WNS directly determines the minimum safe clock period `T_clk,min` and therefore `f_max`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Since `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total = +0.22 ns`, the critical path takes `1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`, meaning the routed 14nm chip can run up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz` even in the slowest `0.72V SS` corner!

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (14nm Physical DRC Closure & M7 Clock Routing Rule)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 67 · 14nm Physical DRC & CTS Closure] Why did constraining Clock Tree Synthesis to metal layers `M2..M7` (`set_clock_routing_rules -net_type root -max_routing_layer M7`) eliminate the upper-metal DRC violations in standalone Synopsys IC Validator (`icv`)?
options: A) Because `M8` and `M9` are thick top-level power/global layers with wide minimum-spacing and fat-wire rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`); keeping high-fanout clock tree branches on `M2..M7` avoids wide-metal stub spacing conflicts and achieves `0 / 242` DRC errors.
B) Because `M7` has zero electrical resistance.
C) Because `icv` only checks `M1`.
D) Because `M8` is made of polysilicon.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the physical pitch and spacing rules of intermediate signal routing layers (`M2..M7`) versus top-level thick power/global distribution layers (`M8, M9`) in a 14nm FinFET BEOL stack.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In `SAED14nm`, `M8/M9` carry the PG mesh straps and enforce wide-metal spacing rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`). Restricting CTS to `M2..M7` eliminates all upper-metal stub conflicts (`0 / 242` DRC violations).
Incorrect — All copper metal layers have finite sheet resistance `R_s`.
Incorrect — Standalone `icv` evaluates all 242 foundry deck rules across FEOL (FinFET active/gate) and BEOL (`M1..M9` and vias).
Incorrect — `M8` is an upper back-end-of-line (BEOL) copper interconnect layer, not front-end polysilicon.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Routing clock nets up to `M7` leaves `M8/M9` clean for power/top routing and resolves all 242 SAED14nm deck rules with `0` violations.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Midterm Q3/Q5/Q10 — Same-Edge Hold Physics Across PVT Corners)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 67 · Advanced Multi-Corner STA Physics] Suppose a classmate sees a Hold violation (`Hold WNS = -0.08 ns`) in PrimeTime at the `ff0p88v125c` (Fast-Fast `0.88V`) corner and proposes lowering the clock frequency from `520 MHz` (`1.923 ns`) down to `250 MHz` (`4.000 ns`) to fix it. Based on Midterm Q3 & Q10, will lowering `f_clk` fix the hold violation, and what is the true physical fix?
options: A) Yes, doubling the clock period adds `+2.077 ns` to Hold Slack.

B) No! Hold is checked on the SAME rising clock edge (`Slack_hold = [t_CQ,min + t_logic,min] - [t_hold,max + t_skew]`), which does NOT contain `T_clk`! Lowering frequency has zero effect on hold slack; the true fix is inserting non-inverting delay buffers (`set_fix_hold`) on the short contamination path to increase `t_logic,min` by >= `0.08 ns`.
C) Yes, because hold violations only happen above 500 MHz.
D) No, the only fix is deleting the flip-flop.
quiz_questions.hint: Write down the Hold Slack equation from Midterm Q3 / Q5 / Q10: does the clock period `T_clk` appear anywhere in `(t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)`?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Adding `+2.077 ns` to `T_clk` increases SETUP slack by `+2.077 ns`, but changes HOLD slack by `0.000 ns`!

Correct! Because Hold checks that a launching DFF does not overwrite a capturing DFF on the SAME clock edge (`t = 0`), `T_clk` cancels out completely. Only adding minimum path delay (delay buffers via `set_fix_hold`) or reducing clock skew fixes a hold violation!
Incorrect — Even a `1 Hz` (`T_clk = 1 second`) clock will fail Hold if `t_CQ,min + t_logic,min < t_hold + t_skew` on the active clock edge!
Incorrect — Deleting pipeline flip-flops breaks the synchronous systolic architecture.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly proven in Midterm Q3, Q5, and Q10: `Slack_hold = (t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)` is independent of `T_clk`. In Fusion Compiler / PrimeTime, `set_fix_hold` inserts small delay cells along fast paths (such as direct `Rpipe` shift wires) so `Slack_hold >= 0.00 ns` across all 3 corners.

Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 68's expected output markers.

quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q3/Q4/Q9 — Setup Slack & F_max Math)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 68 · STA Setup & Hold Equations] Our 14nm Motion Estimator achieves Setup WNS = `+0.22 ns` in the worst-case slow corner (`ss0p72vm40c`) at `T_clk = 1.923 ns` (520 MHz). What is the longest critical-path total arrival + setup + uncertainty time in `ss0p72vm40c`, and what is the maximum achievable clock frequency?
options: A) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns - 0.22 ns = 1.703 ns`; max frequency `f_max = 1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`.
B) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns + 0.22 ns = 2.143 ns`; max frequency = `466 MHz`.
C) Critical path total time = `0.22 ns`; max frequency = `4.5 GHz`.
D) Setup WNS does not affect maximum frequency.
quiz_questions.hint: Use the fundamental Setup Slack identity: `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total`. Solve for `T_path_total = T_clk - Slack_setup`, then compute `f_max = 1 / T_path_total`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Positive slack `+0.22 ns` means the critical path finished `0.22 ns` BEFORE the `1.923 ns` deadline (`1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`), allowing operation up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`!
Incorrect — Adding `+0.22 ns` corresponds to a NEGATIVE slack violation (`-0.22 ns`), whereas our slack is positive (`+0.22 ns`).
Incorrect — `0.22 ns` is the spare timing margin (slack), not the path delay.
Incorrect — Setup WNS directly determines the minimum safe clock period `T_clk,min` and therefore `f_max`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Since `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total = +0.22 ns`, the critical path takes `1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`, meaning the routed 14nm chip can run up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz` even in the slowest `0.72V SS` corner!

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (14nm Physical DRC Closure & M7 Clock Routing Rule)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 68 · 14nm Physical DRC & CTS Closure] Why did constraining Clock Tree Synthesis to metal layers `M2..M7` (`set_clock_routing_rules -net_type root -max_routing_layer M7`) eliminate the upper-metal DRC violations in standalone Synopsys IC Validator (`icv`)?
options: A) Because `M8` and `M9` are thick top-level power/global layers with wide minimum-spacing and fat-wire rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`); keeping high-fanout clock tree branches on `M2..M7` avoids wide-metal stub spacing conflicts and achieves `0 / 242` DRC errors.
B) Because `M7` has zero electrical resistance.
C) Because `icv` only checks `M1`.
D) Because `M8` is made of polysilicon.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the physical pitch and spacing rules of intermediate signal routing layers (`M2..M7`) versus top-level thick power/global distribution layers (`M8, M9`) in a 14nm FinFET BEOL stack.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In `SAED14nm`, `M8/M9` carry the PG mesh straps and enforce wide-metal spacing rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`). Restricting CTS to `M2..M7` eliminates all upper-metal stub conflicts (`0 / 242` DRC violations).
Incorrect — All copper metal layers have finite sheet resistance `R_s`.
Incorrect — Standalone `icv` evaluates all 242 foundry deck rules across FEOL (FinFET active/gate) and BEOL (`M1..M9` and vias).
Incorrect — `M8` is an upper back-end-of-line (BEOL) copper interconnect layer, not front-end polysilicon.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Routing clock nets up to `M7` leaves `M8/M9` clean for power/top routing and resolves all 242 SAED14nm deck rules with `0` violations.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Midterm Q3/Q5/Q10 — Same-Edge Hold Physics Across PVT Corners)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 68 · Advanced Multi-Corner STA Physics] Suppose a classmate sees a Hold violation (`Hold WNS = -0.08 ns`) in PrimeTime at the `ff0p88v125c` (Fast-Fast `0.88V`) corner and proposes lowering the clock frequency from `520 MHz` (`1.923 ns`) down to `250 MHz` (`4.000 ns`) to fix it. Based on Midterm Q3 & Q10, will lowering `f_clk` fix the hold violation, and what is the true physical fix?
options: A) Yes, doubling the clock period adds `+2.077 ns` to Hold Slack.

B) No! Hold is checked on the SAME rising clock edge (`Slack_hold = [t_CQ,min + t_logic,min] - [t_hold,max + t_skew]`), which does NOT contain `T_clk`! Lowering frequency has zero effect on hold slack; the true fix is inserting non-inverting delay buffers (`set_fix_hold`) on the short contamination path to increase `t_logic,min` by >= `0.08 ns`.
C) Yes, because hold violations only happen above 500 MHz.
D) No, the only fix is deleting the flip-flop.
quiz_questions.hint: Write down the Hold Slack equation from Midterm Q3 / Q5 / Q10: does the clock period `T_clk` appear anywhere in `(t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)`?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Adding `+2.077 ns` to `T_clk` increases SETUP slack by `+2.077 ns`, but changes HOLD slack by `0.000 ns`!

Correct! Because Hold checks that a launching DFF does not overwrite a capturing DFF on the SAME clock edge (`t = 0`), `T_clk` cancels out completely. Only adding minimum path delay (delay buffers via `set_fix_hold`) or reducing clock skew fixes a hold violation!
Incorrect — Even a `1 Hz` (`T_clk = 1 second`) clock will fail Hold if `t_CQ,min + t_logic,min < t_hold + t_skew` on the active clock edge!
Incorrect — Deleting pipeline flip-flops breaks the synchronous systolic architecture.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly proven in Midterm Q3, Q5, and Q10: `Slack_hold = (t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)` is independent of `T_clk`. In Fusion Compiler / PrimeTime, `set_fix_hold` inserts small delay cells along fast paths (such as direct `Rpipe` shift wires) so `Slack_hold >= 0.00 ns` across all 3 corners.

quiz_questions.q: [Page 69 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 69's combined one-liner, why do we execute `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 69's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 69's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q3/Q4/Q9 — Setup Slack & F_max Math)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 69 · STA Setup & Hold Equations] Our 14nm Motion Estimator achieves Setup WNS = `+0.22 ns` in the worst-case slow corner (`ss0p72vm40c`) at `T_clk = 1.923 ns` (520 MHz). What is the longest critical-path total arrival + setup + uncertainty time in `ss0p72vm40c`, and what is the maximum achievable clock frequency?
options: A) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns - 0.22 ns = 1.703 ns`; max frequency `f_max = 1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`.
B) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns + 0.22 ns = 2.143 ns`; max frequency = `466 MHz`.
C) Critical path total time = `0.22 ns`; max frequency = `4.5 GHz`.
D) Setup WNS does not affect maximum frequency.
quiz_questions.hint: Use the fundamental Setup Slack identity: `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total`. Solve for `T_path_total = T_clk - Slack_setup`, then compute `f_max = 1 / T_path_total`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Positive slack `+0.22 ns` means the critical path finished `0.22 ns` BEFORE the `1.923 ns` deadline (`1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`), allowing operation up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`!
Incorrect — Adding `+0.22 ns` corresponds to a NEGATIVE slack violation (`-0.22 ns`), whereas our slack is positive (`+0.22 ns`).
Incorrect — `0.22 ns` is the spare timing margin (slack), not the path delay.
Incorrect — Setup WNS directly determines the minimum safe clock period `T_clk,min` and therefore `f_max`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Since `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total = +0.22 ns`, the critical path takes `1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`, meaning the routed 14nm chip can run up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz` even in the slowest `0.72V SS` corner!

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (14nm Physical DRC Closure & M7 Clock Routing Rule)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 69 · 14nm Physical DRC & CTS Closure] Why did constraining Clock Tree Synthesis to metal layers `M2..M7` (`set_clock_routing_rules -net_type root -max_routing_layer M7`) eliminate the upper-metal DRC violations in standalone Synopsys IC Validator (`icv`)?
options: A) Because `M8` and `M9` are thick top-level power/global layers with wide minimum-spacing and fat-wire rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`); keeping high-fanout clock tree branches on `M2..M7` avoids wide-metal stub spacing conflicts and achieves `0 / 242` DRC errors.
B) Because `M7` has zero electrical resistance.
C) Because `icv` only checks `M1`.
D) Because `M8` is made of polysilicon.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the physical pitch and spacing rules of intermediate signal routing layers (`M2..M7`) versus top-level thick power/global distribution layers (`M8, M9`) in a 14nm FinFET BEOL stack.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In `SAED14nm`, `M8/M9` carry the PG mesh straps and enforce wide-metal spacing rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`). Restricting CTS to `M2..M7` eliminates all upper-metal stub conflicts (`0 / 242` DRC violations).
Incorrect — All copper metal layers have finite sheet resistance `R_s`.
Incorrect — Standalone `icv` evaluates all 242 foundry deck rules across FEOL (FinFET active/gate) and BEOL (`M1..M9` and vias).
Incorrect — `M8` is an upper back-end-of-line (BEOL) copper interconnect layer, not front-end polysilicon.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Routing clock nets up to `M7` leaves `M8/M9` clean for power/top routing and resolves all 242 SAED14nm deck rules with `0` violations.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Midterm Q3/Q5/Q10 — Same-Edge Hold Physics Across PVT Corners)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 69 · Advanced Multi-Corner STA Physics] Suppose a classmate sees a Hold violation (`Hold WNS = -0.08 ns`) in PrimeTime at the `ff0p88v125c` (Fast-Fast `0.88V`) corner and proposes lowering the clock frequency from `520 MHz` (`1.923 ns`) down to `250 MHz` (`4.000 ns`) to fix it. Based on Midterm Q3 & Q10, will lowering `f_clk` fix the hold violation, and what is the true physical fix?
options: A) Yes, doubling the clock period adds `+2.077 ns` to Hold Slack.

B) No! Hold is checked on the SAME rising clock edge (`Slack_hold = [t_CQ,min + t_logic,min] - [t_hold,max + t_skew]`), which does NOT contain `T_clk`! Lowering frequency has zero effect on hold slack; the true fix is inserting non-inverting delay buffers (`set_fix_hold`) on the short contamination path to increase `t_logic,min` by >= `0.08 ns`.
C) Yes, because hold violations only happen above 500 MHz.
D) No, the only fix is deleting the flip-flop.
quiz_questions.hint: Write down the Hold Slack equation from Midterm Q3 / Q5 / Q10: does the clock period `T_clk` appear anywhere in `(t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)`?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Adding `+2.077 ns` to `T_clk` increases SETUP slack by `+2.077 ns`, but changes HOLD slack by `0.000 ns`!

Correct! Because Hold checks that a launching DFF does not overwrite a capturing DFF on the SAME clock edge (`t = 0`), `T_clk` cancels out completely. Only adding minimum path delay (delay buffers via `set_fix_hold`) or reducing clock skew fixes a hold violation!
Incorrect — Even a `1 Hz` (`T_clk = 1 second`) clock will fail Hold if `t_CQ,min + t_logic,min < t_hold + t_skew` on the active clock edge!
Incorrect — Deleting pipeline flip-flops breaks the synchronous systolic architecture.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly proven in Midterm Q3, Q5, and Q10: `Slack_hold = (t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)` is independent of `T_clk`. In Fusion Compiler / PrimeTime, `set_fix_hold` inserts small delay cells along fast paths (such as direct `Rpipe` shift wires) so `Slack_hold >= 0.00 ns` across all 3 corners.
