quiz_questions.q: [Page 70 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 70's combined one-liner, why do we execute `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 70's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 70's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q3/Q4/Q9 — Setup Slack & F_max Math)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 70 · STA Setup & Hold Equations] Our 14nm Motion Estimator achieves Setup WNS = `+0.22 ns` in the worst-case slow corner (`ss0p72vm40c`) at `T_clk = 1.923 ns` (520 MHz). What is the longest critical-path total arrival + setup + uncertainty time in `ss0p72vm40c`, and what is the maximum achievable clock frequency?
options: A) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns - 0.22 ns = 1.703 ns`; max frequency `f_max = 1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`.
B) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns + 0.22 ns = 2.143 ns`; max frequency = `466 MHz`.
C) Critical path total time = `0.22 ns`; max frequency = `4.5 GHz`.
D) Setup WNS does not affect maximum frequency.
quiz_questions.hint: Use the fundamental Setup Slack identity: `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total`. Solve for `T_path_total = T_clk - Slack_setup`, then compute `f_max = 1 / T_path_total`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Positive slack `+0.22 ns` means the critical path finished `0.22 ns` BEFORE the `1.923 ns` deadline (`1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`), allowing operation up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`!
Incorrect — Adding `+0.22 ns` corresponds to a NEGATIVE slack violation (`-0.22 ns`), whereas our slack is positive (`+0.22 ns`).
Incorrect — `0.22 ns` is the spare timing margin (slack), not the path delay.
Incorrect — Setup WNS directly determines the minimum safe clock period `T_clk,min` and therefore `f_max`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Since `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total = +0.22 ns`, the critical path takes `1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`, meaning the routed 14nm chip can run up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz` even in the slowest `0.72V SS` corner!

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (14nm Physical DRC Closure & M7 Clock Routing Rule)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 70 · 14nm Physical DRC & CTS Closure] Why did constraining Clock Tree Synthesis to metal layers `M2..M7` (`set_clock_routing_rules -net_type root -max_routing_layer M7`) eliminate the upper-metal DRC violations in standalone Synopsys IC Validator (`icv`)?
options: A) Because `M8` and `M9` are thick top-level power/global layers with wide minimum-spacing and fat-wire rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`); keeping high-fanout clock tree branches on `M2..M7` avoids wide-metal stub spacing conflicts and achieves `0 / 242` DRC errors.
B) Because `M7` has zero electrical resistance.
C) Because `icv` only checks `M1`.
D) Because `M8` is made of polysilicon.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the physical pitch and spacing rules of intermediate signal routing layers (`M2..M7`) versus top-level thick power/global distribution layers (`M8, M9`) in a 14nm FinFET BEOL stack.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In `SAED14nm`, `M8/M9` carry the PG mesh straps and enforce wide-metal spacing rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`). Restricting CTS to `M2..M7` eliminates all upper-metal stub conflicts (`0 / 242` DRC violations).
Incorrect — All copper metal layers have finite sheet resistance `R_s`.
Incorrect — Standalone `icv` evaluates all 242 foundry deck rules across FEOL (FinFET active/gate) and BEOL (`M1..M9` and vias).
Incorrect — `M8` is an upper back-end-of-line (BEOL) copper interconnect layer, not front-end polysilicon.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Routing clock nets up to `M7` leaves `M8/M9` clean for power/top routing and resolves all 242 SAED14nm deck rules with `0` violations.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Midterm Q3/Q5/Q10 — Same-Edge Hold Physics Across PVT Corners)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 70 · Advanced Multi-Corner STA Physics] Suppose a classmate sees a Hold violation (`Hold WNS = -0.08 ns`) in PrimeTime at the `ff0p88v125c` (Fast-Fast `0.88V`) corner and proposes lowering the clock frequency from `520 MHz` (`1.923 ns`) down to `250 MHz` (`4.000 ns`) to fix it. Based on Midterm Q3 & Q10, will lowering `f_clk` fix the hold violation, and what is the true physical fix?
options: A) Yes, doubling the clock period adds `+2.077 ns` to Hold Slack.

B) No! Hold is checked on the SAME rising clock edge (`Slack_hold = [t_CQ,min + t_logic,min] - [t_hold,max + t_skew]`), which does NOT contain `T_clk`! Lowering frequency has zero effect on hold slack; the true fix is inserting non-inverting delay buffers (`set_fix_hold`) on the short contamination path to increase `t_logic,min` by >= `0.08 ns`.
C) Yes, because hold violations only happen above 500 MHz.
D) No, the only fix is deleting the flip-flop.
quiz_questions.hint: Write down the Hold Slack equation from Midterm Q3 / Q5 / Q10: does the clock period `T_clk` appear anywhere in `(t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)`?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Adding `+2.077 ns` to `T_clk` increases SETUP slack by `+2.077 ns`, but changes HOLD slack by `0.000 ns`!

Correct! Because Hold checks that a launching DFF does not overwrite a capturing DFF on the SAME clock edge (`t = 0`), `T_clk` cancels out completely. Only adding minimum path delay (delay buffers via `set_fix_hold`) or reducing clock skew fixes a hold violation!
Incorrect — Even a `1 Hz` (`T_clk = 1 second`) clock will fail Hold if `t_CQ,min + t_logic,min < t_hold + t_skew` on the active clock edge!
Incorrect — Deleting pipeline flip-flops breaks the synchronous systolic architecture.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly proven in Midterm Q3, Q5, and Q10: `Slack_hold = (t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)` is independent of `T_clk`. In Fusion Compiler / PrimeTime, `set_fix_hold` inserts small delay cells along fast paths (such as direct `Rpipe` shift wires) so `Slack_hold >= 0.00 ns` across all 3 corners.

quiz_questions.q: [Page 71 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 71's combined one-liner, why do we execute `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 71's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 71's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q3/Q4/Q9 — Setup Slack & F_max Math)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 71 · STA Setup & Hold Equations] Our 14nm Motion Estimator achieves Setup WNS = `+0.22 ns` in the worst-case slow corner (`ss0p72vm40c`) at `T_clk = 1.923 ns` (520 MHz). What is the longest critical-path total arrival + setup + uncertainty time in `ss0p72vm40c`, and what is the maximum achievable clock frequency?
options: A) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns - 0.22 ns = 1.703 ns`; max frequency `f_max = 1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`.
B) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns + 0.22 ns = 2.143 ns`; max frequency = `466 MHz`.
C) Critical path total time = `0.22 ns`; max frequency = `4.5 GHz`.
D) Setup WNS does not affect maximum frequency.
quiz_questions.hint: Use the fundamental Setup Slack identity: `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total`. Solve for `T_path_total = T_clk - Slack_setup`, then compute `f_max = 1 / T_path_total`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Positive slack `+0.22 ns` means the critical path finished `0.22 ns` BEFORE the `1.923 ns` deadline (`1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`), allowing operation up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`!
Incorrect — Adding `+0.22 ns` corresponds to a NEGATIVE slack violation (`-0.22 ns`), whereas our slack is positive (`+0.22 ns`).
Incorrect — `0.22 ns` is the spare timing margin (slack), not the path delay.
Incorrect — Setup WNS directly determines the minimum safe clock period `T_clk,min` and therefore `f_max`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Since `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total = +0.22 ns`, the critical path takes `1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`, meaning the routed 14nm chip can run up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz` even in the slowest `0.72V SS` corner!

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (14nm Physical DRC Closure & M7 Clock Routing Rule)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 71 · 14nm Physical DRC & CTS Closure] Why did constraining Clock Tree Synthesis to metal layers `M2..M7` (`set_clock_routing_rules -net_type root -max_routing_layer M7`) eliminate the upper-metal DRC violations in standalone Synopsys IC Validator (`icv`)?
options: A) Because `M8` and `M9` are thick top-level power/global layers with wide minimum-spacing and fat-wire rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`); keeping high-fanout clock tree branches on `M2..M7` avoids wide-metal stub spacing conflicts and achieves `0 / 242` DRC errors.
B) Because `M7` has zero electrical resistance.
C) Because `icv` only checks `M1`.
D) Because `M8` is made of polysilicon.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the physical pitch and spacing rules of intermediate signal routing layers (`M2..M7`) versus top-level thick power/global distribution layers (`M8, M9`) in a 14nm FinFET BEOL stack.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In `SAED14nm`, `M8/M9` carry the PG mesh straps and enforce wide-metal spacing rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`). Restricting CTS to `M2..M7` eliminates all upper-metal stub conflicts (`0 / 242` DRC violations).
Incorrect — All copper metal layers have finite sheet resistance `R_s`.
Incorrect — Standalone `icv` evaluates all 242 foundry deck rules across FEOL (FinFET active/gate) and BEOL (`M1..M9` and vias).
Incorrect — `M8` is an upper back-end-of-line (BEOL) copper interconnect layer, not front-end polysilicon.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Routing clock nets up to `M7` leaves `M8/M9` clean for power/top routing and resolves all 242 SAED14nm deck rules with `0` violations.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Midterm Q3/Q5/Q10 — Same-Edge Hold Physics Across PVT Corners)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 71 · Advanced Multi-Corner STA Physics] Suppose a classmate sees a Hold violation (`Hold WNS = -0.08 ns`) in PrimeTime at the `ff0p88v125c` (Fast-Fast `0.88V`) corner and proposes lowering the clock frequency from `520 MHz` (`1.923 ns`) down to `250 MHz` (`4.000 ns`) to fix it. Based on Midterm Q3 & Q10, will lowering `f_clk` fix the hold violation, and what is the true physical fix?
options: A) Yes, doubling the clock period adds `+2.077 ns` to Hold Slack.

B) No! Hold is checked on the SAME rising clock edge (`Slack_hold = [t_CQ,min + t_logic,min] - [t_hold,max + t_skew]`), which does NOT contain `T_clk`! Lowering frequency has zero effect on hold slack; the true fix is inserting non-inverting delay buffers (`set_fix_hold`) on the short contamination path to increase `t_logic,min` by >= `0.08 ns`.
C) Yes, because hold violations only happen above 500 MHz.
D) No, the only fix is deleting the flip-flop.
quiz_questions.hint: Write down the Hold Slack equation from Midterm Q3 / Q5 / Q10: does the clock period `T_clk` appear anywhere in `(t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)`?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Adding `+2.077 ns` to `T_clk` increases SETUP slack by `+2.077 ns`, but changes HOLD slack by `0.000 ns`!

Correct! Because Hold checks that a launching DFF does not overwrite a capturing DFF on the SAME clock edge (`t = 0`), `T_clk` cancels out completely. Only adding minimum path delay (delay buffers via `set_fix_hold`) or reducing clock skew fixes a hold violation!
Incorrect — Even a `1 Hz` (`T_clk = 1 second`) clock will fail Hold if `t_CQ,min + t_logic,min < t_hold + t_skew` on the active clock edge!
Incorrect — Deleting pipeline flip-flops breaks the synchronous systolic architecture.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly proven in Midterm Q3, Q5, and Q10: `Slack_hold = (t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)` is independent of `T_clk`. In Fusion Compiler / PrimeTime, `set_fix_hold` inserts small delay cells along fast paths (such as direct `Rpipe` shift wires) so `Slack_hold >= 0.00 ns` across all 3 corners.

quiz_questions.q: [Page 72 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 72's combined one-liner, why do we execute `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 72's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q3/Q4/Q9 — Setup Slack & F_max Math)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 72 · STA Setup & Hold Equations] Our 14nm Motion Estimator achieves Setup WNS = `+0.22 ns` in the worst-case slow corner (`ss0p72vm40c`) at `T_clk = 1.923 ns` (520 MHz). What is the longest critical-path total arrival + setup + uncertainty time in `ss0p72vm40c`, and what is the maximum achievable clock frequency?
options: A) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns - 0.22 ns = 1.703 ns`; max frequency `f_max = 1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`.
B) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns + 0.22 ns = 2.143 ns`; max frequency = `466 MHz`.
C) Critical path total time = `0.22 ns`; max frequency = `4.5 GHz`.
D) Setup WNS does not affect maximum frequency.
quiz_questions.hint: Use the fundamental Setup Slack identity: `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total`. Solve for `T_path_total = T_clk - Slack_setup`, then compute `f_max = 1 / T_path_total`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Positive slack `+0.22 ns` means the critical path finished `0.22 ns` BEFORE the `1.923 ns` deadline (`1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`), allowing operation up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`!
Incorrect — Adding `+0.22 ns` corresponds to a NEGATIVE slack violation (`-0.22 ns`), whereas our slack is positive (`+0.22 ns`).
Incorrect — `0.22 ns` is the spare timing margin (slack), not the path delay.
Incorrect — Setup WNS directly determines the minimum safe clock period `T_clk,min` and therefore `f_max`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Since `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total = +0.22 ns`, the critical path takes `1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`, meaning the routed 14nm chip can run up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz` even in the slowest `0.72V SS` corner!

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (14nm Physical DRC Closure & M7 Clock Routing Rule)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 72 · 14nm Physical DRC & CTS Closure] Why did constraining Clock Tree Synthesis to metal layers `M2..M7` (`set_clock_routing_rules -net_type root -max_routing_layer M7`) eliminate the upper-metal DRC violations in standalone Synopsys IC Validator (`icv`)?
options: A) Because `M8` and `M9` are thick top-level power/global layers with wide minimum-spacing and fat-wire rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`); keeping high-fanout clock tree branches on `M2..M7` avoids wide-metal stub spacing conflicts and achieves `0 / 242` DRC errors.
B) Because `M7` has zero electrical resistance.
C) Because `icv` only checks `M1`.
D) Because `M8` is made of polysilicon.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the physical pitch and spacing rules of intermediate signal routing layers (`M2..M7`) versus top-level thick power/global distribution layers (`M8, M9`) in a 14nm FinFET BEOL stack.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In `SAED14nm`, `M8/M9` carry the PG mesh straps and enforce wide-metal spacing rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`). Restricting CTS to `M2..M7` eliminates all upper-metal stub conflicts (`0 / 242` DRC violations).
Incorrect — All copper metal layers have finite sheet resistance `R_s`.
Incorrect — Standalone `icv` evaluates all 242 foundry deck rules across FEOL (FinFET active/gate) and BEOL (`M1..M9` and vias).
Incorrect — `M8` is an upper back-end-of-line (BEOL) copper interconnect layer, not front-end polysilicon.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Routing clock nets up to `M7` leaves `M8/M9` clean for power/top routing and resolves all 242 SAED14nm deck rules with `0` violations.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Midterm Q3/Q5/Q10 — Same-Edge Hold Physics Across PVT Corners)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 72 · Advanced Multi-Corner STA Physics] Suppose a classmate sees a Hold violation (`Hold WNS = -0.08 ns`) in PrimeTime at the `ff0p88v125c` (Fast-Fast `0.88V`) corner and proposes lowering the clock frequency from `520 MHz` (`1.923 ns`) down to `250 MHz` (`4.000 ns`) to fix it. Based on Midterm Q3 & Q10, will lowering `f_clk` fix the hold violation, and what is the true physical fix?
options: A) Yes, doubling the clock period adds `+2.077 ns` to Hold Slack.

B) No! Hold is checked on the SAME rising clock edge (`Slack_hold = [t_CQ,min + t_logic,min] - [t_hold,max + t_skew]`), which does NOT contain `T_clk`! Lowering frequency has zero effect on hold slack; the true fix is inserting non-inverting delay buffers (`set_fix_hold`) on the short contamination path to increase `t_logic,min` by >= `0.08 ns`.
C) Yes, because hold violations only happen above 500 MHz.
D) No, the only fix is deleting the flip-flop.
quiz_questions.hint: Write down the Hold Slack equation from Midterm Q3 / Q5 / Q10: does the clock period `T_clk` appear anywhere in `(t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)`?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Adding `+2.077 ns` to `T_clk` increases SETUP slack by `+2.077 ns`, but changes HOLD slack by `0.000 ns`!

Correct! Because Hold checks that a launching DFF does not overwrite a capturing DFF on the SAME clock edge (`t = 0`), `T_clk` cancels out completely. Only adding minimum path delay (delay buffers via `set_fix_hold`) or reducing clock skew fixes a hold violation!
Incorrect — Even a `1 Hz` (`T_clk = 1 second`) clock will fail Hold if `t_CQ,min + t_logic,min < t_hold + t_skew` on the active clock edge!
Incorrect — Deleting pipeline flip-flops breaks the synchronous systolic architecture.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly proven in Midterm Q3, Q5, and Q10: `Slack_hold = (t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)` is independent of `T_clk`. In Fusion Compiler / PrimeTime, `set_fix_hold` inserts small delay cells along fast paths (such as direct `Rpipe` shift wires) so `Slack_hold >= 0.00 ns` across all 3 corners.

Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 73's expected output markers.

quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q3/Q4/Q9 — Setup Slack & F_max Math)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 73 · STA Setup & Hold Equations] Our 14nm Motion Estimator achieves Setup WNS = `+0.22 ns` in the worst-case slow corner (`ss0p72vm40c`) at `T_clk = 1.923 ns` (520 MHz). What is the longest critical-path total arrival + setup + uncertainty time in `ss0p72vm40c`, and what is the maximum achievable clock frequency?
options: A) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns - 0.22 ns = 1.703 ns`; max frequency `f_max = 1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`.
B) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns + 0.22 ns = 2.143 ns`; max frequency = `466 MHz`.
C) Critical path total time = `0.22 ns`; max frequency = `4.5 GHz`.
D) Setup WNS does not affect maximum frequency.
quiz_questions.hint: Use the fundamental Setup Slack identity: `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total`. Solve for `T_path_total = T_clk - Slack_setup`, then compute `f_max = 1 / T_path_total`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Positive slack `+0.22 ns` means the critical path finished `0.22 ns` BEFORE the `1.923 ns` deadline (`1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`), allowing operation up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`!
Incorrect — Adding `+0.22 ns` corresponds to a NEGATIVE slack violation (`-0.22 ns`), whereas our slack is positive (`+0.22 ns`).
Incorrect — `0.22 ns` is the spare timing margin (slack), not the path delay.
Incorrect — Setup WNS directly determines the minimum safe clock period `T_clk,min` and therefore `f_max`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Since `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total = +0.22 ns`, the critical path takes `1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`, meaning the routed 14nm chip can run up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz` even in the slowest `0.72V SS` corner!

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (14nm Physical DRC Closure & M7 Clock Routing Rule)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 73 · 14nm Physical DRC & CTS Closure] Why did constraining Clock Tree Synthesis to metal layers `M2..M7` (`set_clock_routing_rules -net_type root -max_routing_layer M7`) eliminate the upper-metal DRC violations in standalone Synopsys IC Validator (`icv`)?
options: A) Because `M8` and `M9` are thick top-level power/global layers with wide minimum-spacing and fat-wire rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`); keeping high-fanout clock tree branches on `M2..M7` avoids wide-metal stub spacing conflicts and achieves `0 / 242` DRC errors.
B) Because `M7` has zero electrical resistance.
C) Because `icv` only checks `M1`.
D) Because `M8` is made of polysilicon.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the physical pitch and spacing rules of intermediate signal routing layers (`M2..M7`) versus top-level thick power/global distribution layers (`M8, M9`) in a 14nm FinFET BEOL stack.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In `SAED14nm`, `M8/M9` carry the PG mesh straps and enforce wide-metal spacing rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`). Restricting CTS to `M2..M7` eliminates all upper-metal stub conflicts (`0 / 242` DRC violations).
Incorrect — All copper metal layers have finite sheet resistance `R_s`.
Incorrect — Standalone `icv` evaluates all 242 foundry deck rules across FEOL (FinFET active/gate) and BEOL (`M1..M9` and vias).
Incorrect — `M8` is an upper back-end-of-line (BEOL) copper interconnect layer, not front-end polysilicon.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Routing clock nets up to `M7` leaves `M8/M9` clean for power/top routing and resolves all 242 SAED14nm deck rules with `0` violations.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Midterm Q3/Q5/Q10 — Same-Edge Hold Physics Across PVT Corners)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 73 · Advanced Multi-Corner STA Physics] Suppose a classmate sees a Hold violation (`Hold WNS = -0.08 ns`) in PrimeTime at the `ff0p88v125c` (Fast-Fast `0.88V`) corner and proposes lowering the clock frequency from `520 MHz` (`1.923 ns`) down to `250 MHz` (`4.000 ns`) to fix it. Based on Midterm Q3 & Q10, will lowering `f_clk` fix the hold violation, and what is the true physical fix?
options: A) Yes, doubling the clock period adds `+2.077 ns` to Hold Slack.

B) No! Hold is checked on the SAME rising clock edge (`Slack_hold = [t_CQ,min + t_logic,min] - [t_hold,max + t_skew]`), which does NOT contain `T_clk`! Lowering frequency has zero effect on hold slack; the true fix is inserting non-inverting delay buffers (`set_fix_hold`) on the short contamination path to increase `t_logic,min` by >= `0.08 ns`.
C) Yes, because hold violations only happen above 500 MHz.
D) No, the only fix is deleting the flip-flop.
quiz_questions.hint: Write down the Hold Slack equation from Midterm Q3 / Q5 / Q10: does the clock period `T_clk` appear anywhere in `(t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)`?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Adding `+2.077 ns` to `T_clk` increases SETUP slack by `+2.077 ns`, but changes HOLD slack by `0.000 ns`!

Correct! Because Hold checks that a launching DFF does not overwrite a capturing DFF on the SAME clock edge (`t = 0`), `T_clk` cancels out completely. Only adding minimum path delay (delay buffers via `set_fix_hold`) or reducing clock skew fixes a hold violation!
Incorrect — Even a `1 Hz` (`T_clk = 1 second`) clock will fail Hold if `t_CQ,min + t_logic,min < t_hold + t_skew` on the active clock edge!
Incorrect — Deleting pipeline flip-flops breaks the synchronous systolic architecture.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly proven in Midterm Q3, Q5, and Q10: `Slack_hold = (t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)` is independent of `T_clk`. In Fusion Compiler / PrimeTime, `set_fix_hold` inserts small delay cells along fast paths (such as direct `Rpipe` shift wires) so `Slack_hold >= 0.00 ns` across all 3 corners.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Midterm Q3/Q4/Q9 — Setup Slack & F_max Math)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 74 · STA Setup & Hold Equations] Our 14nm Motion Estimator achieves Setup WNS = `+0.22 ns` in the worst-case slow corner (`ss0p72vm40c`) at `T_clk = 1.923 ns` (520 MHz). What is the longest critical-path total arrival + setup + uncertainty time in `ss0p72vm40c`, and what is the maximum achievable clock frequency?
options: A) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns - 0.22 ns = 1.703 ns`; max frequency `f_max = 1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`.
B) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns + 0.22 ns = 2.143 ns`; max frequency = `466 MHz`.
C) Critical path total time = `0.22 ns`; max frequency = `4.5 GHz`.
D) Setup WNS does not affect maximum frequency.
quiz_questions.hint: Use the fundamental Setup Slack identity: `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total`. Solve for `T_path_total = T_clk - Slack_setup`, then compute `f_max = 1 / T_path_total`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Positive slack `+0.22 ns` means the critical path finished `0.22 ns` BEFORE the `1.923 ns` deadline (`1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`), allowing operation up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`!
Incorrect — Adding `+0.22 ns` corresponds to a NEGATIVE slack violation (`-0.22 ns`), whereas our slack is positive (`+0.22 ns`).
Incorrect — `0.22 ns` is the spare timing margin (slack), not the path delay.
Incorrect — Setup WNS directly determines the minimum safe clock period `T_clk,min` and therefore `f_max`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Since `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total = +0.22 ns`, the critical path takes `1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`, meaning the routed 14nm chip can run up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz` even in the slowest `0.72V SS` corner!

options: A) Because `M8` and `M9` are thick top-level power/global layers with wide minimum-spacing and fat-wire rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`); keeping high-fanout clock tree branches on `M2..M7` avoids wide-metal stub spacing conflicts and achieves `0 / 242` DRC errors.
B) Because `M7` has zero electrical resistance.
C) Because `icv` only checks `M1`.
D) Because `M8` is made of polysilicon.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the physical pitch and spacing rules of intermediate signal routing layers (`M2..M7`) versus top-level thick power/global distribution layers (`M8, M9`) in a 14nm FinFET BEOL stack.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In `SAED14nm`, `M8/M9` carry the PG mesh straps and enforce wide-metal spacing rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`). Restricting CTS to `M2..M7` eliminates all upper-metal stub conflicts (`0 / 242` DRC violations).
Incorrect — All copper metal layers have finite sheet resistance `R_s`.
Incorrect — Standalone `icv` evaluates all 242 foundry deck rules across FEOL (FinFET active/gate) and BEOL (`M1..M9` and vias).
Incorrect — `M8` is an upper back-end-of-line (BEOL) copper interconnect layer, not front-end polysilicon.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Midterm Q3/Q5/Q10 — Same-Edge Hold Physics Across PVT Corners)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 74 · Advanced Multi-Corner STA Physics] Suppose a classmate sees a Hold violation (`Hold WNS = -0.08 ns`) in PrimeTime at the `ff0p88v125c` (Fast-Fast `0.88V`) corner and proposes lowering the clock frequency from `520 MHz` (`1.923 ns`) down to `250 MHz` (`4.000 ns`) to fix it. Based on Midterm Q3 & Q10, will lowering `f_clk` fix the hold violation, and what is the true physical fix?
options: A) Yes, doubling the clock period adds `+2.077 ns` to Hold Slack.

B) No! Hold is checked on the SAME rising clock edge (`Slack_hold = [t_CQ,min + t_logic,min] - [t_hold,max + t_skew]`), which does NOT contain `T_clk`! Lowering frequency has zero effect on hold slack; the true fix is inserting non-inverting delay buffers (`set_fix_hold`) on the short contamination path to increase `t_logic,min` by >= `0.08 ns`.
C) Yes, because hold violations only happen above 500 MHz.
D) No, the only fix is deleting the flip-flop.
quiz_questions.hint: Write down the Hold Slack equation from Midterm Q3 / Q5 / Q10: does the clock period `T_clk` appear anywhere in `(t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)`?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Adding `+2.077 ns` to `T_clk` increases SETUP slack by `+2.077 ns`, but changes HOLD slack by `0.000 ns`!

Correct! Because Hold checks that a launching DFF does not overwrite a capturing DFF on the SAME clock edge (`t = 0`), `T_clk` cancels out completely. Only adding minimum path delay (delay buffers via `set_fix_hold`) or reducing clock skew fixes a hold violation!
Incorrect — Even a `1 Hz` (`T_clk = 1 second`) clock will fail Hold if `t_CQ,min + t_logic,min < t_hold + t_skew` on the active clock edge!
Incorrect — Deleting pipeline flip-flops breaks the synchronous systolic architecture.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly proven in Midterm Q3, Q5, and Q10: `Slack_hold = (t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)` is independent of `T_clk`. In Fusion Compiler / PrimeTime, `set_fix_hold` inserts small delay cells along fast paths (such as direct `Rpipe` shift wires) so `Slack_hold >= 0.00 ns` across all 3 corners.

quiz_questions.q: [Page 75 · STA Setup & Hold Equations] Our 14nm Motion Estimator achieves Setup WNS = `+0.22 ns` in the worst-case slow corner (`ss0p72vm40c`) at `T_clk = 1.923 ns` (520 MHz). options: A) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns - 0.22 ns = 1.703 ns`; max frequency `f_max = 1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`.
B) Critical path total time = `1.923 ns + 0.22 ns = 2.143 ns`; max frequency = `466 MHz`.
C) Critical path total time = `0.22 ns`; max frequency = `4.5 GHz`.
D) Setup WNS does not affect maximum frequency.
quiz_questions.hint: Use the fundamental Setup Slack identity: `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total`. Solve for `T_path_total = T_clk - Slack_setup`, then compute `f_max = 1 / T_path_total`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Positive slack `+0.22 ns` means the critical path finished `0.22 ns` BEFORE the `1.923 ns` deadline (`1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`), allowing operation up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`!
Incorrect — Adding `+0.22 ns` corresponds to a NEGATIVE slack violation (`-0.22 ns`), whereas our slack is positive (`+0.22 ns`).
Incorrect — `0.22 ns` is the spare timing margin (slack), not the path delay.
Incorrect — Setup WNS directly determines the minimum safe clock period `T_clk,min` and therefore `f_max`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Since `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total = +0.22 ns`, the critical path takes `1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`, meaning the routed 14nm chip can run up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz` even in the slowest `0.72V SS` corner!

quiz_questions.q: [Page 75 · 14nm Physical DRC & CTS Closure] Why did constraining Clock Tree Synthesis to metal layers `M2..M7` (`set_clock_routing_rules -net_type root -max_routing_layer M7`) eliminate the upper-metal DRC violations in standalone Synopsys IC Validator (`icv`)?
options: A) Because `M8` and `M9` are thick top-level power/global layers with wide minimum-spacing and fat-wire rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`); keeping high-fanout clock tree branches on `M2..M7` avoids wide-metal stub spacing conflicts and achieves `0 / 242` DRC errors.
B) Because `M7` has zero electrical resistance.
C) Because `icv` only checks `M1`.
D) Because `M8` is made of polysilicon.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the physical pitch and spacing rules of intermediate signal routing layers (`M2..M7`) versus top-level thick power/global distribution layers (`M8, M9`) in a 14nm FinFET BEOL stack.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In `SAED14nm`, `M8/M9` carry the PG mesh straps and enforce wide-metal spacing rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`). Restricting CTS to `M2..M7` eliminates all upper-metal stub conflicts (`0 / 242` DRC violations).
Incorrect — All copper metal layers have finite sheet resistance `R_s`.
Incorrect — Standalone `icv` evaluates all 242 foundry deck rules across FEOL (FinFET active/gate) and BEOL (`M1..M9` and vias).
Incorrect — `M8` is an upper back-end-of-line (BEOL) copper interconnect layer, not front-end polysilicon.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Routing clock nets up to `M7` leaves `M8/M9` clean for power/top routing and resolves all 242 SAED14nm deck rules with `0` violations.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Midterm Q3/Q5/Q10 — Same-Edge Hold Physics Across PVT Corners)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 75 · Advanced Multi-Corner STA Physics] Suppose a classmate sees a Hold violation (`Hold WNS = -0.08 ns`) in PrimeTime at the `ff0p88v125c` (Fast-Fast `0.88V`) corner and proposes lowering the clock frequency from `520 MHz` (`1.923 ns`) down to `250 MHz` (`4.000 ns`) to fix it. Based on Midterm Q3 & Q10, will lowering `f_clk` fix the hold violation, and what is the true physical fix?
options: A) Yes, doubling the clock period adds `+2.077 ns` to Hold Slack.

B) No! Hold is checked on the SAME rising clock edge (`Slack_hold = [t_CQ,min + t_logic,min] - [t_hold,max + t_skew]`), which does NOT contain `T_clk`! Lowering frequency has zero effect on hold slack; the true fix is inserting non-inverting delay buffers (`set_fix_hold`) on the short contamination path to increase `t_logic,min` by >= `0.08 ns`.
C) Yes, because hold violations only happen above 500 MHz.
D) No, the only fix is deleting the flip-flop.
quiz_questions.hint: Write down the Hold Slack equation from Midterm Q3 / Q5 / Q10: does the clock period `T_clk` appear anywhere in `(t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)`?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Adding `+2.077 ns` to `T_clk` increases SETUP slack by `+2.077 ns`, but changes HOLD slack by `0.000 ns`!

Correct! Because Hold checks that a launching DFF does not overwrite a capturing DFF on the SAME clock edge (`t = 0`), `T_clk` cancels out completely. Only adding minimum path delay (delay buffers via `set_fix_hold`) or reducing clock skew fixes a hold violation!
Incorrect — Even a `1 Hz` (`T_clk = 1 second`) clock will fail Hold if `t_CQ,min + t_logic,min < t_hold + t_skew` on the active clock edge!
Incorrect — Deleting pipeline flip-flops breaks the synchronous systolic architecture.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly proven in Midterm Q3, Q5, and Q10: `Slack_hold = (t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)` is independent of `T_clk`. In Fusion Compiler / PrimeTime, `set_fix_hold` inserts small delay cells along fast paths (such as direct `Rpipe` shift wires) so `Slack_hold >= 0.00 ns` across all 3 corners.

C) Critical path total time = `0.22 ns`; max frequency = `4.5 GHz`.
D) Setup WNS does not affect maximum frequency.
quiz_questions.hint: Use the fundamental Setup Slack identity: `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total`. Solve for `T_path_total = T_clk - Slack_setup`, then compute `f_max = 1 / T_path_total`.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Positive slack `+0.22 ns` means the critical path finished `0.22 ns` BEFORE the `1.923 ns` deadline (`1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`), allowing operation up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz`!
Incorrect — Adding `+0.22 ns` corresponds to a NEGATIVE slack violation (`-0.22 ns`), whereas our slack is positive (`+0.22 ns`).
Incorrect — `0.22 ns` is the spare timing margin (slack), not the path delay.
Incorrect — Setup WNS directly determines the minimum safe clock period `T_clk,min` and therefore `f_max`.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Since `Slack_setup = T_clk - T_path_total = +0.22 ns`, the critical path takes `1.923 - 0.22 = 1.703 ns`, meaning the routed 14nm chip can run up to `1 / 1.703 ns = 587.2 MHz` even in the slowest `0.72V SS` corner!

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (14nm Physical DRC Closure & M7 Clock Routing Rule)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 76 · 14nm Physical DRC & CTS Closure] Why did constraining Clock Tree Synthesis to metal layers `M2..M7` (`set_clock_routing_rules -net_type root -max_routing_layer M7`) eliminate the upper-metal DRC violations in standalone Synopsys IC Validator (`icv`)?
options: A) Because `M8` and `M9` are thick top-level power/global layers with wide minimum-spacing and fat-wire rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`); keeping high-fanout clock tree branches on `M2..M7` avoids wide-metal stub spacing conflicts and achieves `0 / 242` DRC errors.
B) Because `M7` has zero electrical resistance.
C) Because `icv` only checks `M1`.
D) Because `M8` is made of polysilicon.
quiz_questions.hint: Compare the physical pitch and spacing rules of intermediate signal routing layers (`M2..M7`) versus top-level thick power/global distribution layers (`M8, M9`) in a 14nm FinFET BEOL stack.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In `SAED14nm`, `M8/M9` carry the PG mesh straps and enforce wide-metal spacing rules (`M8.S.6`, `M9.S.6`). Restricting CTS to `M2..M7` eliminates all upper-metal stub conflicts (`0 / 242` DRC violations).
Incorrect — All copper metal layers have finite sheet resistance `R_s`.
Incorrect — Standalone `icv` evaluates all 242 foundry deck rules across FEOL (FinFET active/gate) and BEOL (`M1..M9` and vias).
Incorrect — `M8` is an upper back-end-of-line (BEOL) copper interconnect layer, not front-end polysilicon.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Routing clock nets up to `M7` leaves `M8/M9` clean for power/top routing and resolves all 242 SAED14nm deck rules with `0` violations.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (Midterm Q3/Q5/Q10 — Same-Edge Hold Physics Across PVT Corners)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 76 · Advanced Multi-Corner STA Physics] Suppose a classmate sees a Hold violation (`Hold WNS = -0.08 ns`) in PrimeTime at the `ff0p88v125c` (Fast-Fast `0.88V`) corner and proposes lowering the clock frequency from `520 MHz` (`1.923 ns`) down to `250 MHz` (`4.000 ns`) to fix it. Based on Midterm Q3 & Q10, will lowering `f_clk` fix the hold violation, and what is the true physical fix?
options: A) Yes, doubling the clock period adds `+2.077 ns` to Hold Slack.

B) No! Hold is checked on the SAME rising clock edge (`Slack_hold = [t_CQ,min + t_logic,min] - [t_hold,max + t_skew]`), which does NOT contain `T_clk`! Lowering frequency has zero effect on hold slack; the true fix is inserting non-inverting delay buffers (`set_fix_hold`) on the short contamination path to increase `t_logic,min` by >= `0.08 ns`.
C) Yes, because hold violations only happen above 500 MHz.
D) No, the only fix is deleting the flip-flop.
quiz_questions.hint: Write down the Hold Slack equation from Midterm Q3 / Q5 / Q10: does the clock period `T_clk` appear anywhere in `(t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)`?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Adding `+2.077 ns` to `T_clk` increases SETUP slack by `+2.077 ns`, but changes HOLD slack by `0.000 ns`!

Correct! Because Hold checks that a launching DFF does not overwrite a capturing DFF on the SAME clock edge (`t = 0`), `T_clk` cancels out completely. Only adding minimum path delay (delay buffers via `set_fix_hold`) or reducing clock skew fixes a hold violation!
Incorrect — Even a `1 Hz` (`T_clk = 1 second`) clock will fail Hold if `t_CQ,min + t_logic,min < t_hold + t_skew` on the active clock edge!
Incorrect — Deleting pipeline flip-flops breaks the synchronous systolic architecture.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Directly proven in Midterm Q3, Q5, and Q10: `Slack_hold = (t_CQ,min + t_logic,min) - (t_hold,max + t_skew)` is independent of `T_clk`. In Fusion Compiler / PrimeTime, `set_fix_hold` inserts small delay cells along fast paths (such as direct `Rpipe` shift wires) so `Slack_hold >= 0.00 ns` across all 3 corners.

options: A) 520 MHz (1.923 ns), 16-bit SAD (0000 / 0100 / FF00 all PASS), SAED14nm 125.07 x 62.80 um (7,854.4 um^2), 8,230 cells (449 FFs, 0 SRAMs), 0/242 ICV DRC, 0 LVS errors, 3-Corner PrimeTime Setup WNS +0.71/+0.54/+0.22 ns & Hold WNS 0.00 ns.
B) 100 MHz (10 ns), 8-bit SAD (saturates at 8'hFF), 2 SRAM macros, 14 DRC errors.
C) 400 MHz (2.5 ns), Setup slack -90 ps, Hold slack -820 ps.
D) 50 MHz (20 ns), 3 flip-flops, 1 ns hold violation.
quiz_questions.hint: Cross-check the target clock (`520 MHz`), the 3 directed testbench SAD hex values (`0000`, `0100`, `FF00`), the die size (`125.07 x 62.80 um`), and the 3-corner PrimeTime slacks (`+0.71 / +0.54 / +0.22 ns`).
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Option A lists the exact verified V9 sign-off metrics across RTL simulation, Fusion Compiler 14nm P&R, IC Validator DRC/LVS, and PrimeTime 3-corner STA.
Incorrect — Option B describes the unoptimized 8-bit baseline with DRC errors.
Incorrect — Option C lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 9 & 10 (`400 MHz`, `-90 ps` setup slack, `-820 ps` hold slack).
Incorrect — Option D lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 4 & 5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold slack).
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Option A is our exact V9 sign-off specification; Option C is Midterm Q9/Q10 (`-90 ps` setup, `-820 ps` hold at 400 MHz), and Option D is Midterm Q4/Q5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold violation).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (8-Bit vs. 16-Bit PPA Trade-Off Analysis)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 77 · Advanced PPA (Power, Performance, Area) Trade-Off] Upgrading the Motion Estimator from the 8-bit saturating baseline to the 16-bit full-precision architecture doubled the accumulator/comparator datapath width (`8 -> 16 bits`), increasing standard-cell area by ~2.5x and dynamic power to `0.890 mW` at `520 MHz`. Why is this area/power investment mandatory in a real H.264/HEVC video encoder ASIC?
options: A) Because an 8-bit SAD accumulator saturates at `255 (8'hFF)` whenever average pixel difference exceeds `1.0 LSB` (`256 * 1 = 256 > 255`), blinding the motion estimator on 99%+ of real natural video macroblocks and causing catastrophic motion-vector misprediction and video compression bloat!
B) Because 16-bit registers use zero power.
C) Because 8-bit wires cannot be routed in 14nm.
D) Because 16-bit logic runs at twice the clock period.
quiz_questions.hint: Consider what happens to video compression bit-rate if a motion estimator cannot tell the difference between a candidate with SAD = 256 (`1 LSB/pixel` error) and a candidate with SAD = 65,280 (`255 LSB/pixel` error)!
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In real video frames, almost every candidate block has an average pixel difference `> 1 LSB` (`SAD > 255`). An 8-bit accumulator clips all of them to `255 (0xFF)`, making true motion estimation impossible. Investing `3,416 um^2` (`< 0.004 mm^2`) in 14nm silicon restores 100% mathematical accuracy (`0..65,280`) while still closing `520 MHz` (`+0.22 ns` SS slack)!
Incorrect — Doubling register count increases switching capacitance `C_eff`, raising dynamic power `P = alpha * C * V^2 * f`.
Incorrect — Both 8-bit and 16-bit netlists route cleanly (`0/242 DRC`).
Incorrect — Both designs meet the exact same `520 MHz (1.923 ns)` clock period.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Without 16-bit SAD precision, any macroblock candidate with total distortion `>= 255` saturates to `0xFF`, destroying the comparator's ability to find the true minimum-distortion motion vector `(motionX, motionY)`.

quiz_questions.q: [Page 78 · Advanced PPA (Power, Performance, Area) Trade-Off] Upgrading the Motion Estimator from the 8-bit saturating baseline to the 16-bit full-precision architecture doubled the accumulator/comparator datapath width (`8 -> 16 bits`), increasing standard-cell area by ~2.5x and dynamic power to `0.890 mW` at `520 MHz`. Why is this area/power investment mandatory in a real H.264/HEVC video encoder ASIC?
options: A) Because an 8-bit SAD accumulator saturates at `255 (8'hFF)` whenever average pixel difference exceeds `1.0 LSB` (`256 * 1 = 256 > 255`), blinding the motion estimator on 99%+ of real natural video macroblocks and causing catastrophic motion-vector misprediction and video compression bloat!
B) Because 16-bit registers use zero power.
C) Because 8-bit wires cannot be routed in 14nm.
D) Because 16-bit logic runs at twice the clock period.
quiz_questions.hint: Consider what happens to video compression bit-rate if a motion estimator cannot tell the difference between a candidate with SAD = 256 (`1 LSB/pixel` error) and a candidate with SAD = 65,280 (`255 LSB/pixel` error)!
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In real video frames, almost every candidate block has an average pixel difference `> 1 LSB` (`SAD > 255`). An 8-bit accumulator clips all of them to `255 (0xFF)`, making true motion estimation impossible. Investing `3,416 um^2` (`< 0.004 mm^2`) in 14nm silicon restores 100% mathematical accuracy (`0..65,280`) while still closing `520 MHz` (`+0.22 ns` SS slack)!
Incorrect — Doubling register count increases switching capacitance `C_eff`, raising dynamic power `P = alpha * C * V^2 * f`.
Incorrect — Both 8-bit and 16-bit netlists route cleanly (`0/242 DRC`).
Incorrect — Both designs meet the exact same `520 MHz (1.923 ns)` clock period.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Without 16-bit SAD precision, any macroblock candidate with total distortion `>= 255` saturates to `0xFF`, destroying the comparator's ability to find the true minimum-distortion motion vector `(motionX, motionY)`.

quiz_questions.q: [Page 81 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 81's combined one-liner, why do we execute `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 81's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 81's `required_markers`.

options: A) 520 MHz (1.923 ns), 16-bit SAD (0000 / 0100 / FF00 all PASS), SAED14nm 125.07 x 62.80 um (7,854.4 um^2), 8,230 cells (449 FFs, 0 SRAMs), 0/242 ICV DRC, 0 LVS errors, 3-Corner PrimeTime Setup WNS +0.71/+0.54/+0.22 ns & Hold WNS 0.00 ns.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (8-Bit vs. 16-Bit PPA Trade-Off Analysis)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 81 · Advanced PPA (Power, Performance, Area) Trade-Off] Upgrading the Motion Estimator from the 8-bit saturating baseline to the 16-bit full-precision architecture doubled the accumulator/comparator datapath width (`8 -> 16 bits`), increasing standard-cell area by ~2.5x and dynamic power to `0.890 mW` at `520 MHz`. Why is this area/power investment mandatory in a real H.264/HEVC video encoder ASIC?
options: A) Because an 8-bit SAD accumulator saturates at `255 (8'hFF)` whenever average pixel difference exceeds `1.0 LSB` (`256 * 1 = 256 > 255`), blinding the motion estimator on 99%+ of real natural video macroblocks and causing catastrophic motion-vector misprediction and video compression bloat!
B) Because 16-bit registers use zero power.
C) Because 8-bit wires cannot be routed in 14nm.
D) Because 16-bit logic runs at twice the clock period.
quiz_questions.hint: Consider what happens to video compression bit-rate if a motion estimator cannot tell the difference between a candidate with SAD = 256 (`1 LSB/pixel` error) and a candidate with SAD = 65,280 (`255 LSB/pixel` error)!
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In real video frames, almost every candidate block has an average pixel difference `> 1 LSB` (`SAD > 255`). An 8-bit accumulator clips all of them to `255 (0xFF)`, making true motion estimation impossible. Investing `3,416 um^2` (`< 0.004 mm^2`) in 14nm silicon restores 100% mathematical accuracy (`0..65,280`) while still closing `520 MHz` (`+0.22 ns` SS slack)!
Incorrect — Doubling register count increases switching capacitance `C_eff`, raising dynamic power `P = alpha * C * V^2 * f`.
Incorrect — Both 8-bit and 16-bit netlists route cleanly (`0/242 DRC`).
Incorrect — Both designs meet the exact same `520 MHz (1.923 ns)` clock period.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Without 16-bit SAD precision, any macroblock candidate with total distortion `>= 255` saturates to `0xFF`, destroying the comparator's ability to find the true minimum-distortion motion vector `(motionX, motionY)`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 82 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 82's combined one-liner, why do we execute `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 82's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 82's `required_markers`.

options: A) 520 MHz (1.923 ns), 16-bit SAD (0000 / 0100 / FF00 all PASS), SAED14nm 125.07 x 62.80 um (7,854.4 um^2), 8,230 cells (449 FFs, 0 SRAMs), 0/242 ICV DRC, 0 LVS errors, 3-Corner PrimeTime Setup WNS +0.71/+0.54/+0.22 ns & Hold WNS 0.00 ns.

Incorrect — Option B describes the unoptimized 8-bit baseline with DRC errors.

quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Option A is our exact V9 sign-off specification; Option C is Midterm Q9/Q10 (`-90 ps` setup, `-820 ps` hold at 400 MHz), and Option D is Midterm Q4/Q5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold violation).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (8-Bit vs. 16-Bit PPA Trade-Off Analysis)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 82 · Advanced PPA (Power, Performance, Area) Trade-Off] Upgrading the Motion Estimator from the 8-bit saturating baseline to the 16-bit full-precision architecture doubled the accumulator/comparator datapath width (`8 -> 16 bits`), increasing standard-cell area by ~2.5x and dynamic power to `0.890 mW` at `520 MHz`. Why is this area/power investment mandatory in a real H.264/HEVC video encoder ASIC?
options: A) Because an 8-bit SAD accumulator saturates at `255 (8'hFF)` whenever average pixel difference exceeds `1.0 LSB` (`256 * 1 = 256 > 255`), blinding the motion estimator on 99%+ of real natural video macroblocks and causing catastrophic motion-vector misprediction and video compression bloat!
B) Because 16-bit registers use zero power.
C) Because 8-bit wires cannot be routed in 14nm.
D) Because 16-bit logic runs at twice the clock period.
quiz_questions.hint: Consider what happens to video compression bit-rate if a motion estimator cannot tell the difference between a candidate with SAD = 256 (`1 LSB/pixel` error) and a candidate with SAD = 65,280 (`255 LSB/pixel` error)!
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In real video frames, almost every candidate block has an average pixel difference `> 1 LSB` (`SAD > 255`). An 8-bit accumulator clips all of them to `255 (0xFF)`, making true motion estimation impossible. Investing `3,416 um^2` (`< 0.004 mm^2`) in 14nm silicon restores 100% mathematical accuracy (`0..65,280`) while still closing `520 MHz` (`+0.22 ns` SS slack)!
Incorrect — Doubling register count increases switching capacitance `C_eff`, raising dynamic power `P = alpha * C * V^2 * f`.
Incorrect — Both 8-bit and 16-bit netlists route cleanly (`0/242 DRC`).
Incorrect — Both designs meet the exact same `520 MHz (1.923 ns)` clock period.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Without 16-bit SAD precision, any macroblock candidate with total distortion `>= 255` saturates to `0xFF`, destroying the comparator's ability to find the true minimum-distortion motion vector `(motionX, motionY)`.

quiz_questions.q: [Page 83 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 83's combined one-liner, why do we execute `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 83's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 83's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.q: [Page 83 · End-to-End V1->V9 Mastery Check] Which complete set of metrics summarizes our signed-off V9 16-Bit Motion Estimator ASIC?
options: A) 520 MHz (1.923 ns), 16-bit SAD (0000 / 0100 / FF00 all PASS), SAED14nm 125.07 x 62.80 um (7,854.4 um^2), 8,230 cells (449 FFs, 0 SRAMs), 0/242 ICV DRC, 0 LVS errors, 3-Corner PrimeTime Setup WNS +0.71/+0.54/+0.22 ns & Hold WNS 0.00 ns.
B) 100 MHz (10 ns), 8-bit SAD (saturates at 8'hFF), 2 SRAM macros, 14 DRC errors.
C) 400 MHz (2.5 ns), Setup slack -90 ps, Hold slack -820 ps.
D) 50 MHz (20 ns), 3 flip-flops, 1 ns hold violation.
quiz_questions.hint: Cross-check the target clock (`520 MHz`), the 3 directed testbench SAD hex values (`0000`, `0100`, `FF00`), the die size (`125.07 x 62.80 um`), and the 3-corner PrimeTime slacks (`+0.71 / +0.54 / +0.22 ns`).
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Option A lists the exact verified V9 sign-off metrics across RTL simulation, Fusion Compiler 14nm P&R, IC Validator DRC/LVS, and PrimeTime 3-corner STA.
Incorrect — Option B describes the unoptimized 8-bit baseline with DRC errors.
Incorrect — Option C lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 9 & 10 (`400 MHz`, `-90 ps` setup slack, `-820 ps` hold slack).
Incorrect — Option D lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 4 & 5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold slack).
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Option A is our exact V9 sign-off specification; Option C is Midterm Q9/Q10 (`-90 ps` setup, `-820 ps` hold at 400 MHz), and Option D is Midterm Q4/Q5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold violation).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (8-Bit vs. 16-Bit PPA Trade-Off Analysis)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 83 · Advanced PPA (Power, Performance, Area) Trade-Off] Upgrading the Motion Estimator from the 8-bit saturating baseline to the 16-bit full-precision architecture doubled the accumulator/comparator datapath width (`8 -> 16 bits`), increasing standard-cell area by ~2.5x and dynamic power to `0.890 mW` at `520 MHz`. Why is this area/power investment mandatory in a real H.264/HEVC video encoder ASIC?
options: A) Because an 8-bit SAD accumulator saturates at `255 (8'hFF)` whenever average pixel difference exceeds `1.0 LSB` (`256 * 1 = 256 > 255`), blinding the motion estimator on 99%+ of real natural video macroblocks and causing catastrophic motion-vector misprediction and video compression bloat!
B) Because 16-bit registers use zero power.
C) Because 8-bit wires cannot be routed in 14nm.
D) Because 16-bit logic runs at twice the clock period.
quiz_questions.hint: Consider what happens to video compression bit-rate if a motion estimator cannot tell the difference between a candidate with SAD = 256 (`1 LSB/pixel` error) and a candidate with SAD = 65,280 (`255 LSB/pixel` error)!
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In real video frames, almost every candidate block has an average pixel difference `> 1 LSB` (`SAD > 255`). An 8-bit accumulator clips all of them to `255 (0xFF)`, making true motion estimation impossible. Investing `3,416 um^2` (`< 0.004 mm^2`) in 14nm silicon restores 100% mathematical accuracy (`0..65,280`) while still closing `520 MHz` (`+0.22 ns` SS slack)!
Incorrect — Doubling register count increases switching capacitance `C_eff`, raising dynamic power `P = alpha * C * V^2 * f`.
Incorrect — Both 8-bit and 16-bit netlists route cleanly (`0/242 DRC`).
Incorrect — Both designs meet the exact same `520 MHz (1.923 ns)` clock period.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Without 16-bit SAD precision, any macroblock candidate with total distortion `>= 255` saturates to `0xFF`, destroying the comparator's ability to find the true minimum-distortion motion vector `(motionX, motionY)`.

quiz_questions.q: [Page 84 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 84's combined one-liner, why do we execute `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 84's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 84's `required_markers`.

options: A) 520 MHz (1.923 ns), 16-bit SAD (0000 / 0100 / FF00 all PASS), SAED14nm 125.07 x 62.80 um (7,854.4 um^2), 8,230 cells (449 FFs, 0 SRAMs), 0/242 ICV DRC, 0 LVS errors, 3-Corner PrimeTime Setup WNS +0.71/+0.54/+0.22 ns & Hold WNS 0.00 ns.
B) 100 MHz (10 ns), 8-bit SAD (saturates at 8'hFF), 2 SRAM macros, 14 DRC errors.

D) 50 MHz (20 ns), 3 flip-flops, 1 ns hold violation.
quiz_questions.hint: Cross-check the target clock (`520 MHz`), the 3 directed testbench SAD hex values (`0000`, `0100`, `FF00`), the die size (`125.07 x 62.80 um`), and the 3-corner PrimeTime slacks (`+0.71 / +0.54 / +0.22 ns`).
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Option A lists the exact verified V9 sign-off metrics across RTL simulation, Fusion Compiler 14nm P&R, IC Validator DRC/LVS, and PrimeTime 3-corner STA.
Incorrect — Option B describes the unoptimized 8-bit baseline with DRC errors.

quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Option A is our exact V9 sign-off specification; Option C is Midterm Q9/Q10 (`-90 ps` setup, `-820 ps` hold at 400 MHz), and Option D is Midterm Q4/Q5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold violation).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (8-Bit vs. 16-Bit PPA Trade-Off Analysis)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 84 · Advanced PPA (Power, Performance, Area) Trade-Off] Upgrading the Motion Estimator from the 8-bit saturating baseline to the 16-bit full-precision architecture doubled the accumulator/comparator datapath width (`8 -> 16 bits`), increasing standard-cell area by ~2.5x and dynamic power to `0.890 mW` at `520 MHz`. Why is this area/power investment mandatory in a real H.264/HEVC video encoder ASIC?
options: A) Because an 8-bit SAD accumulator saturates at `255 (8'hFF)` whenever average pixel difference exceeds `1.0 LSB` (`256 * 1 = 256 > 255`), blinding the motion estimator on 99%+ of real natural video macroblocks and causing catastrophic motion-vector misprediction and video compression bloat!
B) Because 16-bit registers use zero power.
C) Because 8-bit wires cannot be routed in 14nm.
D) Because 16-bit logic runs at twice the clock period.
quiz_questions.hint: Consider what happens to video compression bit-rate if a motion estimator cannot tell the difference between a candidate with SAD = 256 (`1 LSB/pixel` error) and a candidate with SAD = 65,280 (`255 LSB/pixel` error)!
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In real video frames, almost every candidate block has an average pixel difference `> 1 LSB` (`SAD > 255`). An 8-bit accumulator clips all of them to `255 (0xFF)`, making true motion estimation impossible. Investing `3,416 um^2` (`< 0.004 mm^2`) in 14nm silicon restores 100% mathematical accuracy (`0..65,280`) while still closing `520 MHz` (`+0.22 ns` SS slack)!
Incorrect — Doubling register count increases switching capacitance `C_eff`, raising dynamic power `P = alpha * C * V^2 * f`.
Incorrect — Both 8-bit and 16-bit netlists route cleanly (`0/242 DRC`).
Incorrect — Both designs meet the exact same `520 MHz (1.923 ns)` clock period.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Without 16-bit SAD precision, any macroblock candidate with total distortion `>= 255` saturates to `0xFF`, destroying the comparator's ability to find the true minimum-distortion motion vector `(motionX, motionY)`.

quiz_questions.q: [Page 85 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 85's combined one-liner, why do we execute `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 85's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 85's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.q: [Page 85 · End-to-End V1->V9 Mastery Check] Which complete set of metrics summarizes our signed-off V9 16-Bit Motion Estimator ASIC?
options: A) 520 MHz (1.923 ns), 16-bit SAD (0000 / 0100 / FF00 all PASS), SAED14nm 125.07 x 62.80 um (7,854.4 um^2), 8,230 cells (449 FFs, 0 SRAMs), 0/242 ICV DRC, 0 LVS errors, 3-Corner PrimeTime Setup WNS +0.71/+0.54/+0.22 ns & Hold WNS 0.00 ns.
B) 100 MHz (10 ns), 8-bit SAD (saturates at 8'hFF), 2 SRAM macros, 14 DRC errors.
C) 400 MHz (2.5 ns), Setup slack -90 ps, Hold slack -820 ps.
D) 50 MHz (20 ns), 3 flip-flops, 1 ns hold violation.
quiz_questions.hint: Cross-check the target clock (`520 MHz`), the 3 directed testbench SAD hex values (`0000`, `0100`, `FF00`), the die size (`125.07 x 62.80 um`), and the 3-corner PrimeTime slacks (`+0.71 / +0.54 / +0.22 ns`).
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Option A lists the exact verified V9 sign-off metrics across RTL simulation, Fusion Compiler 14nm P&R, IC Validator DRC/LVS, and PrimeTime 3-corner STA.
Incorrect — Option B describes the unoptimized 8-bit baseline with DRC errors.
Incorrect — Option C lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 9 & 10 (`400 MHz`, `-90 ps` setup slack, `-820 ps` hold slack).
Incorrect — Option D lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 4 & 5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold slack).
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Option A is our exact V9 sign-off specification; Option C is Midterm Q9/Q10 (`-90 ps` setup, `-820 ps` hold at 400 MHz), and Option D is Midterm Q4/Q5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold violation).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (8-Bit vs. 16-Bit PPA Trade-Off Analysis)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 85 · Advanced PPA (Power, Performance, Area) Trade-Off] Upgrading the Motion Estimator from the 8-bit saturating baseline to the 16-bit full-precision architecture doubled the accumulator/comparator datapath width (`8 -> 16 bits`), increasing standard-cell area by ~2.5x and dynamic power to `0.890 mW` at `520 MHz`. Why is this area/power investment mandatory in a real H.264/HEVC video encoder ASIC?
options: A) Because an 8-bit SAD accumulator saturates at `255 (8'hFF)` whenever average pixel difference exceeds `1.0 LSB` (`256 * 1 = 256 > 255`), blinding the motion estimator on 99%+ of real natural video macroblocks and causing catastrophic motion-vector misprediction and video compression bloat!
B) Because 16-bit registers use zero power.
C) Because 8-bit wires cannot be routed in 14nm.
D) Because 16-bit logic runs at twice the clock period.
quiz_questions.hint: Consider what happens to video compression bit-rate if a motion estimator cannot tell the difference between a candidate with SAD = 256 (`1 LSB/pixel` error) and a candidate with SAD = 65,280 (`255 LSB/pixel` error)!
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In real video frames, almost every candidate block has an average pixel difference `> 1 LSB` (`SAD > 255`). An 8-bit accumulator clips all of them to `255 (0xFF)`, making true motion estimation impossible. Investing `3,416 um^2` (`< 0.004 mm^2`) in 14nm silicon restores 100% mathematical accuracy (`0..65,280`) while still closing `520 MHz` (`+0.22 ns` SS slack)!
Incorrect — Doubling register count increases switching capacitance `C_eff`, raising dynamic power `P = alpha * C * V^2 * f`.
Incorrect — Both 8-bit and 16-bit netlists route cleanly (`0/242 DRC`).
Incorrect — Both designs meet the exact same `520 MHz (1.923 ns)` clock period.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Without 16-bit SAD precision, any macroblock candidate with total distortion `>= 255` saturates to `0xFF`, destroying the comparator's ability to find the true minimum-distortion motion vector `(motionX, motionY)`.

options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 86's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.

choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 86's `required_markers`.

options: A) 520 MHz (1.923 ns), 16-bit SAD (0000 / 0100 / FF00 all PASS), SAED14nm 125.07 x 62.80 um (7,854.4 um^2), 8,230 cells (449 FFs, 0 SRAMs), 0/242 ICV DRC, 0 LVS errors, 3-Corner PrimeTime Setup WNS +0.71/+0.54/+0.22 ns & Hold WNS 0.00 ns.

D) 50 MHz (20 ns), 3 flip-flops, 1 ns hold violation.

Incorrect — Option B describes the unoptimized 8-bit baseline with DRC errors.

Incorrect — Option D lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 4 & 5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold slack).
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Option A is our exact V9 sign-off specification; Option C is Midterm Q9/Q10 (`-90 ps` setup, `-820 ps` hold at 400 MHz), and Option D is Midterm Q4/Q5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold violation).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (8-Bit vs. 16-Bit PPA Trade-Off Analysis)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 86 · Advanced PPA (Power, Performance, Area) Trade-Off] Upgrading the Motion Estimator from the 8-bit saturating baseline to the 16-bit full-precision architecture doubled the accumulator/comparator datapath width (`8 -> 16 bits`), increasing standard-cell area by ~2.5x and dynamic power to `0.890 mW` at `520 MHz`. Why is this area/power investment mandatory in a real H.264/HEVC video encoder ASIC?
options: A) Because an 8-bit SAD accumulator saturates at `255 (8'hFF)` whenever average pixel difference exceeds `1.0 LSB` (`256 * 1 = 256 > 255`), blinding the motion estimator on 99%+ of real natural video macroblocks and causing catastrophic motion-vector misprediction and video compression bloat!
B) Because 16-bit registers use zero power.
C) Because 8-bit wires cannot be routed in 14nm.
D) Because 16-bit logic runs at twice the clock period.
quiz_questions.hint: Consider what happens to video compression bit-rate if a motion estimator cannot tell the difference between a candidate with SAD = 256 (`1 LSB/pixel` error) and a candidate with SAD = 65,280 (`255 LSB/pixel` error)!
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In real video frames, almost every candidate block has an average pixel difference `> 1 LSB` (`SAD > 255`). An 8-bit accumulator clips all of them to `255 (0xFF)`, making true motion estimation impossible. Investing `3,416 um^2` (`< 0.004 mm^2`) in 14nm silicon restores 100% mathematical accuracy (`0..65,280`) while still closing `520 MHz` (`+0.22 ns` SS slack)!
Incorrect — Doubling register count increases switching capacitance `C_eff`, raising dynamic power `P = alpha * C * V^2 * f`.
Incorrect — Both 8-bit and 16-bit netlists route cleanly (`0/242 DRC`).
Incorrect — Both designs meet the exact same `520 MHz (1.923 ns)` clock period.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Without 16-bit SAD precision, any macroblock candidate with total distortion `>= 255` saturates to `0xFF`, destroying the comparator's ability to find the true minimum-distortion motion vector `(motionX, motionY)`.

options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 87's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
