choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 87's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.q: [Page 87 · End-to-End V1->V9 Mastery Check] Which complete set of metrics summarizes our signed-off V9 16-Bit Motion Estimator ASIC?
options: A) 520 MHz (1.923 ns), 16-bit SAD (0000 / 0100 / FF00 all PASS), SAED14nm 125.07 x 62.80 um (7,854.4 um^2), 8,230 cells (449 FFs, 0 SRAMs), 0/242 ICV DRC, 0 LVS errors, 3-Corner PrimeTime Setup WNS +0.71/+0.54/+0.22 ns & Hold WNS 0.00 ns.
B) 100 MHz (10 ns), 8-bit SAD (saturates at 8'hFF), 2 SRAM macros, 14 DRC errors.

D) 50 MHz (20 ns), 3 flip-flops, 1 ns hold violation.
quiz_questions.hint: Cross-check the target clock (`520 MHz`), the 3 directed testbench SAD hex values (`0000`, `0100`, `FF00`), the die size (`125.07 x 62.80 um`), and the 3-corner PrimeTime slacks (`+0.71 / +0.54 / +0.22 ns`).

Incorrect — Option B describes the unoptimized 8-bit baseline with DRC errors.
Incorrect — Option C lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 9 & 10 (`400 MHz`, `-90 ps` setup slack, `-820 ps` hold slack).
Incorrect — Option D lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 4 & 5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold slack).
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Option A is our exact V9 sign-off specification; Option C is Midterm Q9/Q10 (`-90 ps` setup, `-820 ps` hold at 400 MHz), and Option D is Midterm Q4/Q5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold violation).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (8-Bit vs. 16-Bit PPA Trade-Off Analysis)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 87 · Advanced PPA (Power, Performance, Area) Trade-Off] Upgrading the Motion Estimator from the 8-bit saturating baseline to the 16-bit full-precision architecture doubled the accumulator/comparator datapath width (`8 -> 16 bits`), increasing standard-cell area by ~2.5x and dynamic power to `0.890 mW` at `520 MHz`. Why is this area/power investment mandatory in a real H.264/HEVC video encoder ASIC?
options: A) Because an 8-bit SAD accumulator saturates at `255 (8'hFF)` whenever average pixel difference exceeds `1.0 LSB` (`256 * 1 = 256 > 255`), blinding the motion estimator on 99%+ of real natural video macroblocks and causing catastrophic motion-vector misprediction and video compression bloat!
B) Because 16-bit registers use zero power.
C) Because 8-bit wires cannot be routed in 14nm.
D) Because 16-bit logic runs at twice the clock period.
quiz_questions.hint: Consider what happens to video compression bit-rate if a motion estimator cannot tell the difference between a candidate with SAD = 256 (`1 LSB/pixel` error) and a candidate with SAD = 65,280 (`255 LSB/pixel` error)!
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In real video frames, almost every candidate block has an average pixel difference `> 1 LSB` (`SAD > 255`). An 8-bit accumulator clips all of them to `255 (0xFF)`, making true motion estimation impossible. Investing `3,416 um^2` (`< 0.004 mm^2`) in 14nm silicon restores 100% mathematical accuracy (`0..65,280`) while still closing `520 MHz` (`+0.22 ns` SS slack)!
Incorrect — Doubling register count increases switching capacitance `C_eff`, raising dynamic power `P = alpha * C * V^2 * f`.
Incorrect — Both 8-bit and 16-bit netlists route cleanly (`0/242 DRC`).
Incorrect — Both designs meet the exact same `520 MHz (1.923 ns)` clock period.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Without 16-bit SAD precision, any macroblock candidate with total distortion `>= 255` saturates to `0xFF`, destroying the comparator's ability to find the true minimum-distortion motion vector `(motionX, motionY)`.

quiz_questions.hint: Check the environment badge on Page 88: is this step running locally on your MacBook Air or on the remote SFSU Linux EDA server (`mahmoodi`), and how does `snap_step` talk back to the website?

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 88 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 88's combined one-liner, why do we execute `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 88's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 88's `required_markers`.

B) Because Git does not allow more than 10 commits on `main`.
C) Because `main` cannot store PNG files.
D) Because Python only runs on sub-branches.
quiz_questions.hint: Think about how semiconductor engineering teams protect the golden tapeout release branch (`main`) while engineers run hands-on bring-up and replication on feature/practice branches.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Keeping `main` as the immutable golden release and pushing live manual practice logs to `manual-practice-macbook-air` showcases both the finished 14nm ASIC and your verified step-by-step replication trail!
Incorrect — Git branches support unlimited commits.
Incorrect — Both `main` and sub-branches track PNG evidence seamlessly.
Incorrect — Python runs identically regardless of the checked-out Git branch.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Using `manual-practice-macbook-air` isolates your live step-by-step practice progression while preserving the golden reference on `main`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (End-to-End V1→V9 Sign-Off Metrics Audit)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 88 · End-to-End V1->V9 Mastery Check] Which complete set of metrics summarizes our signed-off V9 16-Bit Motion Estimator ASIC?
options: A) 520 MHz (1.923 ns), 16-bit SAD (0000 / 0100 / FF00 all PASS), SAED14nm 125.07 x 62.80 um (7,854.4 um^2), 8,230 cells (449 FFs, 0 SRAMs), 0/242 ICV DRC, 0 LVS errors, 3-Corner PrimeTime Setup WNS +0.71/+0.54/+0.22 ns & Hold WNS 0.00 ns.
B) 100 MHz (10 ns), 8-bit SAD (saturates at 8'hFF), 2 SRAM macros, 14 DRC errors.
C) 400 MHz (2.5 ns), Setup slack -90 ps, Hold slack -820 ps.
D) 50 MHz (20 ns), 3 flip-flops, 1 ns hold violation.
quiz_questions.hint: Cross-check the target clock (`520 MHz`), the 3 directed testbench SAD hex values (`0000`, `0100`, `FF00`), the die size (`125.07 x 62.80 um`), and the 3-corner PrimeTime slacks (`+0.71 / +0.54 / +0.22 ns`).
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Option A lists the exact verified V9 sign-off metrics across RTL simulation, Fusion Compiler 14nm P&R, IC Validator DRC/LVS, and PrimeTime 3-corner STA.
Incorrect — Option B describes the unoptimized 8-bit baseline with DRC errors.
Incorrect — Option C lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 9 & 10 (`400 MHz`, `-90 ps` setup slack, `-820 ps` hold slack).
Incorrect — Option D lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 4 & 5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold slack).
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Option A is our exact V9 sign-off specification; Option C is Midterm Q9/Q10 (`-90 ps` setup, `-820 ps` hold at 400 MHz), and Option D is Midterm Q4/Q5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold violation).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (8-Bit vs. 16-Bit PPA Trade-Off Analysis)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 88 · Advanced PPA (Power, Performance, Area) Trade-Off] Upgrading the Motion Estimator from the 8-bit saturating baseline to the 16-bit full-precision architecture doubled the accumulator/comparator datapath width (`8 -> 16 bits`), increasing standard-cell area by ~2.5x and dynamic power to `0.890 mW` at `520 MHz`. Why is this area/power investment mandatory in a real H.264/HEVC video encoder ASIC?
options: A) Because an 8-bit SAD accumulator saturates at `255 (8'hFF)` whenever average pixel difference exceeds `1.0 LSB` (`256 * 1 = 256 > 255`), blinding the motion estimator on 99%+ of real natural video macroblocks and causing catastrophic motion-vector misprediction and video compression bloat!
B) Because 16-bit registers use zero power.
C) Because 8-bit wires cannot be routed in 14nm.
D) Because 16-bit logic runs at twice the clock period.
quiz_questions.hint: Consider what happens to video compression bit-rate if a motion estimator cannot tell the difference between a candidate with SAD = 256 (`1 LSB/pixel` error) and a candidate with SAD = 65,280 (`255 LSB/pixel` error)!
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In real video frames, almost every candidate block has an average pixel difference `> 1 LSB` (`SAD > 255`). An 8-bit accumulator clips all of them to `255 (0xFF)`, making true motion estimation impossible. Investing `3,416 um^2` (`< 0.004 mm^2`) in 14nm silicon restores 100% mathematical accuracy (`0..65,280`) while still closing `520 MHz` (`+0.22 ns` SS slack)!
Incorrect — Doubling register count increases switching capacitance `C_eff`, raising dynamic power `P = alpha * C * V^2 * f`.
Incorrect — Both 8-bit and 16-bit netlists route cleanly (`0/242 DRC`).
Incorrect — Both designs meet the exact same `520 MHz (1.923 ns)` clock period.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Without 16-bit SAD precision, any macroblock candidate with total distortion `>= 255` saturates to `0xFF`, destroying the comparator's ability to find the true minimum-distortion motion vector `(motionX, motionY)`.

quiz_questions.q: [Page 89 · Beginner Orientation] Before pasting Page 89's one-liner (`Page 89: Packaging All Submission Deliverables (`), which terminal environment should you paste into, and what happens immediately after you press `Return`?
options: A) Paste it into Microsoft Word or a browser URL bar.

C) Paste it into a disconnected terminal window showing `Broken pipe` without reconnecting.
D) Reboot the laptop after every single command.
quiz_questions.hint: Check the environment badge on Page 89: is this step running locally on your MacBook Air or on the remote SFSU Linux EDA server (`mahmoodi`), and how does `snap_step` talk back to the website?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Shell commands must be pasted into an active UNIX terminal emulator (`Terminal.app` or `XQuartz xterm`), not a word processor or browser address bar.

Correct! Pasting into your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`) runs the command inside `snap_step`, which automatically checks the exit code and required markers and updates your live `:8788` web console!

Incorrect — A terminal showing `client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe` has lost its SSH connection; you must either use your clean local terminal window or run the Step 0 Auto-Connect command first.
Incorrect — You never need to reboot between pages; `snap_step` preserves your state continuously from Page 1 to Page 100.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Page 89 runs in your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`). Pressing `Return` triggers `snap_step`, which logs the output, captures the screenshot, and sends real-time verification telemetry to the website.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 89 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 89's combined one-liner, why do we execute `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 89's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `mkdir -p ~/me_asic_new_v1/scripts` performs: Creates isolated directory hierarchy (without failing if directories already exist). And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 89's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Reproducible ASIC Sign-Off & Git Branch Hygiene)

B) Because Git does not allow more than 10 commits on `main`.
C) Because `main` cannot store PNG files.
D) Because Python only runs on sub-branches.
quiz_questions.hint: Think about how semiconductor engineering teams protect the golden tapeout release branch (`main`) while engineers run hands-on bring-up and replication on feature/practice branches.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Keeping `main` as the immutable golden release and pushing live manual practice logs to `manual-practice-macbook-air` showcases both the finished 14nm ASIC and your verified step-by-step replication trail!
Incorrect — Git branches support unlimited commits.
Incorrect — Both `main` and sub-branches track PNG evidence seamlessly.
Incorrect — Python runs identically regardless of the checked-out Git branch.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Using `manual-practice-macbook-air` isolates your live step-by-step practice progression while preserving the golden reference on `main`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (End-to-End V1→V9 Sign-Off Metrics Audit)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 89 · End-to-End V1->V9 Mastery Check] Which complete set of metrics summarizes our signed-off V9 16-Bit Motion Estimator ASIC?
options: A) 520 MHz (1.923 ns), 16-bit SAD (0000 / 0100 / FF00 all PASS), SAED14nm 125.07 x 62.80 um (7,854.4 um^2), 8,230 cells (449 FFs, 0 SRAMs), 0/242 ICV DRC, 0 LVS errors, 3-Corner PrimeTime Setup WNS +0.71/+0.54/+0.22 ns & Hold WNS 0.00 ns.
B) 100 MHz (10 ns), 8-bit SAD (saturates at 8'hFF), 2 SRAM macros, 14 DRC errors.
C) 400 MHz (2.5 ns), Setup slack -90 ps, Hold slack -820 ps.
D) 50 MHz (20 ns), 3 flip-flops, 1 ns hold violation.
quiz_questions.hint: Cross-check the target clock (`520 MHz`), the 3 directed testbench SAD hex values (`0000`, `0100`, `FF00`), the die size (`125.07 x 62.80 um`), and the 3-corner PrimeTime slacks (`+0.71 / +0.54 / +0.22 ns`).
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Option A lists the exact verified V9 sign-off metrics across RTL simulation, Fusion Compiler 14nm P&R, IC Validator DRC/LVS, and PrimeTime 3-corner STA.
Incorrect — Option B describes the unoptimized 8-bit baseline with DRC errors.
Incorrect — Option C lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 9 & 10 (`400 MHz`, `-90 ps` setup slack, `-820 ps` hold slack).
Incorrect — Option D lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 4 & 5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold slack).
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Option A is our exact V9 sign-off specification; Option C is Midterm Q9/Q10 (`-90 ps` setup, `-820 ps` hold at 400 MHz), and Option D is Midterm Q4/Q5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold violation).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (8-Bit vs. 16-Bit PPA Trade-Off Analysis)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 89 · Advanced PPA (Power, Performance, Area) Trade-Off] Upgrading the Motion Estimator from the 8-bit saturating baseline to the 16-bit full-precision architecture doubled the accumulator/comparator datapath width (`8 -> 16 bits`), increasing standard-cell area by ~2.5x and dynamic power to `0.890 mW` at `520 MHz`. Why is this area/power investment mandatory in a real H.264/HEVC video encoder ASIC?
options: A) Because an 8-bit SAD accumulator saturates at `255 (8'hFF)` whenever average pixel difference exceeds `1.0 LSB` (`256 * 1 = 256 > 255`), blinding the motion estimator on 99%+ of real natural video macroblocks and causing catastrophic motion-vector misprediction and video compression bloat!
B) Because 16-bit registers use zero power.
C) Because 8-bit wires cannot be routed in 14nm.
D) Because 16-bit logic runs at twice the clock period.
quiz_questions.hint: Consider what happens to video compression bit-rate if a motion estimator cannot tell the difference between a candidate with SAD = 256 (`1 LSB/pixel` error) and a candidate with SAD = 65,280 (`255 LSB/pixel` error)!
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In real video frames, almost every candidate block has an average pixel difference `> 1 LSB` (`SAD > 255`). An 8-bit accumulator clips all of them to `255 (0xFF)`, making true motion estimation impossible. Investing `3,416 um^2` (`< 0.004 mm^2`) in 14nm silicon restores 100% mathematical accuracy (`0..65,280`) while still closing `520 MHz` (`+0.22 ns` SS slack)!
Incorrect — Doubling register count increases switching capacitance `C_eff`, raising dynamic power `P = alpha * C * V^2 * f`.
Incorrect — Both 8-bit and 16-bit netlists route cleanly (`0/242 DRC`).
Incorrect — Both designs meet the exact same `520 MHz (1.923 ns)` clock period.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Without 16-bit SAD precision, any macroblock candidate with total distortion `>= 255` saturates to `0xFF`, destroying the comparator's ability to find the true minimum-distortion motion vector `(motionX, motionY)`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 90 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 90's combined one-liner, why do we execute `echo 'PROJECT_VARIATIONS: Local=motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual | Re` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Executes sequential step operation: `echo 'PROJECT_VARIATIONS: Local=motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual | Remote=~/me_asic_new_v1 | Branch=manual-practice-macbook-air | Top=module top (11 ports preserved)'` Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 90's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `echo 'PROJECT_VARIATIONS: Local=motion-estimator-14nm-asic-m` performs: Executes sequential step operation: `echo 'PROJECT_VARIATIONS: Local=motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual | Remote=~/me_asic_new_v1 | Branch=manual-practice-macbook-air | Top=module top (11 ports preserved)'` And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 90's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (End-to-End V1→V9 Sign-Off Metrics Audit)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 90 · End-to-End V1->V9 Mastery Check] Which complete set of metrics summarizes our signed-off V9 16-Bit Motion Estimator ASIC?
options: A) 520 MHz (1.923 ns), 16-bit SAD (0000 / 0100 / FF00 all PASS), SAED14nm 125.07 x 62.80 um (7,854.4 um^2), 8,230 cells (449 FFs, 0 SRAMs), 0/242 ICV DRC, 0 LVS errors, 3-Corner PrimeTime Setup WNS +0.71/+0.54/+0.22 ns & Hold WNS 0.00 ns.
B) 100 MHz (10 ns), 8-bit SAD (saturates at 8'hFF), 2 SRAM macros, 14 DRC errors.
C) 400 MHz (2.5 ns), Setup slack -90 ps, Hold slack -820 ps.
D) 50 MHz (20 ns), 3 flip-flops, 1 ns hold violation.
quiz_questions.hint: Cross-check the target clock (`520 MHz`), the 3 directed testbench SAD hex values (`0000`, `0100`, `FF00`), the die size (`125.07 x 62.80 um`), and the 3-corner PrimeTime slacks (`+0.71 / +0.54 / +0.22 ns`).
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Option A lists the exact verified V9 sign-off metrics across RTL simulation, Fusion Compiler 14nm P&R, IC Validator DRC/LVS, and PrimeTime 3-corner STA.
Incorrect — Option B describes the unoptimized 8-bit baseline with DRC errors.
Incorrect — Option C lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 9 & 10 (`400 MHz`, `-90 ps` setup slack, `-820 ps` hold slack).
Incorrect — Option D lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 4 & 5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold slack).
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Option A is our exact V9 sign-off specification; Option C is Midterm Q9/Q10 (`-90 ps` setup, `-820 ps` hold at 400 MHz), and Option D is Midterm Q4/Q5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold violation).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (8-Bit vs. 16-Bit PPA Trade-Off Analysis)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 90 · Advanced PPA (Power, Performance, Area) Trade-Off] Upgrading the Motion Estimator from the 8-bit saturating baseline to the 16-bit full-precision architecture doubled the accumulator/comparator datapath width (`8 -> 16 bits`), increasing standard-cell area by ~2.5x and dynamic power to `0.890 mW` at `520 MHz`. Why is this area/power investment mandatory in a real H.264/HEVC video encoder ASIC?
options: A) Because an 8-bit SAD accumulator saturates at `255 (8'hFF)` whenever average pixel difference exceeds `1.0 LSB` (`256 * 1 = 256 > 255`), blinding the motion estimator on 99%+ of real natural video macroblocks and causing catastrophic motion-vector misprediction and video compression bloat!
B) Because 16-bit registers use zero power.
C) Because 8-bit wires cannot be routed in 14nm.
D) Because 16-bit logic runs at twice the clock period.
quiz_questions.hint: Consider what happens to video compression bit-rate if a motion estimator cannot tell the difference between a candidate with SAD = 256 (`1 LSB/pixel` error) and a candidate with SAD = 65,280 (`255 LSB/pixel` error)!
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In real video frames, almost every candidate block has an average pixel difference `> 1 LSB` (`SAD > 255`). An 8-bit accumulator clips all of them to `255 (0xFF)`, making true motion estimation impossible. Investing `3,416 um^2` (`< 0.004 mm^2`) in 14nm silicon restores 100% mathematical accuracy (`0..65,280`) while still closing `520 MHz` (`+0.22 ns` SS slack)!
Incorrect — Doubling register count increases switching capacitance `C_eff`, raising dynamic power `P = alpha * C * V^2 * f`.
Incorrect — Both 8-bit and 16-bit netlists route cleanly (`0/242 DRC`).
Incorrect — Both designs meet the exact same `520 MHz (1.923 ns)` clock period.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Without 16-bit SAD precision, any macroblock candidate with total distortion `>= 255` saturates to `0xFF`, destroying the comparator's ability to find the true minimum-distortion motion vector `(motionX, motionY)`.

options: A) 520 MHz (1.923 ns), 16-bit SAD (0000 / 0100 / FF00 all PASS), SAED14nm 125.07 x 62.80 um (7,854.4 um^2), 8,230 cells (449 FFs, 0 SRAMs), 0/242 ICV DRC, 0 LVS errors, 3-Corner PrimeTime Setup WNS +0.71/+0.54/+0.22 ns & Hold WNS 0.00 ns.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (8-Bit vs. 16-Bit PPA Trade-Off Analysis)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 91 · Advanced PPA (Power, Performance, Area) Trade-Off] Upgrading the Motion Estimator from the 8-bit saturating baseline to the 16-bit full-precision architecture doubled the accumulator/comparator datapath width (`8 -> 16 bits`), increasing standard-cell area by ~2.5x and dynamic power to `0.890 mW` at `520 MHz`. Why is this area/power investment mandatory in a real H.264/HEVC video encoder ASIC?
options: A) Because an 8-bit SAD accumulator saturates at `255 (8'hFF)` whenever average pixel difference exceeds `1.0 LSB` (`256 * 1 = 256 > 255`), blinding the motion estimator on 99%+ of real natural video macroblocks and causing catastrophic motion-vector misprediction and video compression bloat!
B) Because 16-bit registers use zero power.
C) Because 8-bit wires cannot be routed in 14nm.
D) Because 16-bit logic runs at twice the clock period.
quiz_questions.hint: Consider what happens to video compression bit-rate if a motion estimator cannot tell the difference between a candidate with SAD = 256 (`1 LSB/pixel` error) and a candidate with SAD = 65,280 (`255 LSB/pixel` error)!
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In real video frames, almost every candidate block has an average pixel difference `> 1 LSB` (`SAD > 255`). An 8-bit accumulator clips all of them to `255 (0xFF)`, making true motion estimation impossible. Investing `3,416 um^2` (`< 0.004 mm^2`) in 14nm silicon restores 100% mathematical accuracy (`0..65,280`) while still closing `520 MHz` (`+0.22 ns` SS slack)!
Incorrect — Doubling register count increases switching capacitance `C_eff`, raising dynamic power `P = alpha * C * V^2 * f`.
Incorrect — Both 8-bit and 16-bit netlists route cleanly (`0/242 DRC`).
Incorrect — Both designs meet the exact same `520 MHz (1.923 ns)` clock period.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Without 16-bit SAD precision, any macroblock candidate with total distortion `>= 255` saturates to `0xFF`, destroying the comparator's ability to find the true minimum-distortion motion vector `(motionX, motionY)`.

options: A) 520 MHz (1.923 ns), 16-bit SAD (0000 / 0100 / FF00 all PASS), SAED14nm 125.07 x 62.80 um (7,854.4 um^2), 8,230 cells (449 FFs, 0 SRAMs), 0/242 ICV DRC, 0 LVS errors, 3-Corner PrimeTime Setup WNS +0.71/+0.54/+0.22 ns & Hold WNS 0.00 ns.
B) 100 MHz (10 ns), 8-bit SAD (saturates at 8'hFF), 2 SRAM macros, 14 DRC errors.
C) 400 MHz (2.5 ns), Setup slack -90 ps, Hold slack -820 ps.
D) 50 MHz (20 ns), 3 flip-flops, 1 ns hold violation.
quiz_questions.hint: Cross-check the target clock (`520 MHz`), the 3 directed testbench SAD hex values (`0000`, `0100`, `FF00`), the die size (`125.07 x 62.80 um`), and the 3-corner PrimeTime slacks (`+0.71 / +0.54 / +0.22 ns`).
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Option A lists the exact verified V9 sign-off metrics across RTL simulation, Fusion Compiler 14nm P&R, IC Validator DRC/LVS, and PrimeTime 3-corner STA.
Incorrect — Option B describes the unoptimized 8-bit baseline with DRC errors.
Incorrect — Option C lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 9 & 10 (`400 MHz`, `-90 ps` setup slack, `-820 ps` hold slack).
Incorrect — Option D lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 4 & 5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold slack).
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Option A is our exact V9 sign-off specification; Option C is Midterm Q9/Q10 (`-90 ps` setup, `-820 ps` hold at 400 MHz), and Option D is Midterm Q4/Q5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold violation).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (8-Bit vs. 16-Bit PPA Trade-Off Analysis)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 92 · Advanced PPA (Power, Performance, Area) Trade-Off] Upgrading the Motion Estimator from the 8-bit saturating baseline to the 16-bit full-precision architecture doubled the accumulator/comparator datapath width (`8 -> 16 bits`), increasing standard-cell area by ~2.5x and dynamic power to `0.890 mW` at `520 MHz`. Why is this area/power investment mandatory in a real H.264/HEVC video encoder ASIC?
options: A) Because an 8-bit SAD accumulator saturates at `255 (8'hFF)` whenever average pixel difference exceeds `1.0 LSB` (`256 * 1 = 256 > 255`), blinding the motion estimator on 99%+ of real natural video macroblocks and causing catastrophic motion-vector misprediction and video compression bloat!
B) Because 16-bit registers use zero power.
C) Because 8-bit wires cannot be routed in 14nm.
D) Because 16-bit logic runs at twice the clock period.
quiz_questions.hint: Consider what happens to video compression bit-rate if a motion estimator cannot tell the difference between a candidate with SAD = 256 (`1 LSB/pixel` error) and a candidate with SAD = 65,280 (`255 LSB/pixel` error)!
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In real video frames, almost every candidate block has an average pixel difference `> 1 LSB` (`SAD > 255`). An 8-bit accumulator clips all of them to `255 (0xFF)`, making true motion estimation impossible. Investing `3,416 um^2` (`< 0.004 mm^2`) in 14nm silicon restores 100% mathematical accuracy (`0..65,280`) while still closing `520 MHz` (`+0.22 ns` SS slack)!
Incorrect — Doubling register count increases switching capacitance `C_eff`, raising dynamic power `P = alpha * C * V^2 * f`.
Incorrect — Both 8-bit and 16-bit netlists route cleanly (`0/242 DRC`).
Incorrect — Both designs meet the exact same `520 MHz (1.923 ns)` clock period.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Without 16-bit SAD precision, any macroblock candidate with total distortion `>= 255` saturates to `0xFF`, destroying the comparator's ability to find the true minimum-distortion motion vector `(motionX, motionY)`.

options: A) Executes sequential step operation: `echo '# 520 MHz 16-PE Systolic Motion Estimator ASIC (SAED14nm FinFET)' > ~/me_asic_new_v1/README.md` Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 94's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.

choice_diagnostics: Correct! `echo '# 520 MHz 16-PE Systolic Motion Estimator ASIC (SAED14` performs: Executes sequential step operation: `echo '# 520 MHz 16-PE Systolic Motion Estimator ASIC (SAED14nm FinFET)' > ~/me_asic_new_v1/README.md` And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (8-Bit vs. 16-Bit PPA Trade-Off Analysis)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 94 · Advanced PPA (Power, Performance, Area) Trade-Off] Upgrading the Motion Estimator from the 8-bit saturating baseline to the 16-bit full-precision architecture doubled the accumulator/comparator datapath width (`8 -> 16 bits`), increasing standard-cell area by ~2.5x and dynamic power to `0.890 mW` at `520 MHz`. Why is this area/power investment mandatory in a real H.264/HEVC video encoder ASIC?
options: A) Because an 8-bit SAD accumulator saturates at `255 (8'hFF)` whenever average pixel difference exceeds `1.0 LSB` (`256 * 1 = 256 > 255`), blinding the motion estimator on 99%+ of real natural video macroblocks and causing catastrophic motion-vector misprediction and video compression bloat!
B) Because 16-bit registers use zero power.
C) Because 8-bit wires cannot be routed in 14nm.
D) Because 16-bit logic runs at twice the clock period.
quiz_questions.hint: Consider what happens to video compression bit-rate if a motion estimator cannot tell the difference between a candidate with SAD = 256 (`1 LSB/pixel` error) and a candidate with SAD = 65,280 (`255 LSB/pixel` error)!
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In real video frames, almost every candidate block has an average pixel difference `> 1 LSB` (`SAD > 255`). An 8-bit accumulator clips all of them to `255 (0xFF)`, making true motion estimation impossible. Investing `3,416 um^2` (`< 0.004 mm^2`) in 14nm silicon restores 100% mathematical accuracy (`0..65,280`) while still closing `520 MHz` (`+0.22 ns` SS slack)!
Incorrect — Doubling register count increases switching capacitance `C_eff`, raising dynamic power `P = alpha * C * V^2 * f`.
Incorrect — Both 8-bit and 16-bit netlists route cleanly (`0/242 DRC`).
Incorrect — Both designs meet the exact same `520 MHz (1.923 ns)` clock period.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Without 16-bit SAD precision, any macroblock candidate with total distortion `>= 255` saturates to `0xFF`, destroying the comparator's ability to find the true minimum-distortion motion vector `(motionX, motionY)`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 95 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 95's combined one-liner, why do we execute `cd ~/motion-estimator-asic-lab-notebook-2026` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Executes sequential step operation: `cd ~/motion-estimator-asic-lab-notebook-2026` Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 95's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `cd ~/motion-estimator-asic-lab-notebook-2026` performs: Executes sequential step operation: `cd ~/motion-estimator-asic-lab-notebook-2026` And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 95's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (End-to-End V1→V9 Sign-Off Metrics Audit)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 95 · End-to-End V1->V9 Mastery Check] Which complete set of metrics summarizes our signed-off V9 16-Bit Motion Estimator ASIC?
options: A) 520 MHz (1.923 ns), 16-bit SAD (0000 / 0100 / FF00 all PASS), SAED14nm 125.07 x 62.80 um (7,854.4 um^2), 8,230 cells (449 FFs, 0 SRAMs), 0/242 ICV DRC, 0 LVS errors, 3-Corner PrimeTime Setup WNS +0.71/+0.54/+0.22 ns & Hold WNS 0.00 ns.
B) 100 MHz (10 ns), 8-bit SAD (saturates at 8'hFF), 2 SRAM macros, 14 DRC errors.
C) 400 MHz (2.5 ns), Setup slack -90 ps, Hold slack -820 ps.
D) 50 MHz (20 ns), 3 flip-flops, 1 ns hold violation.
quiz_questions.hint: Cross-check the target clock (`520 MHz`), the 3 directed testbench SAD hex values (`0000`, `0100`, `FF00`), the die size (`125.07 x 62.80 um`), and the 3-corner PrimeTime slacks (`+0.71 / +0.54 / +0.22 ns`).
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Option A lists the exact verified V9 sign-off metrics across RTL simulation, Fusion Compiler 14nm P&R, IC Validator DRC/LVS, and PrimeTime 3-corner STA.
Incorrect — Option B describes the unoptimized 8-bit baseline with DRC errors.
Incorrect — Option C lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 9 & 10 (`400 MHz`, `-90 ps` setup slack, `-820 ps` hold slack).
Incorrect — Option D lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 4 & 5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold slack).
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Option A is our exact V9 sign-off specification; Option C is Midterm Q9/Q10 (`-90 ps` setup, `-820 ps` hold at 400 MHz), and Option D is Midterm Q4/Q5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold violation).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (8-Bit vs. 16-Bit PPA Trade-Off Analysis)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 95 · Advanced PPA (Power, Performance, Area) Trade-Off] Upgrading the Motion Estimator from the 8-bit saturating baseline to the 16-bit full-precision architecture doubled the accumulator/comparator datapath width (`8 -> 16 bits`), increasing standard-cell area by ~2.5x and dynamic power to `0.890 mW` at `520 MHz`. Why is this area/power investment mandatory in a real H.264/HEVC video encoder ASIC?
options: A) Because an 8-bit SAD accumulator saturates at `255 (8'hFF)` whenever average pixel difference exceeds `1.0 LSB` (`256 * 1 = 256 > 255`), blinding the motion estimator on 99%+ of real natural video macroblocks and causing catastrophic motion-vector misprediction and video compression bloat!
B) Because 16-bit registers use zero power.
C) Because 8-bit wires cannot be routed in 14nm.
D) Because 16-bit logic runs at twice the clock period.
quiz_questions.hint: Consider what happens to video compression bit-rate if a motion estimator cannot tell the difference between a candidate with SAD = 256 (`1 LSB/pixel` error) and a candidate with SAD = 65,280 (`255 LSB/pixel` error)!
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In real video frames, almost every candidate block has an average pixel difference `> 1 LSB` (`SAD > 255`). An 8-bit accumulator clips all of them to `255 (0xFF)`, making true motion estimation impossible. Investing `3,416 um^2` (`< 0.004 mm^2`) in 14nm silicon restores 100% mathematical accuracy (`0..65,280`) while still closing `520 MHz` (`+0.22 ns` SS slack)!
Incorrect — Doubling register count increases switching capacitance `C_eff`, raising dynamic power `P = alpha * C * V^2 * f`.
Incorrect — Both 8-bit and 16-bit netlists route cleanly (`0/242 DRC`).
Incorrect — Both designs meet the exact same `520 MHz (1.923 ns)` clock period.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Without 16-bit SAD precision, any macroblock candidate with total distortion `>= 255` saturates to `0xFF`, destroying the comparator's ability to find the true minimum-distortion motion vector `(motionX, motionY)`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 1 · Easy (Beginner Foundation & Terminal Orientation)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 96 · Beginner Orientation] Before pasting Page 96's one-liner (`Page 96: Beginner Debugging Encyclopedia  -  Par`), which terminal environment should you paste into, and what happens immediately after you press `Return`?

C) Paste it into a disconnected terminal window showing `Broken pipe` without reconnecting.
D) Reboot the laptop after every single command.
quiz_questions.hint: Check the environment badge on Page 96: is this step running locally on your MacBook Air or on the remote SFSU Linux EDA server (`mahmoodi`), and how does `snap_step` talk back to the website?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Shell commands must be pasted into an active UNIX terminal emulator (`Terminal.app` or `XQuartz xterm`), not a word processor or browser address bar.

Correct! Pasting into your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`) runs the command inside `snap_step`, which automatically checks the exit code and required markers and updates your live `:8788` web console!

Incorrect — A terminal showing `client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe` has lost its SSH connection; you must either use your clean local terminal window or run the Step 0 Auto-Connect command first.

quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Page 96 runs in your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`). Pressing `Return` triggers `snap_step`, which logs the output, captures the screenshot, and sends real-time verification telemetry to the website.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 96 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 96's combined one-liner, why do we execute `echo 'DIAG_PART1: Checking USER, HOST, DISPLAY, and ~/.ssh permissions` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Starts the macOS XQuartz X11 server and verifies the local/forwarded graphical display socket. Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 96's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `echo 'DIAG_PART1: Checking USER, HOST, DISPLAY, and ~/.ssh p` performs: Starts the macOS XQuartz X11 server and verifies the local/forwarded graphical display socket. And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 96's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Reproducible ASIC Sign-Off & Git Branch Hygiene)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 96 · Reproducible ASIC Sign-Off & Git Hygiene] Why does our workflow commit your MacBook Air step-by-step logs and screenshots to the `manual-practice-macbook-air` sub-branch instead of overwriting `main`?
options: A) So the completed, verified `main` branch portfolio remains 100% intact as a golden reference for recruiters while `manual-practice-macbook-air` records your real-time, chronological Page 1 -> Page 100 manual build evidence.
B) Because Git does not allow more than 10 commits on `main`.
C) Because `main` cannot store PNG files.
D) Because Python only runs on sub-branches.
quiz_questions.hint: Think about how semiconductor engineering teams protect the golden tapeout release branch (`main`) while engineers run hands-on bring-up and replication on feature/practice branches.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Keeping `main` as the immutable golden release and pushing live manual practice logs to `manual-practice-macbook-air` showcases both the finished 14nm ASIC and your verified step-by-step replication trail!
Incorrect — Git branches support unlimited commits.
Incorrect — Both `main` and sub-branches track PNG evidence seamlessly.
Incorrect — Python runs identically regardless of the checked-out Git branch.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Using `manual-practice-macbook-air` isolates your live step-by-step practice progression while preserving the golden reference on `main`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (End-to-End V1→V9 Sign-Off Metrics Audit)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 96 · End-to-End V1->V9 Mastery Check] Which complete set of metrics summarizes our signed-off V9 16-Bit Motion Estimator ASIC?
options: A) 520 MHz (1.923 ns), 16-bit SAD (0000 / 0100 / FF00 all PASS), SAED14nm 125.07 x 62.80 um (7,854.4 um^2), 8,230 cells (449 FFs, 0 SRAMs), 0/242 ICV DRC, 0 LVS errors, 3-Corner PrimeTime Setup WNS +0.71/+0.54/+0.22 ns & Hold WNS 0.00 ns.
B) 100 MHz (10 ns), 8-bit SAD (saturates at 8'hFF), 2 SRAM macros, 14 DRC errors.
C) 400 MHz (2.5 ns), Setup slack -90 ps, Hold slack -820 ps.
D) 50 MHz (20 ns), 3 flip-flops, 1 ns hold violation.
quiz_questions.hint: Cross-check the target clock (`520 MHz`), the 3 directed testbench SAD hex values (`0000`, `0100`, `FF00`), the die size (`125.07 x 62.80 um`), and the 3-corner PrimeTime slacks (`+0.71 / +0.54 / +0.22 ns`).
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Option A lists the exact verified V9 sign-off metrics across RTL simulation, Fusion Compiler 14nm P&R, IC Validator DRC/LVS, and PrimeTime 3-corner STA.
Incorrect — Option B describes the unoptimized 8-bit baseline with DRC errors.
Incorrect — Option C lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 9 & 10 (`400 MHz`, `-90 ps` setup slack, `-820 ps` hold slack).
Incorrect — Option D lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 4 & 5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold slack).
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Option A is our exact V9 sign-off specification; Option C is Midterm Q9/Q10 (`-90 ps` setup, `-820 ps` hold at 400 MHz), and Option D is Midterm Q4/Q5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold violation).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (8-Bit vs. 16-Bit PPA Trade-Off Analysis)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 96 · Advanced PPA (Power, Performance, Area) Trade-Off] Upgrading the Motion Estimator from the 8-bit saturating baseline to the 16-bit full-precision architecture doubled the accumulator/comparator datapath width (`8 -> 16 bits`), increasing standard-cell area by ~2.5x and dynamic power to `0.890 mW` at `520 MHz`. Why is this area/power investment mandatory in a real H.264/HEVC video encoder ASIC?
options: A) Because an 8-bit SAD accumulator saturates at `255 (8'hFF)` whenever average pixel difference exceeds `1.0 LSB` (`256 * 1 = 256 > 255`), blinding the motion estimator on 99%+ of real natural video macroblocks and causing catastrophic motion-vector misprediction and video compression bloat!
B) Because 16-bit registers use zero power.
C) Because 8-bit wires cannot be routed in 14nm.
D) Because 16-bit logic runs at twice the clock period.
quiz_questions.hint: Consider what happens to video compression bit-rate if a motion estimator cannot tell the difference between a candidate with SAD = 256 (`1 LSB/pixel` error) and a candidate with SAD = 65,280 (`255 LSB/pixel` error)!
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In real video frames, almost every candidate block has an average pixel difference `> 1 LSB` (`SAD > 255`). An 8-bit accumulator clips all of them to `255 (0xFF)`, making true motion estimation impossible. Investing `3,416 um^2` (`< 0.004 mm^2`) in 14nm silicon restores 100% mathematical accuracy (`0..65,280`) while still closing `520 MHz` (`+0.22 ns` SS slack)!
Incorrect — Doubling register count increases switching capacitance `C_eff`, raising dynamic power `P = alpha * C * V^2 * f`.
Incorrect — Both 8-bit and 16-bit netlists route cleanly (`0/242 DRC`).
Incorrect — Both designs meet the exact same `520 MHz (1.923 ns)` clock period.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Without 16-bit SAD precision, any macroblock candidate with total distortion `>= 255` saturates to `0xFF`, destroying the comparator's ability to find the true minimum-distortion motion vector `(motionX, motionY)`.

quiz_questions.q: [Page 97 · Beginner Orientation] Before pasting Page 97's one-liner (`Page 97: Beginner Debugging Encyclopedia  -  Par`), which terminal environment should you paste into, and what happens immediately after you press `Return`?

quiz_questions.hint: Check the environment badge on Page 97: is this step running locally on your MacBook Air or on the remote SFSU Linux EDA server (`mahmoodi`), and how does `snap_step` talk back to the website?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Shell commands must be pasted into an active UNIX terminal emulator (`Terminal.app` or `XQuartz xterm`), not a word processor or browser address bar.

Correct! Pasting into your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`) runs the command inside `snap_step`, which automatically checks the exit code and required markers and updates your live `:8788` web console!

Incorrect — A terminal showing `client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe` has lost its SSH connection; you must either use your clean local terminal window or run the Step 0 Auto-Connect command first.

quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Page 97 runs in your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`). Pressing `Return` triggers `snap_step`, which logs the output, captures the screenshot, and sends real-time verification telemetry to the website.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 97 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 97's combined one-liner, why do we execute `which vcs verdi` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Compiles synthesizable Verilog RTL + testbench with Synopsys VCS and executes the 520 MHz cycle-accurate simulation. Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 97's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `which vcs verdi` performs: Compiles synthesizable Verilog RTL + testbench with Synopsys VCS and executes the 520 MHz cycle-accurate simulation. And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 97's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Reproducible ASIC Sign-Off & Git Branch Hygiene)

options: A) So the completed, verified `main` branch portfolio remains 100% intact as a golden reference for recruiters while `manual-practice-macbook-air` records your real-time, chronological Page 1 -> Page 100 manual build evidence.
B) Because Git does not allow more than 10 commits on `main`.
C) Because `main` cannot store PNG files.
D) Because Python only runs on sub-branches.
quiz_questions.hint: Think about how semiconductor engineering teams protect the golden tapeout release branch (`main`) while engineers run hands-on bring-up and replication on feature/practice branches.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Keeping `main` as the immutable golden release and pushing live manual practice logs to `manual-practice-macbook-air` showcases both the finished 14nm ASIC and your verified step-by-step replication trail!
Incorrect — Git branches support unlimited commits.
Incorrect — Both `main` and sub-branches track PNG evidence seamlessly.
Incorrect — Python runs identically regardless of the checked-out Git branch.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Using `manual-practice-macbook-air` isolates your live step-by-step practice progression while preserving the golden reference on `main`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (End-to-End V1→V9 Sign-Off Metrics Audit)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 97 · End-to-End V1->V9 Mastery Check] Which complete set of metrics summarizes our signed-off V9 16-Bit Motion Estimator ASIC?
options: A) 520 MHz (1.923 ns), 16-bit SAD (0000 / 0100 / FF00 all PASS), SAED14nm 125.07 x 62.80 um (7,854.4 um^2), 8,230 cells (449 FFs, 0 SRAMs), 0/242 ICV DRC, 0 LVS errors, 3-Corner PrimeTime Setup WNS +0.71/+0.54/+0.22 ns & Hold WNS 0.00 ns.
B) 100 MHz (10 ns), 8-bit SAD (saturates at 8'hFF), 2 SRAM macros, 14 DRC errors.
C) 400 MHz (2.5 ns), Setup slack -90 ps, Hold slack -820 ps.
D) 50 MHz (20 ns), 3 flip-flops, 1 ns hold violation.
quiz_questions.hint: Cross-check the target clock (`520 MHz`), the 3 directed testbench SAD hex values (`0000`, `0100`, `FF00`), the die size (`125.07 x 62.80 um`), and the 3-corner PrimeTime slacks (`+0.71 / +0.54 / +0.22 ns`).
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Option A lists the exact verified V9 sign-off metrics across RTL simulation, Fusion Compiler 14nm P&R, IC Validator DRC/LVS, and PrimeTime 3-corner STA.
Incorrect — Option B describes the unoptimized 8-bit baseline with DRC errors.
Incorrect — Option C lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 9 & 10 (`400 MHz`, `-90 ps` setup slack, `-820 ps` hold slack).
Incorrect — Option D lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 4 & 5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold slack).
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Option A is our exact V9 sign-off specification; Option C is Midterm Q9/Q10 (`-90 ps` setup, `-820 ps` hold at 400 MHz), and Option D is Midterm Q4/Q5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold violation).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (8-Bit vs. 16-Bit PPA Trade-Off Analysis)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 97 · Advanced PPA (Power, Performance, Area) Trade-Off] Upgrading the Motion Estimator from the 8-bit saturating baseline to the 16-bit full-precision architecture doubled the accumulator/comparator datapath width (`8 -> 16 bits`), increasing standard-cell area by ~2.5x and dynamic power to `0.890 mW` at `520 MHz`. Why is this area/power investment mandatory in a real H.264/HEVC video encoder ASIC?
options: A) Because an 8-bit SAD accumulator saturates at `255 (8'hFF)` whenever average pixel difference exceeds `1.0 LSB` (`256 * 1 = 256 > 255`), blinding the motion estimator on 99%+ of real natural video macroblocks and causing catastrophic motion-vector misprediction and video compression bloat!
B) Because 16-bit registers use zero power.
C) Because 8-bit wires cannot be routed in 14nm.
D) Because 16-bit logic runs at twice the clock period.
quiz_questions.hint: Consider what happens to video compression bit-rate if a motion estimator cannot tell the difference between a candidate with SAD = 256 (`1 LSB/pixel` error) and a candidate with SAD = 65,280 (`255 LSB/pixel` error)!
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In real video frames, almost every candidate block has an average pixel difference `> 1 LSB` (`SAD > 255`). An 8-bit accumulator clips all of them to `255 (0xFF)`, making true motion estimation impossible. Investing `3,416 um^2` (`< 0.004 mm^2`) in 14nm silicon restores 100% mathematical accuracy (`0..65,280`) while still closing `520 MHz` (`+0.22 ns` SS slack)!
Incorrect — Doubling register count increases switching capacitance `C_eff`, raising dynamic power `P = alpha * C * V^2 * f`.
Incorrect — Both 8-bit and 16-bit netlists route cleanly (`0/242 DRC`).
Incorrect — Both designs meet the exact same `520 MHz (1.923 ns)` clock period.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Without 16-bit SAD precision, any macroblock candidate with total distortion `>= 255` saturates to `0xFF`, destroying the comparator's ability to find the true minimum-distortion motion vector `(motionX, motionY)`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 98 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 98's combined one-liner, why do we execute `which fc_shell icv pt_shell` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Executes Synopsys Fusion Compiler (`fc_shell`) for 520 MHz 14nm FinFET synthesis, floorplanning, CTS (`M7`), and detail routing. Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 98's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `which fc_shell icv pt_shell` performs: Executes Synopsys Fusion Compiler (`fc_shell`) for 520 MHz 14nm FinFET synthesis, floorplanning, CTS (`M7`), and detail routing. And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 98's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (End-to-End V1→V9 Sign-Off Metrics Audit)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 98 · End-to-End V1->V9 Mastery Check] Which complete set of metrics summarizes our signed-off V9 16-Bit Motion Estimator ASIC?
options: A) 520 MHz (1.923 ns), 16-bit SAD (0000 / 0100 / FF00 all PASS), SAED14nm 125.07 x 62.80 um (7,854.4 um^2), 8,230 cells (449 FFs, 0 SRAMs), 0/242 ICV DRC, 0 LVS errors, 3-Corner PrimeTime Setup WNS +0.71/+0.54/+0.22 ns & Hold WNS 0.00 ns.
B) 100 MHz (10 ns), 8-bit SAD (saturates at 8'hFF), 2 SRAM macros, 14 DRC errors.
C) 400 MHz (2.5 ns), Setup slack -90 ps, Hold slack -820 ps.
D) 50 MHz (20 ns), 3 flip-flops, 1 ns hold violation.
quiz_questions.hint: Cross-check the target clock (`520 MHz`), the 3 directed testbench SAD hex values (`0000`, `0100`, `FF00`), the die size (`125.07 x 62.80 um`), and the 3-corner PrimeTime slacks (`+0.71 / +0.54 / +0.22 ns`).
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Option A lists the exact verified V9 sign-off metrics across RTL simulation, Fusion Compiler 14nm P&R, IC Validator DRC/LVS, and PrimeTime 3-corner STA.
Incorrect — Option B describes the unoptimized 8-bit baseline with DRC errors.
Incorrect — Option C lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 9 & 10 (`400 MHz`, `-90 ps` setup slack, `-820 ps` hold slack).
Incorrect — Option D lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 4 & 5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold slack).
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Option A is our exact V9 sign-off specification; Option C is Midterm Q9/Q10 (`-90 ps` setup, `-820 ps` hold at 400 MHz), and Option D is Midterm Q4/Q5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold violation).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (8-Bit vs. 16-Bit PPA Trade-Off Analysis)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 98 · Advanced PPA (Power, Performance, Area) Trade-Off] Upgrading the Motion Estimator from the 8-bit saturating baseline to the 16-bit full-precision architecture doubled the accumulator/comparator datapath width (`8 -> 16 bits`), increasing standard-cell area by ~2.5x and dynamic power to `0.890 mW` at `520 MHz`. Why is this area/power investment mandatory in a real H.264/HEVC video encoder ASIC?
options: A) Because an 8-bit SAD accumulator saturates at `255 (8'hFF)` whenever average pixel difference exceeds `1.0 LSB` (`256 * 1 = 256 > 255`), blinding the motion estimator on 99%+ of real natural video macroblocks and causing catastrophic motion-vector misprediction and video compression bloat!
B) Because 16-bit registers use zero power.
C) Because 8-bit wires cannot be routed in 14nm.
D) Because 16-bit logic runs at twice the clock period.
quiz_questions.hint: Consider what happens to video compression bit-rate if a motion estimator cannot tell the difference between a candidate with SAD = 256 (`1 LSB/pixel` error) and a candidate with SAD = 65,280 (`255 LSB/pixel` error)!
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In real video frames, almost every candidate block has an average pixel difference `> 1 LSB` (`SAD > 255`). An 8-bit accumulator clips all of them to `255 (0xFF)`, making true motion estimation impossible. Investing `3,416 um^2` (`< 0.004 mm^2`) in 14nm silicon restores 100% mathematical accuracy (`0..65,280`) while still closing `520 MHz` (`+0.22 ns` SS slack)!
Incorrect — Doubling register count increases switching capacitance `C_eff`, raising dynamic power `P = alpha * C * V^2 * f`.
Incorrect — Both 8-bit and 16-bit netlists route cleanly (`0/242 DRC`).
Incorrect — Both designs meet the exact same `520 MHz (1.923 ns)` clock period.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Without 16-bit SAD precision, any macroblock candidate with total distortion `>= 255` saturates to `0xFF`, destroying the comparator's ability to find the true minimum-distortion motion vector `(motionX, motionY)`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (8-Bit vs. 16-Bit PPA Trade-Off Analysis)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 99 · Advanced PPA (Power, Performance, Area) Trade-Off] Upgrading the Motion Estimator from the 8-bit saturating baseline to the 16-bit full-precision architecture doubled the accumulator/comparator datapath width (`8 -> 16 bits`), increasing standard-cell area by ~2.5x and dynamic power to `0.890 mW` at `520 MHz`. Why is this area/power investment mandatory in a real H.264/HEVC video encoder ASIC?
options: A) Because an 8-bit SAD accumulator saturates at `255 (8'hFF)` whenever average pixel difference exceeds `1.0 LSB` (`256 * 1 = 256 > 255`), blinding the motion estimator on 99%+ of real natural video macroblocks and causing catastrophic motion-vector misprediction and video compression bloat!
B) Because 16-bit registers use zero power.
C) Because 8-bit wires cannot be routed in 14nm.
D) Because 16-bit logic runs at twice the clock period.
quiz_questions.hint: Consider what happens to video compression bit-rate if a motion estimator cannot tell the difference between a candidate with SAD = 256 (`1 LSB/pixel` error) and a candidate with SAD = 65,280 (`255 LSB/pixel` error)!
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In real video frames, almost every candidate block has an average pixel difference `> 1 LSB` (`SAD > 255`). An 8-bit accumulator clips all of them to `255 (0xFF)`, making true motion estimation impossible. Investing `3,416 um^2` (`< 0.004 mm^2`) in 14nm silicon restores 100% mathematical accuracy (`0..65,280`) while still closing `520 MHz` (`+0.22 ns` SS slack)!
Incorrect — Doubling register count increases switching capacitance `C_eff`, raising dynamic power `P = alpha * C * V^2 * f`.
Incorrect — Both 8-bit and 16-bit netlists route cleanly (`0/242 DRC`).
Incorrect — Both designs meet the exact same `520 MHz (1.923 ns)` clock period.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Without 16-bit SAD precision, any macroblock candidate with total distortion `>= 255` saturates to `0xFF`, destroying the comparator's ability to find the true minimum-distortion motion vector `(motionX, motionY)`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 1 · Easy (Beginner Foundation & Terminal Orientation)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 100 · Beginner Orientation] Before pasting Page 100's one-liner (`Page 100: Final 100% Verification Certificate & `), which terminal environment should you paste into, and what happens immediately after you press `Return`?
options: A) Paste it into Microsoft Word or a browser URL bar.

B) Paste it into your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`); `snap_step` executes the command, verifies the output against Page 100's expected result, and either unlocks the green Post-Lab Learning view or provides a 1-click Auto-Debug Fix command if an error occurs.
C) Paste it into a disconnected terminal window showing `Broken pipe` without reconnecting.
D) Reboot the laptop after every single command.
quiz_questions.hint: Check the environment badge on Page 100: is this step running locally on your MacBook Air or on the remote SFSU Linux EDA server (`mahmoodi`), and how does `snap_step` talk back to the website?
choice_diagnostics: Incorrect — Shell commands must be pasted into an active UNIX terminal emulator (`Terminal.app` or `XQuartz xterm`), not a word processor or browser address bar.

Correct! Pasting into your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`) runs the command inside `snap_step`, which automatically checks the exit code and required markers and updates your live `:8788` web console!

Incorrect — A terminal showing `client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe` has lost its SSH connection; you must either use your clean local terminal window or run the Step 0 Auto-Connect command first.
Incorrect — You never need to reboot between pages; `snap_step` preserves your state continuously from Page 1 to Page 100.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: B) Page 100 runs in your clean local MacBook Air Terminal window (`huynguyen@MacBook-Air ~ %`, running `zsh`). Pressing `Return` triggers `snap_step`, which logs the output, captures the screenshot, and sends real-time verification telemetry to the website.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 2 · Easy-Medium (Hands-On Command Mechanics)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 100 · Hands-On Lab Mechanics] In Page 100's combined one-liner, why do we execute `echo '=== PAGE 100 FINAL V1->V9 WORKBOOK SCORECARD ==='` and chain subsequent sub-commands using the logical AND operator (`&&`) inside `snap_step`?
options: A) Executes sequential step operation: `echo '=== PAGE 100 FINAL V1->V9 WORKBOOK SCORECARD ==='` Chaining with `&&` guarantees short-circuit safety (the next sub-command only runs if exit_code == 0), while `snap_step` captures the terminal log, renders a screenshot, and verifies Page 100's expected output markers.
B) The `&&` operator runs all commands in reverse order from right to left.
C) It deletes the main project repository on GitHub.
D) It bypasses all Synopsys license checks by disabling the system clock.
quiz_questions.hint: Recall how UNIX shells (`zsh` and `bash`) evaluate `cmd1 && cmd2`: does `cmd2` execute if `cmd1` returns a non-zero error code?
choice_diagnostics: Correct! `echo '=== PAGE 100 FINAL V1->V9 WORKBOOK SCORECARD ==='` performs: Executes sequential step operation: `echo '=== PAGE 100 FINAL V1->V9 WORKBOOK SCORECARD ==='` And `&&` stops immediately if any sub-command fails so the `:8788` Auto-Debugger can pinpoint and repair the exact failing step.
Incorrect — `&&` evaluates strictly left-to-right, executing the right-hand command only if the left-hand command returned exit code `0`.
Incorrect — `snap_step` strictly isolates all work inside your manual practice workspace (`~/Developer/motion-estimator-14nm-asic-manual` and `manual-practice-macbook-air`), never touching `main`.
Incorrect — Shell operators control process execution flow in the operating system and have no effect on EDA license daemons.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) In UNIX shells (`zsh`/`bash`), `cmd1 && cmd2` short-circuits immediately on any non-zero exit code (`$? != 0`). Wrapping the chain inside `snap_step` logs stdout/stderr, renders the PNG proof, and checks Page 100's `required_markers`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 3 · Medium (Reproducible ASIC Sign-Off & Git Branch Hygiene)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 100 · Reproducible ASIC Sign-Off & Git Hygiene] Why does our workflow commit your MacBook Air step-by-step logs and screenshots to the `manual-practice-macbook-air` sub-branch instead of overwriting `main`?
options: A) So the completed, verified `main` branch portfolio remains 100% intact as a golden reference for recruiters while `manual-practice-macbook-air` records your real-time, chronological Page 1 -> Page 100 manual build evidence.
B) Because Git does not allow more than 10 commits on `main`.
C) Because `main` cannot store PNG files.
D) Because Python only runs on sub-branches.
quiz_questions.hint: Think about how semiconductor engineering teams protect the golden tapeout release branch (`main`) while engineers run hands-on bring-up and replication on feature/practice branches.
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Keeping `main` as the immutable golden release and pushing live manual practice logs to `manual-practice-macbook-air` showcases both the finished 14nm ASIC and your verified step-by-step replication trail!
Incorrect — Git branches support unlimited commits.
Incorrect — Both `main` and sub-branches track PNG evidence seamlessly.
Incorrect — Python runs identically regardless of the checked-out Git branch.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Using `manual-practice-macbook-air` isolates your live step-by-step practice progression while preserving the golden reference on `main`.

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 4 · Hard (End-to-End V1→V9 Sign-Off Metrics Audit)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 100 · End-to-End V1->V9 Mastery Check] Which complete set of metrics summarizes our signed-off V9 16-Bit Motion Estimator ASIC?
options: A) 520 MHz (1.923 ns), 16-bit SAD (0000 / 0100 / FF00 all PASS), SAED14nm 125.07 x 62.80 um (7,854.4 um^2), 8,230 cells (449 FFs, 0 SRAMs), 0/242 ICV DRC, 0 LVS errors, 3-Corner PrimeTime Setup WNS +0.71/+0.54/+0.22 ns & Hold WNS 0.00 ns.
B) 100 MHz (10 ns), 8-bit SAD (saturates at 8'hFF), 2 SRAM macros, 14 DRC errors.
C) 400 MHz (2.5 ns), Setup slack -90 ps, Hold slack -820 ps.
D) 50 MHz (20 ns), 3 flip-flops, 1 ns hold violation.
quiz_questions.hint: Cross-check the target clock (`520 MHz`), the 3 directed testbench SAD hex values (`0000`, `0100`, `FF00`), the die size (`125.07 x 62.80 um`), and the 3-corner PrimeTime slacks (`+0.71 / +0.54 / +0.22 ns`).
choice_diagnostics: Correct! Option A lists the exact verified V9 sign-off metrics across RTL simulation, Fusion Compiler 14nm P&R, IC Validator DRC/LVS, and PrimeTime 3-corner STA.
Incorrect — Option B describes the unoptimized 8-bit baseline with DRC errors.
Incorrect — Option C lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 9 & 10 (`400 MHz`, `-90 ps` setup slack, `-820 ps` hold slack).
Incorrect — Option D lists the numbers from Midterm Questions 4 & 5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold slack).
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Option A is our exact V9 sign-off specification; Option C is Midterm Q9/Q10 (`-90 ps` setup, `-820 ps` hold at 400 MHz), and Option D is Midterm Q4/Q5 (`20 ns` period, `-1 ns` hold violation).

quiz_questions.difficulty_label: Level 5 · Advanced Challenge (8-Bit vs. 16-Bit PPA Trade-Off Analysis)
quiz_questions.q: [Page 100 · Advanced PPA (Power, Performance, Area) Trade-Off] Upgrading the Motion Estimator from the 8-bit saturating baseline to the 16-bit full-precision architecture doubled the accumulator/comparator datapath width (`8 -> 16 bits`), increasing standard-cell area by ~2.5x and dynamic power to `0.890 mW` at `520 MHz`. Why is this area/power investment mandatory in a real H.264/HEVC video encoder ASIC?
options: A) Because an 8-bit SAD accumulator saturates at `255 (8'hFF)` whenever average pixel difference exceeds `1.0 LSB` (`256 * 1 = 256 > 255`), blinding the motion estimator on 99%+ of real natural video macroblocks and causing catastrophic motion-vector misprediction and video compression bloat!
B) Because 16-bit registers use zero power.
C) Because 8-bit wires cannot be routed in 14nm.
D) Because 16-bit logic runs at twice the clock period.
quiz_questions.hint: Consider what happens to video compression bit-rate if a motion estimator cannot tell the difference between a candidate with SAD = 256 (`1 LSB/pixel` error) and a candidate with SAD = 65,280 (`255 LSB/pixel` error)!
choice_diagnostics: Correct! In real video frames, almost every candidate block has an average pixel difference `> 1 LSB` (`SAD > 255`). An 8-bit accumulator clips all of them to `255 (0xFF)`, making true motion estimation impossible. Investing `3,416 um^2` (`< 0.004 mm^2`) in 14nm silicon restores 100% mathematical accuracy (`0..65,280`) while still closing `520 MHz` (`+0.22 ns` SS slack)!
Incorrect — Doubling register count increases switching capacitance `C_eff`, raising dynamic power `P = alpha * C * V^2 * f`.
Incorrect — Both 8-bit and 16-bit netlists route cleanly (`0/242 DRC`).
Incorrect — Both designs meet the exact same `520 MHz (1.923 ns)` clock period.
quiz_questions.explain: Answer Key: A) Without 16-bit SAD precision, any macroblock candidate with total distortion `>= 255` saturates to `0xFF`, destroying the comparator's ability to find the true minimum-distortion motion vector `(motionX, motionY)`.
